dhyana.1: Om. Her whose radiance is like the bandhūka (noon-flower), who dwells on the seat of five skulls, whose jewelled crown bears the shining digit of the moon, who wears a garland of heads,
dhyana.2: who has three eyes, who is clad in red, whose breasts are full, high and shaped like pots, and who holds, in order, a book, a rosary, the gesture of granting boons and the gesture of fearlessness —
dhyana.3: on her, holding these and honoured in the northern tradition (Uttarāmnāya), one should always meditate.
dhyana.4: She who is Caṇḍī, crusher of Madhu, Kaiṭabha and the other demons; she who uprooted Mahiṣāsura; she who crushed Dhūmrekṣaṇa, Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa; she who devoured Raktabīja; the Power who crushed the demons Śumbha and Niśumbha; she who is the supreme giver of accomplishment (siddhi): may that Devī, ruler of the universe, together with her nine crore forms, protect me.
argala.viniyoga: Om. Of this mantra, the Śrī Argalā Stotra, the seer is Viṣṇu, the metre is anuṣṭubh, the deity is Śrī Mahālakṣmī; for the pleasure of Śrī Jagadambā, the Mother of the World, it is applied in recitation as a part of reading the Saptaśatī.
argala.1: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Om. Victory to you, O Devī Cāmuṇḍā; victory to you, O remover of the sufferings of beings; victory to you, O Devī who pervade all; O Kālarātri, salutation to you. ॥1॥
argala.2: You are Jayantī, Maṅgalā, Kālī, Bhadrakālī and Kapālinī; you are Durgā, Śivā, Kṣamā, Dhātrī, Svāhā and Svadhā: salutation to you. ॥2॥
argala.3: O destroyer of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, O giver of boons to Brahmā the Creator, salutation to you. Give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥3॥
argala.4: O destroyer of Mahiṣāsura, O giver of happiness to your devotees, salutation to you. Give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥4॥
argala.5: O Devī, slayer of Dhūmranetra, O giver of dharma (right conduct), pleasure and wealth, give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥5॥
argala.6: O Devī, slayer of Raktabīja, O destroyer of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥6॥
argala.7: O destroyer of Niśumbha and Śumbha, O giver of good to the three worlds, salutation to you. Give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥7॥
argala.8: O Devī, whose two feet are worshipped, O giver of all good fortune, give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥8॥
argala.9: O you whose form and deeds are beyond thought, O destroyer of all enemies, give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥9॥
argala.10: And to those who always bow to you with devotion, O Aparṇā, remover of sins, give them beauty, give them victory, give them fame, and slay their enemies. ॥10॥
argala.11: To those who praise you with devotion, O Caṇḍikā, destroyer of disease, give them beauty, give them victory, give them fame, and slay their enemies. ॥11॥
argala.12: O Caṇḍikā, ever victorious in battle, O destroyer of sin, give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥12॥
argala.13: Give me good fortune and health; O Devī, give me supreme happiness. Give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥13॥
argala.14: O Devī, bring about my welfare; bestow abundant prosperity on me. Give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥14॥
argala.15: Bring about the destruction of those who hate me; bestow on me strength in high measure. Give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥15॥
argala.16: O Ambikā, whose feet are rubbed by the crest-jewels of gods and asuras as they bow down, give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥16॥
argala.17: Make me learned, renowned and prosperous. Give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥17॥
argala.18: O Devī, destroyer of the pride of demons with mighty, staff-like arms, give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥18॥
argala.19: O Caṇḍikā, destroyer of the pride of fierce demons, to me who bow to you give beauty, give victory, give fame, and slay my enemies. ॥19॥
argala.20: O four-armed one, praised by four-faced Brahmā, O Supreme Sovereign, give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥20॥
argala.21: O Devī, ever praised by Kṛṣṇa with unceasing devotion, O Ambikā, give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥21॥
argala.22: O Supreme Sovereign, praised by Śiva, lord of the daughter of the Himālaya, give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥22॥
argala.23: O Supreme Sovereign, worshipped in sincere devotion by Indra, husband of Indrāṇī, give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥23॥
argala.24: O Devī, O Ambikā, who give your devotees a boundless rising of bliss, give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥24॥
argala.25: Give me a charming wife who follows the inclinations of my mind. Give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥25॥
argala.26: O you who carry beings across the ocean of worldly existence so hard to cross, O daughter of the mountain, give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥26॥
argala.27: Having recited this hymn, a person should then recite the great hymn; by fully worshipping the Saptaśatī he obtains a boon that is hard to win. ॥27॥
argala.iti: Thus ends the Argalā Stotra in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa.
kilaka.viniyoga: Om. Of this mantra, the Śrī Kīlaka (the pin, or bolt, of a mantra), the seer is Śiva, the metre is anuṣṭubh, the deity is Śrī Mahāsarasvatī; for the pleasure of Śrī Jagadambā it is applied in recitation as a part of reading the Saptaśatī.
kilaka.1: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Om. To him whose body is pure knowledge, whose divine eyes are the three Vedas, who is the cause of attaining the highest good, to Śiva who bears the half-moon: salutation. ॥1॥
kilaka.2: One should know well all this, the kīlaka even of the mantras; he too attains well-being who is constantly intent on recitation. ॥2॥
kilaka.3: All the rites, uccāṭana (making a person quit his place) and the rest, succeed for those who praise the Devī with devotion through this collection of hymns. ॥3॥
kilaka.4: For him no mantra, no herb, nothing at all is needed; even without recitation, all uccāṭana and the like will succeed. ॥4॥
kilaka.5: Taking to heart the people's fear that all the rites would succeed, Hara bound this whole auspicious hymn in this way. ॥5॥
The dictionaries give nimantrayāmāsa as summoned; some read: Hara summoned the people and declared that all this is auspicious.
kilaka.6: And that hymn of Caṇḍikā he made secret. Through merit one duly attains that binding. ॥6॥
kilaka.7: He too attains well-being in full; there is no doubt of it — he who, with a collected mind, on the fourteenth or the eighth day of the dark fortnight, ॥7॥
kilaka.8: makes an offering to the Devī and receives it back from her; in no other way is she pleased. With a bolt of such a form it has been bolted by Mahādeva. ॥8॥
kilaka.9: He who makes this Caṇḍī free of the bolt and recites it daily is a siddha, a perfected one; he is a gaṇa, one of Śiva's attendants; and he surely becomes a gandharva. ॥9॥
kilaka.10: No sickness comes to him, and fear arises for him nowhere; he does not fall into the power of untimely death, and at death he gains liberation. ॥10॥
kilaka.11: Knowing this, one should begin and then recite it; for one who does not do so perishes. Therefore the wise begin this whole hymn only after knowing it. ॥11॥
kilaka.12: Whatever good fortune and the like is seen among women, all that is by her grace; therefore this auspicious hymn should be recited. ॥12॥
kilaka.13: When this hymn is recited softly, prosperity comes in great measure, and indeed in full; therefore it should certainly be undertaken. ॥13॥
Some read: recited softly it brings some prosperity, recited aloud prosperity in full; therefore it should be begun aloud.
kilaka.14: By her grace come sovereignty, good fortune and health, the destruction of enemies and the supreme liberation; why then should people not praise her? ॥14॥
kilaka.15: The man who constantly remembers Caṇḍikā, even in his heart alone, gains the desire dear to his heart, and the Devī dwells ever in his heart. ॥15॥
kilaka.16: First performing this removal of the bolt, made by Mahādeva, and so making it free of the bolt, those of collected mind should recite it. ॥16॥
kilaka.iti: Thus ends the Kīlaka Stotra of Śrī Bhagavatī.
kavacha.viniyoga: Of this Śrī Caṇḍī Kavaca, the armour-hymn, the seer is Brahmā, the metre is anuṣṭubh, the deity is Cāmuṇḍā, the seed is the Mothers named in the aṅganyāsa, the placing on the limbs, the tattva, the essence, is the deities who bind the directions; it is applied in recitation for the pleasure of Śrī Jagadambā.
kavacha.1: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Om. That which is supremely secret in the world and gives men protection in every way, and which has not been told to anyone, tell that to me, O Grandsire. ॥1॥
kavacha.2: Brahmā said: There is, O Brāhmaṇa, something most secret, which benefits all beings: the holy kavaca, the armour, of the Devī; listen to it, O great sage. ॥2॥
kavacha.3: The first is named Śailaputrī, the second Brahmacāriṇī, the third is named Candraghaṇṭā, and the fourth Kūṣmāṇḍā. ॥3॥
kavacha.4: The fifth is named Skandamātā, the sixth likewise Kātyāyanī, the seventh Kālarātri, and the eighth is named Mahāgaurī. ॥4॥
kavacha.5: And the ninth is Siddhidātrī; these are proclaimed the nine Durgās. These names were declared by the great Veda itself. ॥5॥
Some take brahmaṇā as Brahmā, though he is himself the speaker here: these names were spoken by the great-souled Brahmā himself.
kavacha.6: Those who are being burnt by fire, who are caught among enemies in battle, who are in rough and impassable places, and who, stricken with fear, have gone to the Devī for refuge — ॥6॥
kavacha.7: no misfortune whatever befalls them in the peril of battle, and they do not see calamity that brings grief, sorrow and fear. ॥7॥
kavacha.8: For those who remember the Devī daily with devotion, prosperity grows. O Queen of the gods, those who remember you, you protect; there is no doubt of it. ॥8॥
kavacha.9: Cāmuṇḍā is seated on a corpse, Vārāhī rides a buffalo, Aindrī is mounted on an elephant, Vaiṣṇavī is seated on Garuḍa. ॥9॥
kavacha.10: Nārasiṃhī is of great valour, Śivadūtī of great strength, Māheśvarī rides a bull, Kaumārī has the peacock for her mount. ॥10॥
kavacha.11: The goddess Lakṣmī is seated on a lotus, holds a lotus in her hand and is the beloved of Hari; the goddess Īśvarī, who bears a white form, has a bull for her mount. ॥11॥
kavacha.12: Brāhmī rides a swan and is adorned with every ornament. Thus all these Mothers are endowed with every power of yoga. ॥12॥
kavacha.13: All of them are rich in the beauty of many ornaments and shine with many kinds of gems, all with fine pearls hanging in divine necklaces, ॥13॥
kavacha.14: with indranīla and mahānīla sapphires and splendid rubies; these goddesses are seen mounted on chariots, filled with wrath. ॥14॥
kavacha.15: Conch, discus, mace, spear, plough and the weapon called the pestle, shield, javelin, axe and noose, ॥15॥
kavacha.16: the weapon called the lance, the trident, and the excellent weapon, the Śārṅga bow — for destroying the bodies of the demons and for making the devotees fearless, ॥16॥
kavacha.17: these weapons they bear in this way, and indeed for the good of the gods too. Salutation to you, O greatly fierce one, whose valour is greatly terrible. ॥17॥
kavacha.18: O you of great strength, of great energy, destroyer of great fear, protect me, O Devī, hard to look upon, who increase the fear of enemies. ॥18॥
kavacha.19: May Aindrī protect me in the east, the Fire-deity in the south-east; may Vārāhī guard me in the south, the bearer of the sword in the south-west. ॥19॥
kavacha.20: May Vāruṇī protect me in the west, she who rides the deer in the north-west; may Kauberī guard me in the north, the bearer of the trident in the north-east. ॥20॥
kavacha.21: May Brahmāṇī protect me above, and Vaiṣṇavī likewise below; thus may Cāmuṇḍā, whose mount is a corpse, protect me in the ten directions. ॥21॥
kavacha.22: May Jayā guard me in front, may Vijayā guard me behind, Ajitā on the left side, and Aparājitā on the right. ॥22॥
kavacha.23: May Dyotinī protect my topknot, and Umā, stationed on the crown of my head, Mālādharī on the forehead, and may Yaśasvinī protect my eyebrows. ॥23॥
kavacha.24: May Citranetrā guard my eyes, and Yamaghaṇṭā my side; Trinetrā with her trident, and Caṇḍikā the place between my eyebrows. ॥24॥
kavacha.25: Śaṅkhinī between my eyes, Dvāravāsinī in my ears; may Kālikā protect my cheeks, and Śaṅkarī the roots of my ears. ॥25॥
kavacha.26: May Sugandhā protect the nose, and Carcikā the upper lip; may Amṛtābālā protect the lower lip, and Sarasvatī the tongue. ॥26॥
kavacha.27: May Kaumārī protect the teeth, and Caṇḍikā the region of the throat; may Citraghaṇṭā protect the uvula, and Mahāmāyā the palate. ॥27॥
kavacha.28: May Kāmākṣī protect the chin, and Sarvamaṅgalā my speech; may Bhadrakālī protect the neck, and Dhanurdharī the spine. ॥28॥
kavacha.29: May Nīlagrīvā protect the outer throat, and Nalakūbarī the windpipe; may Khaḍginī protect the two shoulders, and Vajradhāriṇī my two arms. ॥29॥
kavacha.30: May Daṇḍinī protect the two hands, and Ambikā the fingers; may Śūleśvarī protect the nails, and Nareśvarī the belly. ॥30॥
kavacha.31: May Mahādevī protect the breasts, and Śokavināśinī the mind; may the Devī Lalitā protect the heart, and Śūladhāriṇī the abdomen. ॥31॥
kavacha.32: May Kāminī protect the navel, and likewise Guhyeśvarī the private parts; may Durgandhā protect the generative organ, and Guhyavāhinī my anus. ॥32॥
kavacha.33: May Bhagavatī protect the waist, and Meghavāhanā my thighs; may Mahābalā protect the shanks, and Mādhavanāyikā the knees. ॥33॥
kavacha.34: May Nārasiṃhī protect the ankles, and Kauśikī the tops of the feet; may Śrīdharī protect the toes, and Pātālavāsinī the sole. ॥34॥
kavacha.35: May Daṃṣṭrakarālī protect the nails, and Ūrdhvakeśinī the hair; may Kaumārī protect the pores of the skin, and likewise Yogīśvarī the skin. ॥35॥
kavacha.36: May Pārvatī protect the blood, marrow, fat, flesh, bones and fatty tissue; may Kālarātri protect the intestines, and Mukuṭeśvarī the bile. ॥36॥
kavacha.37: May Padmāvatī protect the lotus-calyx (the heart-lotus), and likewise Cūḍāmaṇi the phlegm; may Jvālāmukhī protect the lustre of the nails, and Abhedyā all the joints. ॥37॥
kavacha.38: May Brahmāṇī protect my semen, and likewise Chatreśvarī my shadow; may Dharmadhāriṇī protect my ego, mind and intellect. ॥38॥
kavacha.39: My vital airs prāṇa and apāna, and likewise vyāna, udāna and samāna, may Vajrahastā protect; and may Kalyāṇaśobhanā protect my life-breaths. ॥39॥
kavacha.40: May Yoginī protect me in taste, form, smell, sound and touch; may Nārāyaṇī always protect sattva, rajas and tamas, the three guṇas, the qualities of nature. ॥40॥
kavacha.41: May Vārāhī protect my span of life, and Pārvatī my dharma, my right conduct; may Vaiṣṇavī always protect my renown, my fame and my prosperity. ॥41॥
kavacha.42: May Indrāṇī protect my lineage, and Caṇḍikā my cattle; may Mahālakṣmī protect my sons, and Bhairavī my wife. ॥42॥
kavacha.43: May Dhaneśvarī protect my wealth, and likewise Kaumārī my daughter; may Supathā protect the path, and likewise Kṣemaṅkarī the road. ॥43॥
kavacha.44: At the king's gate may Mahālakṣmī protect me, and Vijayā, who is ever present. And whatever place is left without protection, not covered by the kavaca, this armour of prayer — ॥44॥
kavacha.45: — protect all that for me, O Devī Jayantī, destroyer of sin. One should always recite this holy kavaca, which gives protection of every kind. ॥45॥
kavacha.46: O brahmin sage, because of your devotion I have told you this secret. One should not take a single step without the kavaca if one wishes for one's own good. ॥46॥
kavacha.47: Wherever a man goes who is always covered by the kavaca, there he gains wealth, and victory at all times. ॥47॥
kavacha.48: Whatever desire he thinks of, that he surely obtains; such a man will attain supreme, unequalled sovereignty on earth. ॥48॥
kavacha.49: That mortal becomes fearless and unconquered in battles; the man covered by the kavaca becomes worthy of worship in the three worlds. ॥49॥
kavacha.50: This kavaca of the Devī is hard to obtain even for the gods. Whoever recites it every day at the three junctions of the day, self-controlled and pure, and full of faith — ॥50॥
kavacha.51: — a divine portion comes to him, and he is unconquered in the three worlds; he lives a hundred years and more, free from untimely death. ॥51॥
kavacha.52: All diseases perish, skin sores from spider poison, boils and the like; and whatever poison there is, from things that do not move, from moving creatures, or made by art, perishes too. ॥52॥
kavacha.53: All malevolent rites, the mantras and yantras on earth; those that move on the earth and those that move in the sky, those born in the family and those got by instruction — ॥53॥
kavacha.54: afflictions inborn and hereditary, mālā, ḍākinī and śākinī as well, and the terrible ḍākinīs who move in the mid-air with a mighty roar — ॥54॥
kavacha.55: grahas, the seizing spirits, bhūtas and piśācas, yakṣas, gandharvas and rākṣasas, brahmarākṣasas and vetālas, kūṣmāṇḍas, bhairavas and the like — ॥55॥
kavacha.56: — all these perish at the very sight of one who is covered by the kavaca. His honour rises with the king, and his splendour grows to the highest. ॥56॥
kavacha.57: Such men grow in renown, and their fame increases. Therefore, O sage, a devotee should always recite the kavaca, which grants desires. ॥57॥
kavacha.58: Having first recited the kavaca, one should recite the Caṇḍī Saptaśatī; the accomplishment born of reciting the Caṇḍī comes without obstacle. ॥58॥
kavacha.59: As long as the sphere of the earth endures, with its mountains, woods and forests, so long does his line of sons and grandsons remain on the earth. ॥59॥
kavacha.60: At the end of the body, the supreme abode, very hard to reach even for the gods, that eternal abode the man attains by the grace of Mahāmāyā. ॥60॥
kavacha.61: He goes there, and having gone, he does not come back again. He gains the supreme abode and attains equality with Śiva. ॥61॥
kavacha.iti: Thus ends the Devī Kavaca in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, composed by Hari, Hara and Brahmā.
1.viniyoga: Of this sacred First Episode (Prathama Caritra), the seer is Brahmā; the deity is Mahākālī; the metre is gāyatrī; the power (śakti) is Nandā; the seed (bīja) is Raktadantikā; the element (tattva) is fire; and its essential form is the Ṛgveda. For the pleasure of Śrī Mahākālī, its application is in the recitation of the First Episode.
1.dhyana: Om. Holding in her hands a sword, a discus, a mace, arrows, a bow, an iron club, a trident, a bhuśuṇḍī (a kind of weapon), a severed head and a conch, three-eyed, adorned with ornaments on every limb, with the lustre of a sapphire, with ten faces and ten feet: I worship Mahākālikā, whom the lotus-born Brahmā praised, when Hari had fallen asleep, so that Madhu and Kaiṭabha might be slain.
1.2: Sāvarṇi, son of the Sun, who is called the eighth Manu: hear of his birth from me as I tell it in full, ॥2॥
1.3: and how, by the power of Mahāmāyā, he became the lord of a manvantara, the age of a Manu, that illustrious Sāvarṇi, son of the Sun. ॥3॥
1.4: Long ago, in the Svārociṣa manvantara, a king born of the line of Caitra, named Suratha, ruled over the whole circle of the earth. ॥4॥
1.5: While he was rightly protecting his subjects as if they were his own sons, the Kolāvidhvaṃsin kings then became his enemies. ॥5॥
1.6: A war broke out between them and him, the bearer of a very mighty sceptre; and in that war he was defeated by those Kolāvidhvaṃsins, though they were weaker. ॥6॥
1.7: Then he came back to his own city and became ruler of his own country alone. Then that illustrious one was attacked by those powerful enemies. ॥7॥
1.8: From him, now weakened, his powerful, wicked and evil-minded ministers seized his treasury and his army, then, there in his own city too. ॥8॥
1.9: Then, under the pretext of hunting, that king, robbed of his sovereignty, mounted a horse alone and went into a dense forest. ॥9॥
1.10: There he saw the hermitage of Medhas, best of the twice-born, full of wild beasts grown peaceful and adorned by the sage's disciples. ॥10॥
1.11: Honoured by that sage, he stayed there for some time, wandering here and there in that hermitage of the excellent sage. ॥11॥
1.12: Then, there, his mind drawn by the sense of possession, he thought: That city which my forefathers protected of old is now bereft of me. ॥12॥
1.13: Whether those servants of mine, men of evil conduct, protect it righteously or not, I do not know. That chief elephant of mine, valiant and always in rut, ॥13॥
1.14: having passed into the power of my enemies, what comforts will he get? Those who always followed me for my favour, wealth and food ॥14॥
1.15: surely now attend on other kings. By those men given to spending wrongly, who keep on spending without end, ॥15॥
1.16: that treasury, gathered with great hardship, will be wasted away. These and other things the king kept thinking over constantly. ॥16॥
1.17: There, near the brahmin's hermitage, he saw a merchant. The king asked him: Friend, who are you? And what is the reason for your coming here? ॥17॥
1.18: Why do you appear as if grief-stricken, as if downcast? Having heard these words of the king, spoken with affection, ॥18॥
1.19: the merchant, bowed down with humility, answered the king. ॥19॥
1.21: I am a merchant named Samādhi, born in a family of the wealthy. ॥21॥
1.22: Out of greed for wealth, my wicked sons and wife have driven me out; they have taken my wealth, and I am left without wealth, wife and sons. ॥22॥
1.23: Grieving, and cast out by my trusted kinsmen, I have come to the forest. Such as I am, I do not know whether the news of my sons is good or ill, ॥23॥
1.24: nor, staying here, the news of my kinsmen and my wife. Is it well with them at home now, or is it ill? ॥24॥
1.25: How are they? Are my sons of good conduct, or are they of bad conduct? ॥25॥
1.27: Those greedy ones, sons, wife and the rest, who drove you out for the sake of wealth: ॥27॥
1.28: why does your mind bind itself to them in affection? ॥28॥
1.30: It is just as you have said, these words about me. ॥30॥
1.31: What am I to do? My mind will not turn hard towards those who, greedy for wealth, gave up love for their father and cast me out, ॥31॥
1.32: and gave up love for husband and kinsmen; towards them alone my mind is loving. Though I know, I cannot grasp what this is, O wise one: ॥32॥
1.33: that my mind leans in love even towards kinsmen without merit. For their sake sighs and dejection arise in me. ॥33॥
1.34: What am I to do, since my mind does not grow hard towards those who have no love? ॥34॥
1.36: Then, O brahmin, the two together went up to that sage. ॥36॥
1.37: That merchant named Samādhi and that best of kings, having exchanged courtesies with him as custom required and as he deserved, ॥37॥
1.38: sat down, and the merchant and the king talked of certain things. ॥38॥
1.40: O revered one, I wish to ask you one thing; tell me that. ॥40॥
1.41: That which, though my own mind has no control over it, brings distress to my mind: the attachment that I, who have lost my kingdom, have even to all the parts of the kingdom, ॥41॥
1.42: this I have though I know, just as an ignorant man would. What is this, O best of sages? And this merchant has been humiliated by his sons, his wife and his servants, and cast off as well, ॥42॥
1.43: and forsaken by his own people; yet he feels deep affection for them. Thus he, and I as well, are both deeply distressed. ॥43॥
1.44: Our minds are drawn by attachment even to objects whose faults we have seen. So what is this, O fortunate one, that delusion takes hold even of the two of us, who have knowledge? ॥44॥
1.45: And this bewilderment arises in me and in him, each blind in discernment. ॥45॥
1.47: Every creature has knowledge within the range of the objects of the senses. ॥47॥
1.48: And the objects, O fortunate one, come in this way to each separately: some creatures are blind by day, and others likewise blind at night. ॥48॥
1.49: Some creatures see equally by day and by night. Humans have knowledge, it is true; but they are certainly not the only ones, ॥49॥
1.50: for cattle, birds, wild beasts and the like all have knowledge; and the knowledge of humans is that which those beasts and birds have. ॥50॥
1.51: And what belongs to humans belongs to them as well, and the rest too is alike in both. Though they have knowledge, look at these birds: into the beaks of their young ॥51॥
1.52: out of delusion they are intent on dropping grain, though they themselves are tormented by hunger. Humans, O tiger among men, look with longing to their sons ॥52॥
1.53: out of greed, for a return of the favour; do you not see them? Even so, they are cast down into the pit of delusion, with its whirlpool of attachment, ॥53॥
1.54: by the power of Mahāmāyā, the great illusion, a power that keeps worldly existence in being. So no wonder should be felt at this: she is the Yoganidrā, the yogic sleep, of the Lord of the world, ॥54॥
1.55: and she is the Mahāmāyā of Hari; by her the world is deluded. For that Devī, the Bhagavatī, the minds even of the wise ॥55॥
1.56: she, Mahāmāyā, draws away by force and hands over to delusion. By her this entire world, moving and unmoving, is brought forth. ॥56॥
1.57: When she is gracious, it is she who becomes the giver of boons to men for their liberation. She is the supreme knowledge, the cause of liberation, eternal; ॥57॥
1.58: and she herself is the cause of bondage to worldly existence; she is the sovereign over all lords. ॥58॥
1.60: O revered one, who is that Devī whom you call Mahāmāyā? ॥60॥
1.61: How did she come into being, and what is her work, O twice-born? And whatever power that Devī has, whatever her nature and whatever her origin, ॥61॥
1.62: all that I wish to hear from you, O best of the knowers of brahman, the supreme reality. ॥62॥
1.64: She is eternal indeed; the world is her form; by her all this is pervaded. ॥64॥
1.65: Even so, hear from me how she comes forth in many ways. When she appears to accomplish the work of the gods, ॥65॥
1.66: then, though eternal, she is said in the world to have been born. When the world had become one single ocean, and Viṣṇu, the blessed Lord and master, ॥66॥
1.67: spread out Śeṣa as his bed and took to yogic sleep at the end of the kalpa, the cosmic age, then two terrible asuras, the renowned Madhu and Kaiṭabha, ॥67॥
1.68: sprung from the wax of Viṣṇu's ears, rose up to kill Brahmā. Brahmā, the lord of creatures, seated on the lotus of Viṣṇu's navel, ॥68॥
1.69: seeing those two fierce asuras and Janārdana fast asleep, and steady with a single-pointed heart, praised that Yoganidrā ॥69॥
1.70: to awaken Hari — her who had made her abode in Hari's eyes, the sovereign of the universe, the sustainer of the world, who brings about its preservation and dissolution, ॥70॥
1.71: the Bhagavatī Nidrā, the incomparable Sleep of Viṣṇu: Brahmā, the lord of radiance, praised her. ॥71॥
1.73: You are Svāhā, you are Svadhā, you indeed are the call vaṣaṭ; svara, the sacred tone of recitation, is your very self. ॥73॥
1.74: You are sudhā, the nectar of immortality; in the eternal syllable Om you abide threefold, as its measures; and you abide as the eternal half-measure, which cannot be uttered distinctly. ॥74॥
1.75: You alone are Sandhyā and Sāvitrī; you, O Devī, are the supreme mother. By you this universe is upheld; by you this world is created. ॥75॥
1.76: By you, O Devī, it is protected, and you always devour it at the end. At its creation you are the form of creation, and in its protection the form of preservation; ॥76॥
1.77: and likewise, at the end of this world, the form of its dissolution, O you whose being is the world. You are the great knowledge, the great illusion, the great intellect, the great memory, ॥77॥
1.78: and you are the great delusion, the great Devī, the great sovereign. And you are prakṛti, the primal nature of all, who brings forth the three guṇas, the strands of nature. ॥78॥
1.79: You are Kālarātri, the night of dissolution; Mahārātri, the great night; and the dreadful Moharātri, the night of delusion. You are Śrī, you are the sovereign, you are Hrī, modesty; you are understanding, whose mark is awareness. ॥79॥
1.80: You are bashfulness, nourishment and likewise contentment; you are peace, and forbearance too. You bear the sword and the trident, you are terrible, you bear the mace and likewise the discus, ॥80॥
1.81: the conch and the bow; arrows, the bhuśuṇḍī and the iron club are your weapons. You are gentle, gentler still, and far more beautiful than everything that is gentle. ॥81॥
1.82: Of all things higher and lower, you alone are the highest; you are the supreme sovereign. And whatever thing there is anywhere, whether real or unreal, O you who are the self of all, ॥82॥
1.83: the power of all of it is you: what praise of you can I offer? You, by whom even he who creates the world, protects the world and devours the world ॥83॥
1.84: has been brought under the sway of sleep: who here is able to praise you? Since Viṣṇu, I and Īśāna (Śiva) as well ॥84॥
1.85: have been made by you to take on bodies, who then could have the power to praise you? You, O Devī, thus praised for your own exalted powers, ॥85॥
1.86: delude these two unassailable asuras, Madhu and Kaiṭabha, and let Acyuta, the lord of the world, be quickly brought to wakefulness, ॥86॥
1.87: and let awareness be roused in him to slay these two great asuras. ॥87॥
1.89: Thus praised there and then by Brahmā the Creator, the Devī Tāmasī, ॥89॥
1.90: to awaken Viṣṇu so that he might slay Madhu and Kaiṭabha, from his eyes, mouth, nose, arms and heart, and likewise from his chest, ॥90॥
1.91: came forth and stood before the eyes of Brahmā, whose birth is unmanifest. And released by her, Janārdana, the lord of the world, rose up ॥91॥
1.92: from his serpent-bed on the one ocean; and then he saw those two, Madhu and Kaiṭabha, evil-minded, of surpassing strength and valour, ॥92॥
1.93: their eyes red with anger, set on devouring Brahmā. Then, rising up, the Lord Hari fought with the two ॥93॥
1.94: for five thousand years, the all-pervading Lord with his arms as his weapons. And the two, maddened by their surpassing strength and deluded by Mahāmāyā, ॥94॥
1.95: said to Keśava: Choose a boon from us. ॥95॥
1.97: If you two are now pleased with me, then both of you must be slain by me. ॥97॥
1.98: What use is any other boon here? For this much alone is what I have chosen. ॥98॥
1.100: Thus deceived, the two then saw that the whole world was made of water; ॥100॥
1.101: seeing this, they said to the lotus-eyed Lord: Slay us where the earth is not flooded with water. ॥101॥
1.103: Saying, So be it, the Lord, the bearer of the conch, discus and mace, placed them on his thigh and with his discus cut off the heads of the two. ॥103॥
1.104: Thus, praised by Brahmā, she herself came forth. Now hear once more of the power of this Devī; I shall tell you. Aiṃ Om. ॥104॥
1.iti: Svasti, may it be well. Thus ends the first chapter, named the Slaying of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, of the Devī Māhātmya in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, the age of the Manu Sāvarṇi. ॥1॥
2.viniyoga: Of this sacred Middle Episode (Madhyama Caritra), the seer is Viṣṇu; the deity is Śrī Mahālakṣmī; the metre is uṣṇik; the power (śakti) is Śākambharī; the seed (bīja) is Durgā; the element (tattva) is air; and its essential form is the Yajurveda. For the pleasure of Śrī Mahālakṣmī, its application is in the recitation of the Middle Episode.
2.dhyana: Om. Holding in her hands a rosary and an axe, a mace, an arrow and a thunderbolt, a lotus, a bow, a water-pot, a staff, a spear, a sword and a shield, a conch, a bell, a wine-cup, a trident, a noose and the Sudarśana discus, with the lustre of coral: I worship here Mahālakṣmī, crusher of the buffalo Mahiṣa, seated on a lotus.
2.2: Long ago there was a war between the gods and the asuras for a full hundred years, when Mahiṣa was the lord of the asuras and Purandara (Indra) the lord of the gods. ॥2॥
2.3: There the army of the gods was defeated by the asuras of great valour, and having conquered all the gods, Mahiṣāsura became Indra. ॥3॥
2.4: Then the defeated gods, with the lotus-born Brahmā, the lord of creatures, at their head, went to where Śiva and Viṣṇu, whose banner bears Garuḍa, were. ॥4॥
2.5: Just as it had happened, the doings of Mahiṣāsura were told to those two by the gods, the full account of how the gods had been overcome. ॥5॥
2.6: The gods said: Of Sūrya, Indra, Agni, Vāyu and Candra, of Yama and of Varuṇa, and of the others too, he himself now occupies the offices. ॥6॥
2.7: All the hosts of the gods, driven out of heaven by him, the evil-minded Mahiṣa, wander on the earth like mortals. ॥7॥
2.8: All this we have told you, the doings of the enemy of the immortals. We have come to you for refuge; let thought be given to slaying him. ॥8॥
2.9: Hearing such words from the gods, Madhusūdana, the slayer of Madhu, and Śambhu (Śiva) grew angry, both their faces twisted with frowning brows. ॥9॥
2.10: Then from the face of Viṣṇu, the bearer of the discus, filled with great anger, there came forth a great radiance, and from Brahmā and Śaṅkara as well. ॥10॥
2.11: And from the bodies of the other gods too, Indra and the rest, a very great radiance came forth, and it all merged into one. ॥11॥
2.12: A mass of exceeding radiance, like a mountain ablaze, the gods saw there, its flames filling all the quarters of the sky. ॥12॥
2.13: That matchless radiance there, born from the bodies of all the gods, gathered into one and became a woman, pervading the three worlds with her lustre. ॥13॥
2.14: The radiance that was Śiva's gave birth to her face; from Yama's came her hair, and from the radiance of Viṣṇu her arms. ॥14॥
2.15: From the Moon's radiance came the pair of breasts, and from Indra's the waist; from Varuṇa's the shanks and thighs, and the hips from the radiance of the Earth. ॥15॥
2.16: From Brahmā's radiance came the feet, and their toes from the Sun's radiance; from that of the Vasus the fingers, and from Kubera's the nose. ॥16॥
2.17: Her teeth arose from the radiance of Prajāpati, and likewise her three eyes were born from the radiance of Agni. ॥17॥
2.18: Her two brows were the radiance of the two twilights, and her ears that of the Wind; and from the radiances of the other gods too the auspicious Śivā came into being. ॥18॥
2.19: Then, seeing her who had arisen from the mass of radiance of all the gods, the immortals, oppressed by Mahiṣa, were filled with joy. And then the gods gave her their own weapons, each his own. ॥19॥
2.20: Śiva, who bears the Pināka bow, drew a trident out of his own trident and gave it to her; and Kṛṣṇa (Viṣṇu) drew a discus from his own discus and gave it. ॥20॥
2.21: Varuṇa gave her a conch, and Agni a spear; Māruta, the Wind, gave a bow, and likewise two quivers full of arrows. ॥21॥
2.22: Indra, lord of the immortals, drew a thunderbolt out of his own thunderbolt, and the thousand-eyed god gave it to her, with a bell taken from the elephant Airāvata. ॥22॥
2.23: Yama gave a staff from his staff of death, and the lord of the waters, Varuṇa, a noose; Prajāpati gave a rosary, and Brahmā a water-pot. ॥23॥
2.24: The Sun filled all the pores of her skin with his own rays, and Kāla, Time, gave her a sword and a spotless shield. ॥24॥
2.25: The Ocean of Milk gave a spotless necklace and a pair of garments that never wear out, and a divine crest-jewel, a pair of earrings and bracelets; ॥25॥
2.26: a bright crescent-moon ornament as well, armlets on all her arms, a pair of shining anklets likewise, a peerless necklet, ॥26॥
2.27: and jewelled rings on all her fingers. Viśvakarmā gave her an exceedingly bright axe, ॥27॥
2.28: missiles of many forms, and impenetrable armour too. A garland of unfading lotuses for her head, and another for her breast, ॥28॥
2.29: the Ocean gave her, and a most beautiful lotus as well. Himavān gave a lion to be her mount, and jewels of many kinds. ॥29॥
2.30: Kubera, the lord of wealth, gave a drinking cup never empty of wine. And Śeṣa, lord of all serpents, gave her, adorned with great gems, ॥30॥
2.31: a necklace of serpents; it is he who bears this earth. By the other gods too, with ornaments and weapons likewise, the Devī, ॥31॥
2.32: being so honoured, roared aloud again and again, with peals of laughter. With her terrible roar the whole sky was filled. ॥32॥
2.33: From that boundless, exceedingly great roar a mighty echo arose. All the worlds were shaken, and the oceans trembled. ॥33॥
2.34: The earth quaked, and all the mountains shook. And the gods in their joy said to her, the rider of the lion: Victory to you! ॥34॥
2.35: And the sages, their bodies bowed in devotion, praised her. Seeing all the three worlds in turmoil, the enemies of the immortals, ॥35॥
2.36: with all their armies armed and ready, rose up with weapons raised. Mahiṣāsura cried out in anger: Ah! What is this? ॥36॥
2.37: Surrounded by all the asuras, he rushed towards that sound. Then he saw the Devī, who filled the three worlds with her radiance, ॥37॥
2.38: under the tread of whose feet the earth was bowed down, whose crown grazed the sky, who shook all the netherworlds with the twang of her bowstring, ॥38॥
2.39: and who stood with her thousand arms spread over the directions all around. Then began the battle of the enemies of the gods with that Devī, ॥39॥
2.40: a battle in which the spaces between the quarters blazed with weapons and missiles hurled in many ways. Mahiṣāsura's general, the great asura named Cikṣura, ॥40॥
2.41: fought; and Cāmara too, with others, accompanied by an army of all four divisions. The great asura named Udagra, with sixty thousand chariots, ॥41॥
2.42: fought; and Mahāhanu with an army of a crore (ten million), and the great asura Asiloman with five crore; ॥42॥
2.43: and Bāṣkala fought in the battle with an army of sixty lakh (six million). Parivārita, with many hosts of thousands of elephants and horses ॥43॥
Some take parivāritaḥ not as a name but as 'surrounded', describing Bāṣkala.
2.44: and a crore of chariots around him, fought in that battle. And the asura named Biḍāla, with five hundred crore ॥44॥
2.45: chariots around him, fought there in the conflict. And others there, by tens of thousands, surrounded by chariots, elephants and horses, ॥45॥
2.46: great asuras, fought with the Devī there in the conflict. And with thousands of crores upon crores of chariots, of elephants likewise, ॥46॥
2.47: and of horses around him, Mahiṣāsura was there in the battle. With javelins and bhindipālas, short darts hurled by hand, with spears and pestles likewise, ॥47॥
2.48: with swords, axes and paṭṭiśas, edged spears, they fought the Devī in the conflict. Some hurled spears, and others nooses. ॥48॥
2.49: With blows of their swords they set about killing the Devī. Then the Devī Caṇḍikā, in her turn, those weapons and missiles ॥49॥
2.50: cut to pieces in mere play, raining down her own weapons and missiles. Her face showing no strain, praised by the gods and seers, the Devī, ॥50॥
2.51: the Sovereign One, hurled weapons and missiles into the bodies of the asuras as well. And the Devī's mount, the lion, enraged too, shaking its mane, ॥51॥
2.52: ranged through the asura armies like a fire through forests. And the breaths that Ambikā breathed out as she fought in the battle, ॥52॥
2.53: those very breaths at once became gaṇas, troops of attendants, by hundreds of thousands. They fought with axes, bhindipālas, swords and paṭṭiśas, ॥53॥
2.54: Strengthened by the Devī's power, they went on destroying the hosts of asuras. The attendants sounded drums, and others likewise conches, ॥54॥
2.55: and others likewise played mṛdaṅgas in that great festival of battle. Then the Devī, with her trident, her mace and showers of spears, ॥55॥
2.56: and with swords and other weapons, slew great asuras by hundreds; and she felled others as well, who were stupefied by the sound of the bell. ॥56॥
2.57: And she bound other asuras with her noose and dragged them over the ground. Some were cut in two by sharp strokes of the sword, and others likewise, ॥57॥
2.58: crushed by the downward blow of the mace, lie on the ground. And some, struck hard by the pestle, vomited blood. ॥58॥
2.59: Some fell to the ground, pierced in the chest by the trident. Some on the battlefield were riddled through by a flood of arrows, ॥59॥
2.60: and, swooping like hawks, those tormentors of the gods gave up their lives. The arms of some were cut off, and others likewise had their necks severed. ॥60॥
2.61: The heads of others fell; others were split through the middle; and still other great asuras, their legs cut off, fell to the earth. ॥61॥
2.62: Some, split in two by the Devī, were left with one arm, one eye and one foot. And others, even with their heads cut off, fell and rose up again. ॥62॥
2.63: Headless trunks, grasping their finest weapons, fought with the Devī; and others there in the battle danced to the rhythm of the instruments. ॥63॥
2.64: Headless trunks whose heads had been cut off, with sword, spear and pike in hand, other great asuras kept crying to the Devī: Stop! Stop! ॥64॥
2.65: With the chariots, elephants and horses that had been felled, and with the asuras, the earth became impassable there, where that great battle took place. ॥65॥
2.66: There at once great rivers, floods of blood, flowed forth in the midst of the asura army, the blood of elephants, asuras and horses. ॥66॥
2.67: In a moment Ambikā brought that vast army of the asuras to destruction, just as fire destroys a great heap of grass and wood. ॥67॥
2.68: And that lion, letting out a mighty roar and shaking its mane, seemed to be searching out the life-breaths from the bodies of the enemies of the gods. ॥68॥
2.69: There the Devī and those attendants fought such a battle with the asuras that the gods in heaven, showering flowers, were delighted with them. ॥69॥
2.iti: Svasti, may it be well. Thus ends the second chapter, named the Slaying of Mahiṣāsura's Army, of the Devī Māhātmya in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, the age of the Manu Sāvarṇi. ॥2॥
3.dhyana: Om. She whose radiance is that of a thousand rising suns, who wears red silk and a garland of heads, whose breasts are smeared with blood, who holds a rosary, knowledge (the book), the gesture of fearlessness and the gesture of granting boons in her lotus hands, whose lotus face is lovely, shining with three eyes, the Devī whose crown is set with the moon and jewels and who is seated on a lotus: to her I bow.
3.2: Seeing that army being slaughtered, the great asura Cikṣura, the commander, then went in anger to fight Ambikā. ॥2॥
3.3: In the battle that asura rained a shower of arrows on the Devī, as a cloud rains a shower of water on the peak of Mount Meru. ॥3॥
3.4: Then the Devī, cutting down his masses of arrows in mere play, slew his horses with arrows, and the driver of the horses as well. ॥4॥
3.5: And at once she cut down his bow and his very lofty banner, and with swift arrows pierced him in the limbs, his bow now cut. ॥5॥
3.6: With his bow cut, without a chariot, his horses slain and his charioteer slain, that asura rushed at the Devī, bearing sword and shield. ॥6॥
3.7: Striking the lion's head with his sharp-edged sword, he, very swift, struck the Devī too on her left arm. ॥7॥
3.8: On reaching her arm, the sword shattered, O prince. Then he, his eyes red with anger, seized a trident. ॥8॥
3.9: And then the great asura hurled it at Bhadrakālī, blazing with radiance like the disc of the sun coming from the sky. ॥9॥
3.10: Seeing that trident flying at her, the Devī released a trident of her own; by it that trident was broken into a hundred pieces, and so was the great asura. ॥10॥
3.11: When that mighty commander of Mahiṣa's army was slain, Cāmara, tormentor of the gods, came mounted on an elephant. ॥11॥
3.12: He too then hurled a spear at the Devī; and Ambikā swiftly struck it with a cry of huṃ and brought it down to the ground, lustreless. ॥12॥
3.13: Cāmara, enraged at the sight of the spear fallen and broken, hurled a trident; that too she cut down with arrows. ॥13॥
3.14: Then the lion leapt up and, settling between the elephant's frontal globes, fought fiercely, hand to hand, with that enemy of the gods. ॥14॥
3.15: Then the two, fighting, came down from that elephant to the ground, and fought on, greatly enraged, with most terrible blows. ॥15॥
3.16: Then, springing swiftly into the sky and swooping down, the lion struck off Cāmara's head with a blow of its paw. ॥16॥
3.17: And Udagra was slain in battle by the Devī with stones, trees and the like, and Karāla too was struck down with teeth, fists and open palms. ॥17॥
3.18: The Devī, enraged, crushed Uddhata with blows of her mace, and slew Bāṣkala with a bhindipāla, and Tāmra and Andhaka with arrows. ॥18॥
3.19: Ugrāsya and Ugravīrya, and likewise Mahāhanu, the three-eyed Supreme Devī slew with her trident. ॥19॥
3.20: She sent Biḍāla's head falling from his body with her sword, and with arrows sent both Durdhara and Durmukha to the abode of Yama. ॥20॥
3.21: As his own army was thus being destroyed, Mahiṣāsura terrified those attendants with his own buffalo form. ॥21॥
3.22: Some by blows of his muzzle, others likewise by the stamping of his hooves, and others, lashed by his tail and torn apart by his two horns, ॥22॥
3.23: Some others, by his charge, by his bellowing and by his whirling, and others by the blast of his breath, he felled to the ground. ॥23॥
3.24: Having felled the host of her attendants, the pramathas, that asura rushed forward to kill the lion of the Great Devī. Then Ambikā grew angry. ॥24॥
3.25: He too, of great might, in his anger pounding the face of the earth with his hooves, hurled lofty mountains with his two horns, and bellowed. ॥25॥
3.26: Crushed by his swift circling, the earth was shattered; and the ocean, lashed by his tail, flooded everything around. ॥26॥
3.27: Torn apart by his tossing horns, the clouds went to pieces; and mountains, flung up by the wind of his breath, fell from the sky by hundreds. ॥27॥
3.28: Seeing the great asura thus swollen with rage and rushing at her, Caṇḍikā then grew wrathful, to slay him. ॥28॥
3.29: She cast her noose over him and bound that great asura. And he, bound in the great battle, gave up his buffalo form. ॥29॥
3.30: Then at once he became a lion. Just as Ambikā was cutting off his head, at that very moment a man appeared with a sword in his hand. ॥30॥
3.31: Then at once the Devī cut down that man with her arrows, together with his sword and shield. Then he became a great elephant. ॥31॥
3.32: With his trunk he dragged at that great lion, and trumpeted; but as he was dragging, the Devī cut off his trunk with her sword. ॥32॥
3.33: Then the great asura took on his buffalo body once more, and just as before threw the three worlds, with all that moves and does not move, into turmoil. ॥33॥
3.34: Then Caṇḍikā, the Mother of the world, enraged, drank the excellent drink; she drank again and again, and laughed, her eyes turned red. ॥34॥
3.35: And the asura too roared, swollen with the pride of his strength and valour, and with his two horns hurled mountains at Caṇḍikā. ॥35॥
3.36: And she, pulverising with showers of arrows those mountains hurled by him, spoke to him in faltering syllables, through the flush that intoxication had raised on her face. ॥36॥
3.38: Roar, roar for a moment, fool, while I drink this madhu, the honeyed wine. When you are slain by me right here, the gods will soon be roaring. ॥38॥
3.40: Having spoken thus, she sprang up and mounted that great asura, and pressing down his throat with her foot, she struck him with her trident. ॥40॥
3.41: Then he, trodden underfoot by her, out of his own mouth had come only half-way, held fast by the power of the Devī. ॥41॥
3.42: Only half emerged and still fighting, that great asura was felled by the Devī, who cut off his head with her great sword. ॥42॥
3.43: Then that whole army of the daityas, crying out in dismay, perished; and all the hosts of the gods attained the highest joy. ॥43॥
3.44: The gods, together with the celestial great sages, praised that Devī; the lords of the gandharvas, the celestial musicians, sang, and the troupes of apsarases, the celestial dancers, danced. ॥44॥
3.iti: Svasti, may it be well. Thus ends the third chapter, named the Slaying of Mahiṣāsura, of the Devī Māhātmya in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, the age of the Manu Sāvarṇi. ॥3॥
4.dhyana: Om. Her whose lustre is like a dark cloud, who strikes fear into the ranks of her enemies with her side-glances, who has the crescent moon bound on her crown, who holds in her hands a conch, a discus, a sword and a trident too, who has three eyes, who is mounted on the shoulders of a lion, who fills all the three worlds with her radiance, Durgā named Jayā, surrounded by the gods and served by those who seek siddhi, spiritual attainment: on her one should meditate.
4.2: When the exceedingly mighty one, that evil-souled one, and the army of the gods' foes had been slain by the Devī, the hosts of gods led by Indra, their necks and shoulders bowed low in reverence, praised her in words, their bodies made lovely by hair standing on end in their great joy. ॥2॥
4.3: The Devī who by her own power has pervaded this world, whose form is the gathered powers of all the hosts of gods: to that Ambikā, worthy of worship by all the gods and great sages, we bow in devotion. May she bring about what is auspicious for us. ॥3॥
4.4: She whose incomparable power the blessed Ananta, Brahmā and Hara cannot describe, nor her might: may that Caṇḍikā set her mind on the protection of the whole world and on the destruction of the fear of evil. ॥4॥
4.5: You who are yourself Śrī, good fortune, in the homes of the virtuous, Alakṣmī, misfortune, in the homes of the sinful, understanding in the hearts of the wise, faith in the good, and modesty in one born of a noble family: to you we bow. Protect the universe, O Devī. ॥5॥
4.6: How shall we describe this inconceivable form of yours? Or your great and surpassing valour that brought the asuras to ruin? Or those deeds of yours in battles which surpass all, O Devī, among all the hosts of asuras, gods and the rest? ॥6॥
4.7: You are the cause of all the worlds; though you have the three guṇas, the strands of nature, you are not known to have their faults; even to Hari, Hara and the others you are boundless. You are the refuge of all; this whole world is a portion of you; for you are prakṛti, nature, unmanifest, supreme and primal. ॥7॥
4.8: She at whose utterance the whole company of gods attains satisfaction in every sacrifice, O Devī: you are that Svāhā; and you are the cause of satisfaction for the hosts of ancestors too; for that very reason people utter you as Svadhā as well. ॥8॥
4.9: You who are the cause of liberation, whose great vows are beyond thought, who are constantly practised by those whose senses are well restrained and for whom truth is the essence, by sages who seek liberation and have cast off every fault: you indeed are that blessed and supreme Knowledge, O Devī. ॥9॥
4.10: Your very self is sound; you are the treasury of the most pure Ṛk and Yajus verses, and of the Sāman chants, with their Udgītha and the lovely recitation of their words. O Devī, you are the blessed Trayī, the three Vedas; for the sustaining of the world you are Vārtā, livelihood; you destroy the gravest sufferings of all the worlds. ॥10॥
4.11: You are Medhā, intelligence, O Devī, who know the essence of all the scriptures; you are Durgā, the boat across the hard-to-cross ocean of worldly existence, free of attachment; you are Śrī, who has made her sole abode in the heart of Viṣṇu, the foe of Kaiṭabha; you alone are Gaurī, who has her place in the moon-crested Śiva. ॥11॥
4.12: Your face, gently smiling, spotless, like the disc of the full moon, lovely with the lustre of the finest gold: it is most wonderful that even so, seized with fury, Mahiṣāsura, having seen that face, suddenly struck at it. ॥12॥
4.13: But, O Devī, having seen your face angry, terrible with knitted brows, its hue like the rising moon, that at once Mahiṣa did not give up his life is very strange; for who can survive the sight of Death in his anger? ॥13॥
4.14: Be gracious, O Devī; you who are supreme, be gracious for our welfare. When angered, you destroy whole families at once. This has been known just now, for this vast army of Mahiṣāsura has been wiped out. ॥14॥
4.15: They are honoured in their lands; theirs is wealth, theirs is fame, and their circle of kin does not falter; they alone are blessed, with sons, servants and wives who are devoted to them — those with whom you are pleased, you who always grant prosperity. ॥15॥
4.16: O Devī, the virtuous man always performs every righteous deed, each day and with the greatest reverence, and then goes to heaven by your grace; are you not then, O Devī, the giver of rewards in all three worlds? ॥16॥
4.17: O Durgā, when remembered you take away the fear of every creature, and when remembered by those at ease you grant them a mind exceedingly auspicious. O remover of poverty, sorrow and fear, who is there other than you whose heart is ever tender to do good to all? ॥17॥
4.18: By the slaying of these the world attains happiness; and these, even though they may have committed sin enough to keep them long in hell, may meet death in battle and go to heaven: surely it is with this thought, O Devī, that you slay the enemies. ॥18॥
4.19: Why do you not reduce to ashes by a mere look all the asuras? That you hurl your weapon at the enemies is so that even foes, purified by the weapon, may go to the higher worlds: such is your kindly thought towards those hostile ones. ॥19॥
4.20: That by the fierce flashing of the masses of light from your sword and by the mass of lustre at your trident's point the eyes of the asuras did not perish, the reason is this: on your face, a match for the radiant crescent of the moon, they were gazing. ॥20॥
4.21: O Devī, your nature subdues the conduct of the wicked; this form of yours is beyond thought, and no other can equal it; and your valour slays those who seized the gods' prowess; thus you have shown compassion even towards enemies. ॥21॥
4.22: With what can this prowess of yours be compared? And where is there a form that strikes fear into enemies yet is exceedingly captivating? Mercy in the heart and ruthlessness in battle are seen, O Devī, giver of boons, in you alone in all the three worlds. ॥22॥
4.23: By destroying the foes you have saved this whole triple world; slaying them at the head of the battle, you have brought even those enemy hosts to heaven; and our fear, too, is gone, the fear born of the frenzied enemies of the gods. Salutation to you. ॥23॥
4.24: O Devī, protect us with the trident; protect us, O Ambikā, with the sword as well; protect us with the sound of the bell and with the twang of the bowstring. ॥24॥
4.25: Protect us in the east and in the west, O Caṇḍikā; protect us in the south; and likewise in the north, O sovereign Devī, by whirling your own trident. ॥25॥
4.26: Those gentle forms of yours which roam the three worlds, and those that are exceedingly terrible: with them protect us, and the earth as well. ॥26॥
4.27: O Ambikā, the sword, the trident, the mace and whatever other weapons are yours, clinging to your hands, tender as young leaves: with them protect us on every side. ॥27॥
4.29: Thus praised by the gods, with divine flowers sprung in the Nandana garden the sustainer of the worlds was worshipped, and likewise with perfumes and unguents. ॥29॥
4.30: Devoutly perfumed with divine incense by all the gods, she, her face bright with grace, spoke to all the gods, who were bowed before her. ॥30॥
4.32: All you gods, choose whatever you desire from me. ॥32॥
4.34: The Bhagavatī has done everything; nothing remains. ॥34॥
4.35: since this enemy of ours, Mahiṣāsura, has been slain. And yet, if a boon is to be given to us by you, O great sovereign, ॥35॥
4.36: each time you are remembered, may you destroy our gravest calamities; and, O you of spotless face, the mortal who will praise you with these hymns — ॥36॥
4.37: for the increase of his fortunes, such as riches and wife, through wealth, abundance and splendour, may you, O Ambikā, always be gracious to us. ॥37॥
4.39: Propitiated in this way by the gods for the world's sake and their own, Bhadrakālī said: So be it; and she disappeared, O king. ॥39॥
4.40: Thus, O king, I have told you how in former times the Devī, who desires the good of the three worlds, arose from the bodies of the gods. ॥40॥
4.41: And again, how she came forth from the body of Gaurī to slay the wicked daityas, and likewise Śumbha and Niśumbha, ॥41॥
4.42: and to protect the worlds, as the benefactress of the gods: hear that as I relate it; I tell it to you just as it was. Hrīṃ Om. ॥42॥
4.iti: Svasti, may it be well. Thus ends the fourth chapter, named the Praise by Śakra and the Other Gods, of the Devī Māhātmya in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, the age of the Manu Sāvarṇi. ॥4॥
5.viniyoga: Of this sacred Final Episode (Uttara Caritra), the seer is Rudra; the deity is Śrī Mahāsarasvatī; the metre is anuṣṭubh; the power (śakti) is Bhīmā; the seed (bīja) is Bhrāmarī; the element (tattva) is the sun; and its essential form is the Sāmaveda. For the pleasure of Śrī Mahāsarasvatī, its application is in the reading of the Final Episode.
5.dhyana: Holding bell, trident and plough, conch and pestle, discus, bow and arrow in her lotus-hands, radiant as the cool-rayed moon that shines when the clouds are gone, born from the body of Gaurī, the support of the three worlds: here I worship Mahāsarasvatī, who crushes Śumbha and the other daityas.
5.2: Long ago the two asuras Śumbha and Niśumbha took from Indra, the lord of Śacī, the three worlds and the shares of the sacrifice, relying on their pride and might. ॥2॥
5.3: Those two themselves took over the place of the Sun, and in the same way the office of the Moon, and then those of Kubera, of Yama and of Varuṇa as well. ॥3॥
5.4: Those two themselves took over the power of Vāyu, the wind, and the work of Agni, fire, as well. Then the gods were driven out, robbed of their sovereignty and defeated. ॥4॥
5.5: Stripped of their offices, all the gods, cast out by those two great asuras, called to mind that invincible Devī. ॥5॥
5.6: They thought: She gave us a boon, saying: When I am remembered in times of calamity, I will at that very moment destroy all your gravest misfortunes. ॥6॥
5.7: Having so resolved, the gods went to Himavat, the lord of mountains, and there they then praised the Devī, Viṣṇumāyā. ॥7॥
5.9: Salutation to the Devī, to the great Devī; to Śivā, the auspicious one, salutation always. Salutation to Prakṛti, primal nature, to Bhadrā, the gracious one. With minds restrained, we bow to her. ॥9॥
5.10: Salutation to the fierce one; to the eternal one, to Gaurī, to the sustainer, salutation again and again. To her who is moonlight and who has the form of the moon, to her who is happiness, salutation always. ॥10॥
5.11: To her who is the welfare, the growth and the success of those who bow, we offer salutation again and again. To Nairṛtī, to the fortune of kings, to Śarvāṇī: to you, salutation again and again. ॥11॥
5.12: To Durgā, to her who carries us across difficulties, to the Essence, to her who does all things, to Khyāti, who is renown, and likewise to Kṛṣṇā, the dark one, and to Dhūmrā, the smoke-hued one: salutation always. ॥12॥
5.13: We bow to her who is exceedingly gentle and exceedingly fierce; to her, salutation again and again. Salutation to the Devī who is the foundation of the world; to Kṛti, who is action, salutation again and again. ॥13॥
5.14: The Devī who in all beings is called Viṣṇumāyā, the māyā of Viṣṇu: salutation to her. ॥14॥
5.16: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥16॥
5.17: The Devī who in all beings is called consciousness: salutation to her. ॥17॥
5.19: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥19॥
5.20: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of intelligence: salutation to her. ॥20॥
5.22: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥22॥
5.23: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of sleep: salutation to her. ॥23॥
5.25: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥25॥
5.26: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of hunger: salutation to her. ॥26॥
5.28: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥28॥
5.29: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of shadow: salutation to her. ॥29॥
5.31: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥31॥
5.32: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of power: salutation to her. ॥32॥
5.34: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥34॥
5.35: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of thirst: salutation to her. ॥35॥
5.37: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥37॥
5.38: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of forbearance: salutation to her. ॥38॥
5.40: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥40॥
5.41: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of birth: salutation to her. ॥41॥
5.43: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥43॥
5.44: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of modesty: salutation to her. ॥44॥
5.46: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥46॥
5.47: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of peace: salutation to her. ॥47॥
5.49: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥49॥
5.50: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of faith: salutation to her. ॥50॥
5.52: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥52॥
5.53: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of beauty: salutation to her. ॥53॥
5.55: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥55॥
5.56: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of good fortune: salutation to her. ॥56॥
5.58: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥58॥
5.59: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of livelihood: salutation to her. ॥59॥
5.61: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥61॥
5.62: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of memory: salutation to her. ॥62॥
5.64: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥64॥
5.65: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of compassion: salutation to her. ॥65॥
5.67: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥67॥
5.68: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of contentment: salutation to her. ॥68॥
5.70: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥70॥
5.71: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of a mother: salutation to her. ॥71॥
5.73: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥73॥
5.74: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of error: salutation to her. ॥74॥
5.76: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥76॥
5.77: She who presides over the senses of beings, and who in all beings is ever present: to that all-pervading Devī, salutation again and again. ॥77॥
5.78: She who abides pervading this entire world in the form of consciousness: salutation to her. ॥78॥
5.80: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥80॥
5.81: Praised in former times by the gods because they had gained what they desired, and likewise served day after day by Indra, lord of the gods: may she, the Sovereign One, the cause of good, bring about for us what is auspicious and blessed, and strike down calamities. ॥81॥
5.82: She is the Ruler to whom now we gods, tormented by the arrogant daityas, bow in salutation; and she, when remembered by those whose bodies are bowed in devotion, at that very moment destroys all our calamities. ॥82॥
5.84: As the gods there were intent on praise in this way, Pārvatī came to bathe in the waters of the Jāhnavī, the Gaṅgā, O prince. ॥84॥
5.85: She of lovely brows said to those gods: Who is it that you are praising here? And from the sheath of her body Śivā came forth and said: ॥85॥
5.86: This hymn to me is being offered by the gods, cast out by the daitya Śumbha, assembled together, and defeated in battle by Niśumbha. ॥86॥
5.87: Because Ambikā came forth from the sheath (kośa) of that Pārvatī's body, for that reason she is sung of in all the worlds as Kauśikī. ॥87॥
5.88: When she had come forth, that Pārvatī too became dark, and, having made the Himālaya her dwelling, became known as Kālikā. ॥88॥
5.89: Then Ambikā, bearing a supreme and most enchanting form, was seen by Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, the two who served Śumbha and Niśumbha. ॥89॥
5.90: And the two told Śumbha of her, exceedingly lovely as she was: O great king, a certain woman dwells there, lighting up the Himālaya. ॥90॥
5.91: Such a supreme form has not been seen anywhere by anyone. Let it be found out who this goddess may be, and let her be taken, O lord of the asuras. ॥91॥
5.92: A jewel among women, exceedingly lovely of limb, lighting up the directions with her radiance, she is staying there, O lord of the daityas; you ought to see her. ॥92॥
5.93: O lord, whatever jewels, gems, elephants, horses and the like there are in the three worlds, all of them now shine in your house. ॥93॥
5.94: Airāvata, the jewel among elephants, has been brought from Indra; so too this Pārijāta tree, and in the same way the horse Uccaiḥśravas. ॥94॥
5.95: This aerial chariot yoked with swans stands in your courtyard; a jewel of its kind, the wondrous one that was Brahmā's, it has been brought here. ॥95॥
5.96: This treasure, Mahāpadma, has been brought from Kubera, the lord of riches; and a garland of unfading lotuses, full of filaments, was the ocean's gift. ॥96॥
5.97: Varuṇa's umbrella that streams gold stands in your house; likewise this finest of chariots, which once belonged to Prajāpati. ॥97॥
5.98: O lord, Death's spear named Utkrāntidā (she who makes life depart) has been seized by you; the noose of the king of the waters, Varuṇa, is in your brother's possession. ॥98॥
5.99: And all the kinds of gems born of the ocean are Niśumbha's; Agni too gave you a pair of garments that are cleansed by fire. ॥99॥
5.100: Thus, O lord of the daityas, all the jewels have been brought to you. This lovely lady is the jewel among women: why do you not take her? ॥100॥
5.102: Having heard these words of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, Śumbha then sent the great asura Sugrīva to the Devī as his messenger. ॥102॥
5.103: Śumbha said: Go there and tell her this and this, on my word; and act quickly, in such a way that she comes gladly. ॥103॥
5.104: He went there, to where she was staying on a very beautiful spot of the mountain, and then he spoke to the Devī gently, in a sweet voice. ॥104॥
5.106: O Devī, Śumbha, lord of the daityas, is the supreme lord in the three worlds. I am a messenger sent by him, and I have come here to you. ॥106॥
5.107: He whose command is never hindered among any of the divine orders of beings, who has conquered all the enemies of the daityas: hear what he has said. ॥107॥
5.108: The whole of the three worlds is mine; the gods are subject to my will; all the shares of the sacrifices I enjoy, each one separately. ॥108॥
5.109: The choicest jewels in the three worlds are, every one, in my power; so too the jewel among elephants, the mount of the king of the gods, has been taken. ॥109॥
5.110: The jewel among horses that arose from the churning of the Ocean of Milk, the one named Uccaiḥśravas, has been offered to me by the immortals, bowing low. ॥110॥
5.111: And whatever other beings and things among the gods, the gandharvas and the serpents are jewels of their kind, O beautiful one, are with me alone. ॥111॥
5.112: O Devī, we regard you as the jewel among women in the world. So come to us, for we are the enjoyers of jewels. ॥112॥
5.113: Me, or else my younger brother Niśumbha of mighty valour, you should accept, O you of restless glances, for you are truly a jewel. ॥113॥
5.114: By becoming my wife you will gain supreme, unequalled sovereignty. Weigh this well in your mind, and become my wife. ॥114॥
5.116: Thus addressed, the Devī then spoke, smiling deeply within, Durgā, the blessed and auspicious one, by whom this world is upheld. ॥116॥
5.118: What you have said is true; nothing you have spoken here is false. Śumbha is lord of the three worlds, and Niśumbha too is his like. ॥118॥
5.119: But in this matter, how can I make false what I have vowed? Hear the vow that I made long ago, out of my little understanding. ॥119॥
5.120: He who conquers me in battle, who takes away my pride, who in the world is equal to me in strength, he will be my husband. ॥120॥
5.121: So let Śumbha come here, or the mighty Niśumbha; let him conquer me and quickly take my hand here: why delay? ॥121॥
5.123: You are arrogant; O Devī, do not speak like this before me. In the three worlds, what man could stand before Śumbha and Niśumbha? ॥123॥
5.124: Even before the other daityas, none of the gods stands face to face in battle, O Devī; how much less you, a woman, alone? ॥124॥
5.125: All the gods, led by Indra, could not stand before them in battle; how will you, a woman, go to face them, Śumbha and the others? ॥125॥
5.126: So go, as I myself tell you, to Śumbha and Niśumbha; do not go with your dignity stripped from you by being dragged by the hair. ॥126॥
5.128: So it is: Śumbha is mighty, and Niśumbha too is such. But what can I do, since my vow was made long ago without reflection? ॥128॥
5.129: So go, and all this that I have told you, tell the lord of the asuras with care; and let him do what is fitting. ॥129॥
5.iti: Svasti, may it be well. Thus ends the fifth chapter, named the Devī's Dialogue with the Messenger, of the Devī Māhātmya in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, the age of the Manu Sāvarṇi. ॥5॥
6.dhyana: Om. Her whose seat is the lord of serpents, whose slender, creeper-like body, with the great string of gems that crowns the serpents' hoods, shines bright; who is like the sun in radiance, and lit with three eyes; whose hands hold a rosary, a pitcher, a skull and a lotus; who wears the half-moon as her crest; the supreme one, who dwells in the body of Bhairava, the all-knowing Lord: on Padmāvatī I meditate.
6.2: Having heard these words of the Devī, the messenger, filled with indignation, went back to the king of the daityas and reported them to him in full. ॥2॥
6.3: Then, having heard that report of the messenger, the king of the asuras spoke in anger to Dhūmralocana, a chief of the daityas: ॥3॥
6.4: O Dhūmralocana, quickly, surrounded by your own army, bring that wicked woman by force, distraught from being dragged by the hair. ॥4॥
6.5: And if anyone else rises up to protect her, he is to be slain, be he a god, a yakṣa or a gandharva. ॥5॥
6.7: Then, so commanded by him, the daitya Dhūmralocana quickly, surrounded by sixty thousand asuras, set out at speed. ॥7॥
6.8: Then, seeing the Devī stationed on the snowy mountain, he called out loudly: Go to Śumbha and Niśumbha. ॥8॥
6.9: If you do not come to my master willingly today, then I will take you by force, distraught from being dragged by the hair. ॥9॥
6.11: Sent by the lord of the daityas, mighty and surrounded by an army, if you take me thus by force, then what can I do to you? ॥11॥
6.13: Thus addressed, the asura Dhūmralocana rushed at her; then Ambikā reduced him to ashes with the mere sound huṃ. ॥13॥
6.14: Then upon the enraged great army of the asuras Ambikā rained sharp arrows, and spears and axes as well. ॥14॥
6.15: Then, shaking its mane in fury and letting out a most terrible roar, the lion, the Devī's own mount, fell upon the army of the asuras. ॥15॥
6.16: Some daityas it slew with blows of its paw, others with its mouth, and other great asuras by trampling them and with its lip. ॥16॥
6.17: The maned lion tore open the bellies of some with its claws, and likewise, with blows of its paw, it struck heads from bodies. ॥17॥
6.18: Others in the same way it left with arms and heads cut off, and, shaking its mane, it drank the blood from the bellies of yet others. ॥18॥
6.19: In a moment that whole army was brought to ruin by the mighty one, that lion, the Devī's mount, exceedingly enraged. ॥19॥
6.20: Hearing that the asura Dhūmralocana had been slain by the Devī, and that the whole army had then been destroyed by the Devī's lion, ॥20॥
6.21: Śumbha, the overlord of the daityas, grew furious, his lip quivering, and he commanded the two great asuras, Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa: ॥21॥
6.22: O Caṇḍa, O Muṇḍa, surrounded by many troops, go there, and when you have gone, let her be brought here quickly, ॥22॥
6.23: dragged by the hair or bound. If you are in any doubt in the fight, then let her be slain by all the asuras with all their weapons. ॥23॥
6.24: When that wicked woman has been slain and the lion struck down, come back quickly; or else bind and seize that Ambikā and bring her. ॥24॥
6.iti: Svasti, may it be well. Thus ends the sixth chapter, named the Slaying of Dhūmralocana, General of Śumbha and Niśumbha, of the Devī Māhātmya in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, the age of the Manu Sāvarṇi. ॥6॥
7.dhyana: Om. Let me meditate on her who, on a jewelled seat, listens to the sweet recitation of a parrot, and whose limbs are dark, who has set one foot on a lotus, who bears a digit of the moon, who plays the vīṇā, who wears a garland of kalhāra lilies, whose shining bodice is closely fastened, who is clad in jewelled garments: Mātaṅgī, who holds a conch-shell cup, who is flushed with sweet wine, whose forehead shines with a tilaka mark.
7.2: Then, so commanded, those daityas, with Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa at their head, with an army of four divisions, set out with weapons raised. ॥2॥
7.3: Then they saw the Devī, gently smiling, stationed upon the lion on a great golden peak of the king of mountains. ॥3॥
7.4: Seeing her, they made ready and strove to seize her, and others, with bows drawn and swords in hand, drew near her. ॥4॥
7.5: Then Ambikā grew fiercely angry with those enemies, and with her anger her face then turned black as ink. ॥5॥
7.6: From the broad expanse of her forehead, knit with a frown, there swiftly came forth Kālī, terrible of face, bearing sword and noose. ॥6॥
7.7: She bore a strange khaṭvāṅga, a skull-topped staff, and was adorned with a garland of human heads; she was clad in a tiger-skin, her flesh was withered, and she was exceedingly dreadful. ॥7॥
7.8: Her mouth gaped very wide, she was fearsome with her lolling tongue; her eyes were sunken and red, and she filled the quarters with her roar. ॥8॥
7.9: Falling upon them with speed and slaying the great asuras, she devoured that host there in the army of the enemies of the gods. ॥9॥
7.10: The elephants, with their rear-guards, goad-bearing drivers, warriors and bells, she seized with one hand and flung into her mouth. ॥10॥
7.11: Likewise a warrior with his horses, and a chariot with its charioteer, she put into her mouth and chewed most dreadfully with her teeth. ॥11॥
7.12: One she caught by the hair, another by the neck; another she pressed down with her foot, and yet another she crushed with her chest. ॥12॥
7.13: And the weapons and great missiles hurled by those asuras she caught with her mouth in fury, and ground them to pieces with her teeth too. ॥13॥
7.14: That whole army of the mighty, evil-souled asuras she then trampled; some she devoured, and others she struck down. ॥14॥
7.15: Some were slain by the sword, some beaten with the khaṭvāṅga; and struck likewise by the points of her teeth, the asuras went to their destruction. ॥15॥
7.16: Seeing that entire army of the asuras felled in a moment, Caṇḍa rushed at Kālī, that most fearsome one. ॥16॥
7.17: The great asura Caṇḍa covered her of the terrible eyes with showers of most dreadful arrows, and Muṇḍa with discuses hurled by the thousand. ॥17॥
7.18: Those many discuses, entering her mouth, shone like a great many orbs of the sun passing into the belly of a cloud. ॥18॥
7.19: Then, in exceeding wrath, roaring terribly, Kālī, of the dreadful face, gleaming with teeth fearful to behold, laughed a fearsome laugh. ॥19॥
7.20: And rising up onto the great lion, the Devī ran at Caṇḍa, and seizing him by the hair, cut off his head with that sword. ॥20॥
7.21: Then Muṇḍa, seeing Caṇḍa felled, rushed at her; in her fury she struck him too with the sword and brought him down to the ground. ॥21॥
7.22: Then what was left of the army after the slaughter, seeing Caṇḍa felled and Muṇḍa too, of very great valour, fled to every quarter, stricken with fear. ॥22॥
7.23: And Kālī, taking the head of Caṇḍa and the head of Muṇḍa as well, went up to Caṇḍikā and spoke amid fierce peals of laughter: ॥23॥
7.24: Here I have offered you Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, two great sacrificial beasts; in the sacrifice of battle you yourself will slay Śumbha and Niśumbha. ॥24॥
7.26: Then, seeing the two great asuras Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa brought before her, the auspicious Caṇḍikā spoke gentle words to Kālī: ॥26॥
7.27: Since you have seized Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa and come here, you will therefore be renowned in the world as the Devī Cāmuṇḍā. ॥27॥
7.iti: Svasti, may it be well. Thus ends the seventh chapter, named the Slaying of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, of the Devī Māhātmya in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, the age of the Manu Sāvarṇi. ॥7॥
8.dhyana: Om. She who is red as the dawn, whose eyes ripple with waves of compassion, whose hands hold the noose, the goad, the arrow and the bow, who is surrounded by rays, Aṇimā and the other powers: on that Bhavānī I meditate as my very self.
8.2: When the daitya Caṇḍa had been slain and Muṇḍa struck down, and many armies had been destroyed, the lord of the asuras, ॥2॥
8.3: Śumbha the mighty, his mind then wholly in the grip of anger, ordered all the armies of the daityas to make ready. ॥3॥
8.4: Today let eighty-six daityas, weapons raised, go forth with all their forces; let eighty-four of the Kambus march out, each surrounded by his own troops. ॥4॥
8.5: Let the fifty clans of asuras, of boundless valour, and the hundred clans of the Dhaumras go forth at my command. ॥5॥
8.6: Let the Kālakas, the Daurhṛdas, the Maurvas and likewise the Kālikeya asuras, equipped for battle, march out in haste at my command. ॥6॥
8.7: Having thus given his orders, Śumbha, lord of the asuras, whose rule was fearsome, went forth surrounded by many thousands of great armies. ॥7॥
8.8: Seeing that most terrifying army approaching, Caṇḍikā with the twang of her bowstring filled the space between earth and sky. ॥8॥
8.9: Then, O king, the lion gave an exceedingly great roar, and with the sound of her bell Ambikā swelled those roars. ॥9॥
8.10: With the quarters filled by the sound of the bowstring, the lion and the bell, Kālī, her mouth opened wide, outdid them all with her terrifying roars. ॥10॥
8.11: Hearing that roar, the daitya armies, from all four sides, surrounded the Devī, the lion and Kālī in their rage. ॥11॥
8.12: Meanwhile, O king, for the destruction of the enemies of the gods and for the welfare of the lions among the immortals, endowed with exceeding valour and strength, ॥12॥
8.13: the śaktis, the powers, of Brahmā, Śiva, Kārttikeya and Viṣṇu, and likewise of Indra, came out of their bodies and went to Caṇḍikā in the forms of those gods. ॥13॥
8.14: Whatever form each god had, and whatever ornaments and mount, in just that way his śakti came to fight the asuras. ॥14॥
