8.15: Seated on a celestial car yoked with swans, holding a rosary and a water-pot, came the śakti of Brahmā; she is called Brahmāṇī. ॥15॥
8.16: Māheśvarī, mounted on a bull, holding a splendid trident, with great serpents for bracelets and adorned with the crescent moon, arrived. ॥16॥
8.17: And Kaumārī, spear in hand, whose mount is a splendid peacock, came forth to fight the daityas: Ambikā in the form of Kārttikeya. ॥17॥
8.18: Likewise the śakti Vaiṣṇavī, seated upon Garuḍa, came forward with conch, discus, mace, the Śārṅga bow and sword in her hands. ॥18॥
8.19: The śakti of Hari, who bears the incomparable form of the sacrificial Boar, she too came there, bearing a boar's body. ॥19॥
8.20: Nārasiṃhī, bearing a body like that of Nṛsiṃha, arrived there, the hosts of stars scattered by the tossing of her mane. ॥20॥
8.21: Likewise Aindrī, thunderbolt in hand, seated upon the king of elephants, arrived, thousand-eyed; just as Śakra is, so was she. ॥21॥
8.22: Then Śiva, surrounded by those śaktis of the gods, said to Caṇḍikā: Let the asuras be slain quickly, for my pleasure. ॥22॥
8.23: Then from the body of the Devī there came forth, most terrifying, the śakti Caṇḍikā, exceedingly fierce, howling like a hundred jackals. ॥23॥
8.24: And she, the Unvanquished, said to Śiva of the smoke-grey matted locks: O Lord, go as messenger to Śumbha and Niśumbha. ॥24॥
8.25: Tell Śumbha and Niśumbha, the two exceedingly proud dānavas, and the other dānavas who are assembled there for battle: ॥25॥
8.26: Let Indra have the three worlds, and let the gods partake of the oblations; go to Pātāla, the underworld, if you wish to live. ॥26॥
8.27: But if, from pride in your strength, you are eager for battle, then come, and let my jackals be sated with your flesh. ॥27॥
8.28: Because Śiva himself was appointed by that Devī to the office of messenger, she became renowned in this world as Śivadūtī, she whose messenger is Śiva. ॥28॥
8.29: The great asuras too, having heard the Devī's words as Śiva announced them, were filled with fury and went to where Kātyāyanī stood. ॥29॥
8.30: Then, first of all, at the front, with showers of arrows, spears and pikes the enemies of the gods, their wrath roused, rained down upon that Devī. ॥30॥
8.31: And she cut down those arrows, tridents, spears and axes hurled at her, playfully, with great arrows loosed from her twanging bow. ॥31॥
8.32: Likewise, in front of him, Kālī, rending the foes with the fall of her trident and crushing them with her khaṭvāṅga, then ranged about the field. ॥32॥
8.33: Robbed of valour by water flung from her kamaṇḍalu, her water-pot, and robbed of vigour: so Brahmāṇī left the enemies wherever she ran. ॥33॥
8.34: Māheśvarī with her trident, likewise Vaiṣṇavī with her discus, and Kaumārī, exceedingly wrathful, likewise with her spear, slew the daityas. ॥34॥
8.35: By the fall of Aindrī's thunderbolt, daityas and dānavas by the hundreds fell to the earth torn apart, pouring forth streams of blood. ॥35॥
8.36: Shattered by blows of the snout, their chests wounded by the tips of the tusks, struck by her of the boar form, they fell, torn also by the discus. ॥36॥
8.37: Devouring other great asuras torn apart by her claws, Nārasiṃhī ranged through the battle, filling the quarters and the sky with her roar. ॥37॥
8.38: Stricken by Śivadūtī with her fierce peals of laughter, the asuras fell to the earth, and then she devoured those who had fallen. ॥38॥
8.39: Seeing the host of Mothers, enraged, thus crushing the great asuras, the soldiers of the gods' enemies fled by various means. ॥39॥
8.40: Seeing the daityas, harassed by the host of Mothers, intent on flight, the great asura Raktabīja came forward in wrath to fight. ॥40॥
8.41: Whenever a drop of blood falls from his body to the ground, a great asura of his own size springs up on the earth. ॥41॥
8.42: Mace in hand, that great asura fought against the śakti of Indra; then Aindrī struck Raktabīja with her own thunderbolt. ॥42॥
8.43: From him, struck by the thunderbolt, much blood quickly flowed; from it arose warriors of his form and of his prowess. ॥43॥
8.44: As many drops of blood as fell from his body, so many men were born, with his valour, strength and prowess. ॥44॥
8.45: And those men born of the blood also fought there against the Mothers, a fight most dreadful with the fall of exceedingly fierce weapons. ॥45॥
8.46: And again, when the stroke of the thunderbolt wounded his head, blood flowed, and from it men were born by the thousands. ॥46॥
8.47: And Vaiṣṇavī struck him in battle with her discus; Aindrī beat that lord of the asuras with a mace. ॥47॥
8.48: By great asuras born from the flowing blood of him whom Vaiṣṇavī's discus had pierced, of his own size and by the thousands, the world was filled. ॥48॥
8.49: Kaumārī struck with her spear, and Vārāhī likewise with her sword, and Māheśvarī with her trident, the great asura Raktabīja. ॥49॥
8.50: And that daitya too, the great asura Raktabīja, possessed by anger, struck with his mace all the Mothers, each one separately. ॥50॥
8.51: As he was struck in many ways with spears, tridents and the like, the stream of his blood that fell upon the ground brought asuras into being by the hundreds. ॥51॥
8.52: And by those asuras born from the asura's blood the whole world was filled; then the gods were seized by the utmost fear. ॥52॥
8.53: Seeing those gods dejected, Caṇḍikā spoke quickly; she said to Kālī: O Cāmuṇḍā, open your mouth wide. ॥53॥
8.54: The drops of blood arising from the strokes of my weapons, and the great asuras that arise from the drop of blood, receive with this swift mouth of yours. ॥54॥
8.55: Roam the battlefield, devouring the great asuras born from it. Thus this daitya, his blood drained, will go to destruction. ॥55॥
8.56: With the fierce ones being devoured by you, no others will arise. Having said this to her, the Devī then struck him with her trident. ॥56॥
8.57: With her mouth Kālī took in Raktabīja's blood. Then, there, he struck Caṇḍikā with his mace. ॥57॥
8.58: The blow of the mace caused her not even the slightest pain. But from the body of him who had been struck, much blood flowed. ॥58॥
8.59: From wherever it flowed, Cāmuṇḍā received it with her mouth; and the great asuras who arose in her mouth from the falling blood, ॥59॥
8.60: those Cāmuṇḍā then devoured, and she drank his blood. The Devī, with trident, thunderbolt, arrows, swords and pikes, ॥60॥
8.61: struck down that Raktabīja, whose blood Cāmuṇḍā had drunk. Struck by the multitude of weapons, he fell upon the face of the earth. ॥61॥
8.62: And the great asura Raktabīja, O protector of the earth, was left bloodless. Then, O king, the gods attained incomparable joy. ॥62॥
8.63: The host of Mothers born from them danced, wild with the intoxication of blood. ॥63॥
8.iti: Svasti, may it be well. Thus ends the eighth chapter, named the Slaying of Raktabīja, of the Devī Māhātmya in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, the age of the Manu Sāvarṇi. ॥8॥
9.dhyana: Om. Glowing like the bandhūka flower and like gold, bearing a lovely rosary, the noose and the goad, and the gesture of granting boons in its own staff-like arms, with a digit of the moon for its ornament, three-eyed: in that form, half Ambikā and half Īśa, the Lord Śiva, I ceaselessly take refuge.
9.2: O revered one, you have told me this wonderful account: the greatness of the Devī's deeds in the slaying of Raktabīja. ॥2॥
9.3: And I wish to hear further: when Raktabīja had been struck down, what deed did Śumbha do, and the exceedingly wrathful Niśumbha? ॥3॥
9.5: When Raktabīja had been struck down, they flew into an unequalled rage, the asura Śumbha and Niśumbha, now that the others too had been slain in the battle. ॥5॥
9.6: Seeing his great army being slaughtered and swelling with indignation, Niśumbha then charged with the chief host of the asuras. ॥6॥
9.7: In front of him, and likewise behind him and on both his flanks, great asuras, biting their lips in anger, came up to slay the Devī. ॥7॥
9.8: Śumbha too, of great valour, came on, surrounded by his own forces, having fought with the Mothers, to slay Caṇḍikā in his anger. ॥8॥
9.9: Then an exceedingly fierce battle took place between the Devī and Śumbha and Niśumbha; the two loosed an exceedingly terrible rain of arrows, like two clouds pouring down rain. ॥9॥
9.10: With her own masses of arrows Caṇḍikā cut down the arrows those two had shot, and she struck the two lords of the asuras on their limbs with floods of weapons. ॥10॥
9.11: Niśumbha, taking up a sharp sword and a gleaming shield, struck on the head the lion, the Devī's excellent mount. ॥11॥
9.12: When her mount was struck, the Devī, with a kṣurapra, a razor-edged arrow, swiftly cut down Niśumbha's excellent sword and also his shield, marked with eight moons. ॥12॥
9.13: When his shield and sword were cut down, that asura hurled a spear; that too, as it came straight at her, she cut in two with her discus. ॥13॥
9.14: Then the dānava Niśumbha, swollen with rage, seized a trident; and as it came, the Devī crushed that too to powder with a blow of her fist. ॥14॥
9.15: Then he too whirled a mace and hurled it at Caṇḍikā; it too, shattered by the Devī's trident, was turned to ashes. ॥15॥
9.16: Then, as that foremost of the daityas came on, axe in hand, the Devī struck him with floods of arrows and felled him to the ground. ॥16॥
9.17: When his brother Niśumbha, of terrible prowess, had fallen to the ground, Śumbha, exceedingly enraged, set out to slay Ambikā. ॥17॥
9.18: Standing in his chariot, and with arms raised high aloft, holding supreme weapons — eight arms beyond compare — he shone, filling the whole sky. ॥18॥
9.19: Seeing him coming, the Devī blew her conch, and also made her bowstring twang, a sound exceedingly hard to bear. ॥19॥
9.20: And she filled the quarters with the sound of her own bell, a sound that destroyed the vigour of all the daitya armies. ॥20॥
9.21: Then the lion, with great roars that made the elephants give up their great rut, filled the sky, the earth and likewise the ten directions. ॥21॥
9.22: Then Kālī, leaping up into the sky, struck the earth with both her hands; by that resounding blow the sounds before it were drowned out. ॥22॥
9.23: Śivadūtī let out a loud, ominous peal of laughter; at those sounds the asuras trembled, and Śumbha went into the utmost rage. ॥23॥
9.24: When Ambikā cried out: Stand, stand, you wicked one! then the gods stationed in the sky called out: Victory! ॥24॥
9.25: The spear that Śumbha came forward and hurled, exceedingly dreadful with its flames, shining like a mass of fire as it came on, was beaten back with a great meteor. ॥25॥
9.26: Śumbha's lion-roar filled all the space within the three worlds; and the dreadful crash of a thunderclap overpowered it, O lord of the earth. ॥26॥
9.27: The Devī cut down the arrows Śumbha shot, and Śumbha those she sent, each with their own fierce arrows, by hundreds and by thousands. ॥27॥
9.28: Then Caṇḍikā, enraged, struck him with her trident; and he, struck down then, fell senseless to the ground. ॥28॥
9.29: Then Niśumbha, regaining consciousness, took up his bow and struck with arrows the Devī, Kālī and the lion as well. ॥29॥
9.30: And again, making ten thousand arms, the lord of the dānavas, the son of Diti, covered Caṇḍikā with his discus-weapons. ॥30॥
9.31: Then the blessed Durgā, destroyer of the pain of hard straits, enraged, the Devī cut down with her own arrows those discuses and those arrows. ॥31॥
9.32: Then Niśumbha, seizing a mace, rushed swiftly at Caṇḍikā to slay her, surrounded by the daitya army. ॥32॥
9.33: Even as he rushed upon her, Caṇḍikā swiftly cut his mace with her sharp-edged sword; and he took up a trident. ॥33॥
9.34: As Niśumbha, the tormentor of the immortals, came on, trident in hand, Caṇḍikā pierced him in the heart with her trident, hurled with force. ॥34॥
9.35: From the heart of him, pierced by the trident, there came forth another, a man of great strength and great valour, who was saying: Stand! ॥35॥
9.36: As he was coming out, the Devī laughed aloud and then cut off his head with her sword; then he fell to the ground. ॥36॥
9.37: Then the lion, crushing their necks with his fierce fangs, devoured those asuras; and likewise Kālī and Śivadūtī devoured others. ॥37॥
9.38: Some great asuras, pierced through by Kaumārī's spear, perished; others were driven off by water made holy by Brahmāṇī's mantras. ॥38॥
9.39: Likewise others fell, pierced by Māheśvarī's trident; some, by the blows of Vārāhī's snout, were pounded to dust on the ground. ॥39॥
9.40: Dānavas were cut to pieces by Vaiṣṇavī's discus, and likewise others by the thunderbolt let fly from the tip of Aindrī's hand. ॥40॥
9.41: Some asuras perished; some fled from the great battle; and Kālī, Śivadūtī and the lion, the king of beasts, devoured others. ॥41॥
9.iti: Svasti, may it be well. Thus ends the ninth chapter, named the Slaying of Niśumbha, of the Devī Māhātmya in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, the age of the Manu Sāvarṇi. ॥9॥
10.dhyana: Om. Her who glows like heated gold, whose eyes are the sun, the moon and fire, who holds the bow and arrows with the goad, the noose and the trident in her lovely arms, whose form is Śiva and Śakti, Kāmeśvarī, who wears the crescent moon: her I worship in my heart.
10.2: Seeing his brother Niśumbha, dear to him as his own life, slain, and his army being slaughtered, Śumbha in his anger spoke these words: ॥2॥
10.3: O Durgā, spoilt by the pride of your strength, do not be arrogant. You fight relying on the strength of other women, and yet you are so very haughty. ॥3॥
10.5: I alone am here in the world; who else, a second, is there besides me? See, wicked one, these powers of mine entering into me alone. ॥5॥
10.6: Then all those goddesses, headed by Brahmāṇī, were dissolved into the body of that Devī; then Ambikā alone was there. ॥6॥
10.8: The many forms in which I stood here through my power, those I have withdrawn; I stand alone in the battle. Be steady. ॥8॥
10.10: Then a battle began between the two, the Devī and Śumbha, a terrible battle, as all the gods and the asuras looked on. ॥10॥
10.11: With showers of arrows, with sharp weapons and with most dreadful missiles, the battle between the two went on again, terrifying all the worlds. ॥11॥
10.12: The hundreds of divine missiles that Ambikā then let fly, the lord of the daityas broke with weapons that warded them off. ॥12॥
10.13: And the divine missiles he let fly, the Supreme Devī broke as if in play, with fierce cries of huṃ and the like. ॥13॥
10.14: Then that asura covered the Devī with hundreds of arrows; and the Devī, angered at that, cut his bow with her arrows in turn. ॥14॥
10.15: When his bow was cut, the lord of the daityas then took up a spear; that too, as it rested in his hand, the Devī cut with her discus. ॥15॥
10.16: Then, taking up a sword and a shining shield marked with a hundred moons, the sovereign lord of the daityas rushed at that Devī. ॥16॥
10.17: Even as he rushed on, Caṇḍikā swiftly cut his sword with sharp arrows loosed from her bow, and also his shield, spotless as the sun's rays; and she struck down his horses, and his chariot with the charioteer. ॥17॥
10.18: Then that daitya, his horses slain, his bow cut, left without a charioteer, seized a dreadful war-hammer, intent on killing Ambikā. ॥18॥
10.19: As he rushed on, the Devī cut his war-hammer with sharp arrows; even so he ran at her swiftly, raising his fist. ॥19॥
10.20: That bull among the daityas brought his fist down on the Devī's heart; and the Devī too struck him on the chest with the palm of her hand. ॥20॥
10.21: Struck by the blow of her palm, that king of the daityas fell to the ground, and at once rose up again, just as before. ॥21॥
10.22: And leaping up, he seized the Devī and rose high into the sky; there too Caṇḍikā fought with him, with nothing to support her. ॥22॥
10.23: Then in the sky the daitya and Caṇḍikā fought each other hand to hand, a combat never seen before, which filled the siddhas and sages with wonder. ॥23॥
10.24: Then Ambikā, having fought hand to hand with him for a long time, lifted him up, whirled him round and hurled him to the ground. ॥24॥
10.25: Thrown down, he reached the earth and, swift, raising his fist, the wicked one rushed at her, wishing to slay Caṇḍikā. ॥25॥
10.26: Then, as he came on, the lord of all the daitya people the Devī pierced in the chest with her trident and felled to the ground. ॥26॥
10.27: Wounded by the point of the Devī's trident, he fell to the ground, lifeless, shaking all the earth with its oceans, islands and mountains. ॥27॥
10.28: Then, when that evil-souled one was slain, all became serene; the world attained great well-being, and the sky became clear. ॥28॥
10.29: The clouds of ill omen, with their meteors, that had been there before were stilled; and when he was felled there, the rivers likewise flowed within their courses. ॥29॥
10.30: Then all the hosts of gods became full of joy at heart when he was slain, and the gandharvas sang sweetly. ॥30॥
10.31: Likewise others played music, and the hosts of apsarases danced; pure winds likewise blew, and the sun shone with a fair light. ॥31॥
10.32: The fires that had gone out blazed up, and the sounds that had arisen in the quarters were stilled. ॥32॥
10.iti: Svasti, may it be well. Thus ends the tenth chapter, named the Slaying of Śumbha, of the Devī Māhātmya in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, the age of the Manu Sāvarṇi. ॥10॥
11.dhyana: Om. Her whose radiance is that of the rising sun, who wears the moon as her crown, whose breasts are high, who has three eyes, whose face is smiling, whose hands show the gesture of granting boons, the goad, the noose and the gesture of fearlessness: Bhuvaneśī I worship.
11.2: When the great lord of the asuras had been slain there by the Devī, the gods together with Indra, with Agni at their head, praised her, Kātyāyanī, for they had gained what they desired, their blooming lotus-faces lighting up the quarters. ॥2॥
11.3: O Devī, who take away the distress of those who come to you for refuge, be gracious. Be gracious, O Mother of all the world. Be gracious, O ruler of the universe; protect the universe. You, O Devī, are the sovereign of all that moves and does not move. ॥3॥
11.4: You alone have become the support of the world, for you abide in the form of the earth; by you, abiding in the form of the waters, all this is nourished, O you whose valour none can overstep. ॥4॥
11.5: You are the power of Viṣṇu, of boundless valour; you are the seed of the universe, the supreme māyā, the power that deludes. O Devī, all this is held in delusion; you indeed, when gracious, are the cause of liberation on earth. ॥5॥
11.6: All forms of knowledge, O Devī, are your aspects, and so are all women, every one, throughout the worlds. By you alone, the Mother, all this is filled. What praise can there be of you? You are beyond all that is to be praised, the highest speech. ॥6॥
Read as one compound, stavya-parā-aparā-uktiḥ, the last line is also taken to mean: you are the higher and the lower speech about all that is to be praised.
11.7: When, as the Devī who are all beings, the giver of enjoyment and liberation, you have been praised, what excellent words could there be for further praise? ॥7॥
11.8: O you who abide in the heart of every person in the form of intelligence, O Devī, giver of heaven and liberation, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥8॥
11.9: O you who, in the form of kalā, kāṣṭhā and the other measures of time, bring about change, O you who have the power to bring the universe to its end, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥9॥
11.10: O auspiciousness of all that is auspicious, O Śivā, the auspicious one, accomplisher of every aim, O giver of refuge, O three-eyed one, O Gaurī, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥10॥
11.11: O you who are the power of creation, preservation and destruction, O eternal one, O abode of the guṇas, the strands of nature, O you who are made of the guṇas, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥11॥
11.12: O you who are intent on rescuing the wretched and the afflicted who come to you for refuge, O Devī who take away the distress of all, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥12॥
11.13: O you who are seated in the celestial car yoked with swans, who bear the form of Brahmāṇī, O Devī who sprinkle water with kuśa grass, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥13॥
11.14: O you who hold the trident, the moon and the serpent, who ride the great bull, O Nārāyaṇī in the form of Māheśvarī, salutation to you. ॥14॥
11.15: O you who are surrounded by peacocks and cocks, who bear the great spear, O sinless one, O you who abide in the form of Kaumārī, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥15॥
11.16: O you who have taken up the supreme weapons, the conch, the discus, the mace and the Śārṅga bow, be gracious, O you in the form of Vaiṣṇavī; O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥16॥
11.17: O you who hold the fierce great discus, who lifted up the earth on your tusk, O Śivā in the form of the Boar, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥17॥
11.18: O you who, in the fierce form of the Man-Lion, set out to slay the daityas, O you who undertake the protection of the three worlds, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥18॥
11.19: O crowned one, wielder of the great thunderbolt, resplendent with a thousand eyes, O Aindrī, taker of Vṛtra's life, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥19॥
11.20: O you who, in the form of Śivadūtī, slew the mighty host of the daityas, O you of terrible form and mighty roar, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥20॥
11.21: O you whose face is dreadful with fangs, who are adorned with a garland of heads, O Cāmuṇḍā, crusher of Muṇḍa, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥21॥
11.22: O Lakṣmī, O Modesty, O great Knowledge, O Faith, O Nourishment, O Svadhā, offering to the ancestors, O Constant one, O great Night, O Mahāmāyā, great power of illusion, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥22॥
11.23: O Medhā, intelligence, O Sarasvatī, O excellent one, O Prosperity, O tawny Bābhravī, O dark Tāmasī, O self-restrained one, O Sovereign, be gracious; O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥23॥
11.24: O you who are the form of all, O Mistress of all, O you who are endowed with every power, protect us from fears, O Devī; O Devī Durgā, salutation to you. ॥24॥
11.25: May this gentle face of yours, adorned with three eyes, protect us from all beings. O Kātyāyanī, salutation to you. ॥25॥
11.26: Fearsome with flames, exceedingly fierce, the slayer of all the asuras: may your trident protect us from fear. O Bhadrakālī, salutation to you. ॥26॥
11.27: That bell which, filling the world with its sound, destroys the might of the daityas: may it protect us from sins, O Devī, as children are protected. ॥27॥
11.28: Smeared with the mire of the blood and fat of the asuras, gleaming in your hand, may your sword be auspicious. O Caṇḍikā, we bow to you. ॥28॥
11.29: When pleased, you destroy all diseases, but when angered, all the desires that are longed for. For people who have taken refuge in you there is no calamity; those who have taken refuge in you indeed become a refuge for others. ॥29॥
11.30: This slaughter which you have wrought today, O Devī, of the great asuras, the haters of dharma, of what is right, making your own form manifold through many forms: O Ambikā, who else could accomplish that? ॥30॥
11.31: In the branches of knowledge, in the scriptures, and in the lamps of discernment, the primeval words (the Vedas), who is there other than you? In the pit of attachment, filled with exceedingly great darkness, who else makes this universe whirl about so intensely? ॥31॥
11.32: Where there are rākṣasas, where there are serpents of deadly venom, where there are enemies, where there are hosts of robbers, where there is a forest fire, and likewise in the midst of the ocean: there you stand and protect the universe. ॥32॥
11.33: O Queen of the universe, you protect the universe; as the very self of the universe, you uphold the universe here. You are to be revered by the lord of the universe; those who bow to you in devotion become the refuge of the universe. ॥33॥
11.34: O Devī, be gracious; protect us from the fear of enemies always, just as you have done at once, now, by slaying the asuras. Swiftly quell the sins of every world, and the great calamities that arise when evil portents ripen. ॥34॥
11.35: O Devī, remover of the afflictions of the universe, be gracious to those who bow to you. O you who are worthy of praise by the dwellers of the three worlds, be the giver of boons to the worlds. ॥35॥
11.37: O hosts of gods, I am the giver of boons. Whatever boon you desire in your minds, choose it; I shall give it, a boon for the good of the worlds. ॥37॥
11.39: O Sovereign of all, the quelling of every affliction that besets the three worlds and the destruction of our enemies: may you accomplish them in just this way. ॥39॥
11.41: When the Vaivasvata manvantara, the age of the Manu Vaivasvata, has come, in the twenty-eighth yuga, cycle of ages, two other great asuras, Śumbha and Niśumbha, will be born. ॥41॥
11.42: Born in the house of the cowherd Nanda, from the womb of Yaśodā, I shall then destroy those two, dwelling on the Vindhya mountain. ॥42॥
11.43: Again, in an exceedingly terrible form, upon the earth I shall descend and slay the dānavas of Vipracitti's line as well. ॥43॥
11.44: And as I devour those fierce great asuras of Vipracitti's line, my teeth will become red, like pomegranate flowers. ॥44॥
11.45: Then the gods in heaven, and humans in the world of mortals, praising me, will ever call me Raktadantikā, the red-toothed one. ॥45॥
11.46: And again, in a drought lasting a hundred years, when there is no water, remembered by the sages, I shall appear on the earth, not born of a womb. ॥46॥
11.47: Then I shall look upon the sages with a hundred eyes, and so people will celebrate me as Śatākṣī, the hundred-eyed. ॥47॥
11.48: Then, O gods, with vegetables grown from my own body, which sustain life, I shall nourish the whole world until the rains come. ॥48॥
11.49: Then I shall become renowned on earth as Śākambharī, she who nourishes with vegetables, and right there I shall slay the great asura called Durgama. ॥49॥
11.50: And so my name will become renowned as Durgā Devī. And again, when on the Himālaya I take on a terrible form ॥50॥
11.51: and devour the rākṣasas to protect the sages, then all the sages, their bodies bowed low, will praise me. ॥51॥
11.52: And so my name will become renowned as Bhīmā Devī, the terrible Devī. When the asura named Aruṇa causes great affliction in the three worlds, ॥52॥
11.53: then I shall take on a bee-form made up of countless bees, and for the good of the three worlds I shall slay that great asura. ॥53॥
11.54: And then people everywhere will praise me as Bhrāmarī, the Devī of the bees. Thus, whenever affliction arising from the dānavas comes about, ॥54॥
11.55: then each time I shall descend and bring about the destruction of the enemies. ॥55॥
11.iti: Svasti, may it be well. Thus ends the eleventh chapter, named the Praise of Nārāyaṇī, of the Devī Māhātmya in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, the age of the Manu Sāvarṇi. ॥11॥
12.dhyana: Om. Her whose radiance equals the splendour of lightning, who is seated on the shoulder of the lion, who is fearsome, who is attended by maidens whose hands gleam with swords and shields, who holds in her hands the discus, mace, sword, shield, arrows, bow, bowstring and the threatening gesture of the raised forefinger, who is fiery in nature, who bears the moon: the three-eyed Durgā I worship.
12.2: Whoever, with a collected mind, will praise me constantly with these hymns, all his affliction I shall bring to rest, without doubt. ॥2॥
12.3: Those who will tell of the destruction of Madhu and Kaiṭabha and the slaying of Mahiṣāsura, and likewise of the slaying of Śumbha and Niśumbha, ॥3॥
12.4: and those who, single-minded, on the eighth, the fourteenth and the ninth days of the lunar fortnight, will listen with devotion to my excellent Māhātmya, ॥4॥
12.5: for them there will be no wrongdoing at all, nor calamities born of wrongdoing; there will be no poverty, nor parting from those they love. ॥5॥
12.6: No fear will come to him from enemies, from robbers or from the king, nor will it ever arise from weapons, from fire or from a flood of water. ॥6॥
12.7: Therefore this Māhātmya of mine should be recited by those of collected mind, and always heard with devotion: it is the supreme and great means of welfare. ॥7॥
12.8: All calamities born of great epidemics, and likewise the threefold portent, my Māhātmya can quell. ॥8॥
12.9: The shrine of mine where this is duly recited every day, that I shall never forsake; my presence is established there. ॥9॥
12.10: At the presenting of offerings, in worship, in the fire rite and at a great festival, this whole Māhātmya of mine should be recited and also made to be heard. ॥10॥
12.11: The offering and worship, done as it may be by one who knows or even by one who does not, I shall receive with love, and likewise the fire oblation so offered. ॥11॥
12.12: In the autumn season the great worship is performed, the yearly one; having heard this Māhātmya of mine at it, filled with devotion, ॥12॥
12.13: a man will be freed from all afflictions and endowed with wealth and grain by my grace; of this there is no doubt. ॥13॥
12.14: Having heard this Māhātmya of mine, and likewise my auspicious manifestations and my valour in battles, a man becomes fearless. ॥14॥
12.15: Enemies are destroyed, welfare comes about, and the family of men who listen to my Māhātmya rejoices. ॥15॥
12.16: In every rite of pacification, and likewise on seeing a bad dream, and in severe afflictions from the planets, one should listen to my Māhātmya. ॥16॥
12.17: Calamities subside, and so do the dreadful afflictions from the planets, and a bad dream seen by men turns into a good dream. ॥17॥
12.18: It brings peace to children seized by the bālagrahas, the spirits that seize children, and when men's union is broken, it is the best means of making friendship. ॥18॥
12.19: It is supreme in destroying the strength of all the wicked; by its mere recitation it destroys rākṣasas, evil spirits and piśācas. ॥19॥
12.20: This whole Māhātmya of mine brings about my presence. With animal offerings, flowers, arghya water and incense, and likewise with excellent perfumes and lamps, ॥20॥
12.21: with the feeding of brāhmaṇas, with oblations, with sprinkling water day and night, and with various other enjoyments and gifts, the pleasure given to me over a year, ॥21॥
12.22: that same pleasure is given to me when this is recited or heard but once. Heard, it removes sins and grants health as well. ॥22॥
12.23: The recital of my manifestations gives protection from evil spirits. My deeds in battles, the slaying of the wicked daityas: ॥23॥
12.24: when they are heard, men feel no fear caused by enemies. And the hymns which you gods have made, and those which the brahmarṣis have made, ॥24॥
12.25: and those made by Brahmā, may they grant an auspicious understanding. In a forest or on a desolate road, surrounded by a forest fire, ॥25॥
12.26: or surrounded by robbers in a lonely place, or seized by enemies, or pursued by lions and tigers, or in the forest by wild elephants, ॥26॥
12.27: or ordered by an angry king to be put to death, or held in bonds, or tossed by the wind while on a ship on the great ocean, ॥27॥
12.28: or when weapons are falling in an exceedingly terrible battle, or in all dreadful afflictions, or even when tormented by pain, ॥28॥
12.29: A man who remembers these deeds of mine is set free from danger. By my power, lions and the like, robbers, and enemies as well ॥29॥
12.30: flee while still far off from one who remembers my deeds. ॥30॥
12.32: Having spoken thus, the blessed Caṇḍikā, of fierce valour, ॥32॥
12.33: vanished right there while all the gods looked on. And those gods too, free from fear, took up their own offices as before; ॥33॥
12.34: their enemies slain, they all enjoyed their shares in the sacrifice. As for the daityas, when Śumbha, the enemy of the gods, had been slain by the Devī in battle, ॥34॥
12.35: he, the destroyer of the world, exceedingly fierce and of matchless valour, and Niśumbha too, of great might, had been slain — those of them who were left went to Pātāla, the underworld. ॥35॥
12.36: Thus that blessed Devī, though eternal, again and again comes forth, O king, and protects the world. ॥36॥
12.37: By her this universe is deluded, and she alone brings the universe to birth; when entreated she grants knowledge, and when pleased, prosperity. ॥37॥
12.38: This whole cosmos, O lord of men, is pervaded by her, by the Great Devī, Mahākālī, whose very form is Mahāmārī, the great destroyer. ॥38॥
12.39: She herself, at the appointed time, is Mahāmārī; she herself, the unborn, becomes creation; she herself, the eternal one, in due time sustains living beings. ॥39॥
12.40: In times of prosperity she herself is Lakṣmī in the homes of men, granting increase; and in times of want she herself likewise becomes Alakṣmī, misfortune, for their ruin. ॥40॥
12.41: Praised, and duly worshipped with flowers, and with fragrances, incense and the like, she gives wealth and sons, a mind set on dharma (right conduct), and an auspicious destiny. ॥41॥
12.iti: Svasti, may it be well. Thus ends the twelfth chapter, named the Words of the Bhagavatī, of the Devī Māhātmya in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, the age of the Manu Sāvarṇi. ॥12॥
13.dhyana: Om. She whose radiance is like the orb of the rising sun, who has four arms and three eyes, who holds the noose and the goad and shows the gestures of granting boons and of fearlessness: I worship her, Śivā, the auspicious Devī.
13.2: This supreme Glory of the Devī, O king, has been told to you. Such is the power of that Devī by whom this world is upheld. ॥2॥
13.3: In the same way, knowledge is brought about by the divine Viṣṇumāyā, Viṣṇu's power of illusion. By her you, this merchant, and likewise other discerning men ॥3॥
13.4: are being deluded and have been deluded, and others too will fall into delusion. Go for refuge, O great king, to her, the supreme sovereign Devī. ॥4॥
13.5: When worshipped, she alone gives men enjoyment, heaven and final liberation. ॥5॥
13.7: Having heard these words of his, Suratha, that lord of men, ॥7॥
13.8: bowed down before that greatly blessed sage of rigorous vows, and, despondent through his excessive sense of possession and the seizure of his kingdom, ॥8॥
13.9: went at once to practise austerity, and so did that merchant, O great sage; and, for the sake of beholding Ambā, the Mother, the king took his place on the sandy bank of a river. ॥9॥
13.10: And that merchant too performed austerity, reciting the supreme Devī Sūkta, the hymn to the Devī. The two of them made an earthen image of the Devī on that sandbank, ॥10॥
13.11: and worshipped her with flowers, incense, fire offerings and libations, fasting, self-controlled, their minds fixed on her, and wholly absorbed. ॥11॥
13.12: And the two also made an offering sprinkled with blood from their own bodies. When, self-controlled, they had worshipped her thus for three years, ॥12॥
13.13: Caṇḍikā, the upholder of the world, well pleased, appeared before them and spoke. ॥13॥
13.15: Whatever is asked for by you, O king, and by you, O joy of your family, receive all of it from me: well pleased, I give it to you. ॥15॥
13.17: Then the king chose, for another birth, an imperishable kingdom, and here, in this very life, his own kingdom, with his enemies' forces crushed by might. ॥17॥
13.18: Then the merchant too, his mind weary of the world, chose knowledge: being wise, he chose the knowledge that ends attachment in the form of 'mine' and 'I'. ॥18॥
13.20: In a very few days, O king, you will obtain your own kingdom. ॥20॥
13.21: When you have slain your enemies, it will stand unshaken for you there. ॥21॥
13.22: And when you have died, obtaining birth once more from the god Vivasvat, the Sun, ॥22॥
13.23: you will be on earth the Manu named Sāvarṇika. ॥23॥
13.24: And, O best of merchants, the boon that you have desired from me, ॥24॥
13.25: that I grant you: for your final perfection, knowledge will be yours. ॥25॥
13.27: Having thus given the two of them the boon each desired, the Devī, ॥27॥
13.28: praised by the two of them with devotion, vanished at once. Thus, having received the boon from the Devī, Suratha, the foremost of kṣatriyas, the warrior order, ॥28॥
13.29: will obtain birth from Sūrya, the Sun, and become Sāvarṇi, the Manu. ॥29॥
13.end: Thus, having received the boon from the Devī, Suratha, the foremost of kṣatriyas, the warrior order, will obtain birth from Sūrya and become Sāvarṇi, the Manu. Klīṃ Om.
13.iti: Svasti, may it be well. Thus ends the thirteenth chapter, named the Granting of Boons to Suratha and the Merchant, of the Devī Māhātmya in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, the age of the Manu Sāvarṇi. ॥13॥
aparadha.1: Om. Having committed a hundred offences, if one then calls out the name Jagadambā, Mother of the world, the state one attains is not attained even by Brahmā and the other gods. ॥1॥
aparadha.2: I am guilty of offences, and I have come to you for refuge, O Mother of the world. Now I am one who deserves your compassion; do as you wish. ॥2॥
aparadha.3: Through ignorance, forgetfulness or confusion, whatever has been done too little or too much, may all that be forgiven, O Devī; be gracious, O Supreme Sovereign. ॥3॥
aparadha.4: O Kāmeśvarī, O Mother of the world, whose form is being, consciousness and bliss, accept this worship with love; be gracious, O Supreme Sovereign. ॥4॥
aparadha.5: The Devī is made of all forms, and the whole world is made of the Devī. Therefore I bow to you, the Supreme Sovereign, whose form is the universe. ॥5॥
aparadha.6: Whatever syllable has dropped out, and whatever may be lacking its mātrā, the measure of a vowel, may all that become complete by your grace, O Great Sovereign. ॥6॥
aparadha.7: O Mother of the world, whatever I have uttered here in this recitation lacking a visarga, a bindu (the nasal dot) or a syllable, may that become wholly complete through your grace, and may the fulfilment of my resolve always come about. ॥7॥
aparadha.8: Whatever lacks a mātrā, a bindu, the pair of dots (the visarga), a word, a pair of words, a letter or the like; whatever was done with devotion or without it, in due order or by force, clearly or indistinctly, O Mother; and whatever, through delusion or ignorance, has now been read or left unread in this hymn of yours: may all that be complete in all its parts by your grace, O Bhagavatī, giver of boons; be gracious. ॥8॥
aparadha.9: Be gracious, O Bhagavatī, O Mother; be gracious, O you who love your devotees. Show me your grace, O Devī; O Durgā, O Devī, salutation to you. ॥9॥
aparadha.iti: Thus ends the Aparādhakṣamāpaṇa Stotra, the hymn asking pardon for offences.
devi-sukta.1: Om. I move with the Rudras and with the Vasus; I move with the Ādityas and with the Viśvedevas, the All-gods, too. I uphold both Mitra and Varuṇa; I uphold Indra and Agni, and I uphold both the Aśvins. ॥1॥
devi-sukta.2: I uphold Soma, who is to be pressed; I uphold Tvaṣṭṛ, and Pūṣan and Bhaga. I bestow wealth on the one who offers oblations, on the zealous sacrificer who presses the Soma. ॥2॥
devi-sukta.3: I am the sovereign queen, the gatherer of riches, the knowing one, the first of those worthy of worship. Such as I am, the gods have set me out in many places, me who dwell in many places and make myself enter into many beings. ॥3॥
devi-sukta.4: Through me he eats food, he who sees, who breathes, who hears what is spoken. Not knowing me, they yet dwell in me. Hear, O famed one: I tell you what is worthy of belief. ॥4॥
Some take upakṣiyanti in the sense of wasting away and read: those who do not know me waste away.
devi-sukta.5: I myself declare this, which is welcomed by gods and by men alike. Whomever I desire, him I make mighty; him I make a Brahmā, him a seer, him one of fine wisdom. ॥5॥
Some read brahmāṇam not as Brahmā but as a brahman, a priest versed in the sacred word.
devi-sukta.6: I stretch the bow for Rudra, so that his arrow may slay the hater of sacred knowledge. I make battle for the people; I have entered into heaven and earth. ॥6॥
devi-sukta.7: I give birth to the father on the summit of this world; my source is within the waters, in the ocean. From there I spread out over all the worlds, and I touch yonder heaven with my height. ॥7॥
devi-sukta.8: I alone blow forth like the wind, laying hold of all the worlds. Beyond heaven, beyond this earth too, so vast have I become through my greatness. ॥8॥
devi-sukta.iti: Thus ends the Devī Sūkta, as the Ṛgveda gives it.

dhyana.1: Om. Her whose radiance is like the bandhūka (noon-flower), who dwells on the seat of five skulls,
whose jewelled crown bears the shining digit of the moon, who wears a garland of heads,
dhyana.2: who has three eyes, who is clad in red, whose breasts are full, high and shaped like pots,
and who holds, in order, a book, a rosary, the gesture of granting boons and the gesture of fearlessness —
dhyana.3: on her, holding these and honoured in the northern tradition (Uttarāmnāya), one should always meditate.
dhyana.4: She who is Caṇḍī, crusher of Madhu, Kaiṭabha and the other demons; she who uprooted Mahiṣāsura;
she who crushed Dhūmrekṣaṇa, Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa; she who devoured Raktabīja;
the Power who crushed the demons Śumbha and Niśumbha; she who is the supreme giver of accomplishment (siddhi):
may that Devī, ruler of the universe, together with her nine crore forms, protect me.
argala.viniyoga: Om. Of this mantra, the Śrī Argalā Stotra, the seer is Viṣṇu,
the metre is anuṣṭubh, the deity is Śrī Mahālakṣmī;
for the pleasure of Śrī Jagadambā, the Mother of the World, it is applied in recitation as a part of reading the Saptaśatī.
argala.1: Om. Victory to you, O Devī Cāmuṇḍā; victory to you, O remover of the sufferings of beings;
victory to you, O Devī who pervade all; O Kālarātri, salutation to you. ॥1॥
argala.2: You are Jayantī, Maṅgalā, Kālī, Bhadrakālī and Kapālinī;
you are Durgā, Śivā, Kṣamā, Dhātrī, Svāhā and Svadhā: salutation to you. ॥2॥
argala.3: O destroyer of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, O giver of boons to Brahmā the Creator, salutation to you.
Give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥3॥
argala.4: O destroyer of Mahiṣāsura, O giver of happiness to your devotees, salutation to you.
Give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥4॥
argala.5: O Devī, slayer of Dhūmranetra, O giver of dharma (right conduct), pleasure and wealth,
give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥5॥
argala.6: O Devī, slayer of Raktabīja, O destroyer of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa,
give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥6॥
argala.7: O destroyer of Niśumbha and Śumbha, O giver of good to the three worlds, salutation to you.
Give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥7॥
argala.8: O Devī, whose two feet are worshipped, O giver of all good fortune,
give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥8॥
argala.9: O you whose form and deeds are beyond thought, O destroyer of all enemies,
give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥9॥
argala.10: And to those who always bow to you with devotion, O Aparṇā, remover of sins,
give them beauty, give them victory, give them fame, and slay their enemies. ॥10॥
argala.11: To those who praise you with devotion, O Caṇḍikā, destroyer of disease,
give them beauty, give them victory, give them fame, and slay their enemies. ॥11॥
argala.12: O Caṇḍikā, ever victorious in battle, O destroyer of sin,
give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥12॥
argala.13: Give me good fortune and health; O Devī, give me supreme happiness.
Give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥13॥
argala.14: O Devī, bring about my welfare; bestow abundant prosperity on me.
Give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥14॥
argala.15: Bring about the destruction of those who hate me; bestow on me strength in high measure.
Give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥15॥
argala.16: O Ambikā, whose feet are rubbed by the crest-jewels of gods and asuras as they bow down,
give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥16॥
argala.17: Make me learned, renowned and prosperous.
Give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥17॥
argala.18: O Devī, destroyer of the pride of demons with mighty, staff-like arms,
give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥18॥
argala.19: O Caṇḍikā, destroyer of the pride of fierce demons, to me who bow to you
give beauty, give victory, give fame, and slay my enemies. ॥19॥
argala.20: O four-armed one, praised by four-faced Brahmā, O Supreme Sovereign,
give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥20॥
argala.21: O Devī, ever praised by Kṛṣṇa with unceasing devotion, O Ambikā,
give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥21॥
argala.22: O Supreme Sovereign, praised by Śiva, lord of the daughter of the Himālaya,
give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥22॥
argala.23: O Supreme Sovereign, worshipped in sincere devotion by Indra, husband of Indrāṇī,
give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥23॥
argala.24: O Devī, O Ambikā, who give your devotees a boundless rising of bliss,
give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥24॥
argala.25: Give me a charming wife who follows the inclinations of my mind.
Give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥25॥
argala.26: O you who carry beings across the ocean of worldly existence so hard to cross, O daughter of the mountain,
give me beauty, give me victory, give me fame, and slay my enemies. ॥26॥
argala.27: Having recited this hymn, a person should then recite the great hymn;
by fully worshipping the Saptaśatī he obtains a boon that is hard to win. ॥27॥
argala.iti: Thus ends the Argalā Stotra in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa.
kilaka.viniyoga: Om. Of this mantra, the Śrī Kīlaka (the pin, or bolt, of a mantra), the seer is Śiva, the metre is anuṣṭubh,
the deity is Śrī Mahāsarasvatī; for the pleasure of Śrī Jagadambā
it is applied in recitation as a part of reading the Saptaśatī.
kilaka.1: Om. To him whose body is pure knowledge, whose divine eyes are the three Vedas,
who is the cause of attaining the highest good, to Śiva who bears the half-moon: salutation. ॥1॥
kilaka.2: One should know well all this, the kīlaka even of the mantras;
he too attains well-being who is constantly intent on recitation. ॥2॥
kilaka.3: All the rites, uccāṭana (making a person quit his place) and the rest, succeed
for those who praise the Devī with devotion through this collection of hymns. ॥3॥
kilaka.4: For him no mantra, no herb, nothing at all is needed;
even without recitation, all uccāṭana and the like will succeed. ॥4॥
kilaka.5: Taking to heart the people's fear that all the rites would succeed,
Hara bound this whole auspicious hymn in this way. ॥5॥
kilaka.6: And that hymn of Caṇḍikā he made secret.
Through merit one duly attains that binding. ॥6॥
kilaka.7: He too attains well-being in full; there is no doubt of it —
he who, with a collected mind, on the fourteenth or the eighth day of the dark fortnight, ॥7॥
kilaka.8: makes an offering to the Devī and receives it back from her; in no other way is she pleased.
With a bolt of such a form it has been bolted by Mahādeva. ॥8॥
kilaka.9: He who makes this Caṇḍī free of the bolt and recites it daily
is a siddha, a perfected one; he is a gaṇa, one of Śiva's attendants; and he surely becomes a gandharva. ॥9॥
kilaka.10: No sickness comes to him, and fear arises for him nowhere;
he does not fall into the power of untimely death, and at death he gains liberation. ॥10॥
kilaka.11: Knowing this, one should begin and then recite it; for one who does not do so perishes.
Therefore the wise begin this whole hymn only after knowing it. ॥11॥
kilaka.12: Whatever good fortune and the like is seen among women,
all that is by her grace; therefore this auspicious hymn should be recited. ॥12॥
kilaka.13: When this hymn is recited softly, prosperity comes in great measure,
and indeed in full; therefore it should certainly be undertaken. ॥13॥
kilaka.14: By her grace come sovereignty, good fortune and health,
the destruction of enemies and the supreme liberation; why then should people not praise her? ॥14॥
kilaka.15: The man who constantly remembers Caṇḍikā, even in his heart alone,
gains the desire dear to his heart, and the Devī dwells ever in his heart. ॥15॥
kilaka.16: First performing this removal of the bolt, made by Mahādeva,
and so making it free of the bolt, those of collected mind should recite it. ॥16॥
kilaka.iti: Thus ends the Kīlaka Stotra of Śrī Bhagavatī.
kavacha.viniyoga: Of this Śrī Caṇḍī Kavaca, the armour-hymn, the seer is Brahmā, the metre is anuṣṭubh,
the deity is Cāmuṇḍā, the seed is the Mothers named in the aṅganyāsa, the placing on the limbs,
the tattva, the essence, is the deities who bind the directions; it is applied in recitation for the pleasure of Śrī Jagadambā.
kavacha.1: Om. That which is supremely secret in the world and gives men protection in every way,
and which has not been told to anyone, tell that to me, O Grandsire. ॥1॥
kavacha.2: There is, O Brāhmaṇa, something most secret, which benefits all beings:
the holy kavaca, the armour, of the Devī; listen to it, O great sage. ॥2॥
kavacha.3: The first is named Śailaputrī, the second Brahmacāriṇī,
the third is named Candraghaṇṭā, and the fourth Kūṣmāṇḍā. ॥3॥
kavacha.4: The fifth is named Skandamātā, the sixth likewise Kātyāyanī,
the seventh Kālarātri, and the eighth is named Mahāgaurī. ॥4॥
kavacha.5: And the ninth is Siddhidātrī; these are proclaimed the nine Durgās.
These names were declared by the great Veda itself. ॥5॥
kavacha.6: Those who are being burnt by fire, who are caught among enemies in battle,
who are in rough and impassable places, and who, stricken with fear, have gone to the Devī for refuge — ॥6॥
kavacha.7: no misfortune whatever befalls them in the peril of battle,
and they do not see calamity that brings grief, sorrow and fear. ॥7॥
kavacha.8: For those who remember the Devī daily with devotion, prosperity grows.
O Queen of the gods, those who remember you, you protect; there is no doubt of it. ॥8॥
kavacha.9: Cāmuṇḍā is seated on a corpse, Vārāhī rides a buffalo,
Aindrī is mounted on an elephant, Vaiṣṇavī is seated on Garuḍa. ॥9॥
kavacha.10: Nārasiṃhī is of great valour, Śivadūtī of great strength,
Māheśvarī rides a bull, Kaumārī has the peacock for her mount. ॥10॥
kavacha.11: The goddess Lakṣmī is seated on a lotus, holds a lotus in her hand and is the beloved of Hari;
the goddess Īśvarī, who bears a white form, has a bull for her mount. ॥11॥
kavacha.12: Brāhmī rides a swan and is adorned with every ornament.
Thus all these Mothers are endowed with every power of yoga. ॥12॥
kavacha.13: All of them are rich in the beauty of many ornaments and shine with many kinds of gems,
all with fine pearls hanging in divine necklaces, ॥13॥
kavacha.14: with indranīla and mahānīla sapphires and splendid rubies;
these goddesses are seen mounted on chariots, filled with wrath. ॥14॥
kavacha.15: Conch, discus, mace, spear, plough and the weapon called the pestle,
kavacha.16: the weapon called the lance, the trident, and the excellent weapon, the Śārṅga bow —
for destroying the bodies of the demons and for making the devotees fearless, ॥16॥
kavacha.17: these weapons they bear in this way, and indeed for the good of the gods too.
Salutation to you, O greatly fierce one, whose valour is greatly terrible. ॥17॥
kavacha.18: O you of great strength, of great energy, destroyer of great fear,
protect me, O Devī, hard to look upon, who increase the fear of enemies. ॥18॥
kavacha.19: May Aindrī protect me in the east, the Fire-deity in the south-east;
may Vārāhī guard me in the south, the bearer of the sword in the south-west. ॥19॥
kavacha.20: May Vāruṇī protect me in the west, she who rides the deer in the north-west;
may Kauberī guard me in the north, the bearer of the trident in the north-east. ॥20॥
kavacha.21: May Brahmāṇī protect me above, and Vaiṣṇavī likewise below;
thus may Cāmuṇḍā, whose mount is a corpse, protect me in the ten directions. ॥21॥
kavacha.22: May Jayā guard me in front, may Vijayā guard me behind,
Ajitā on the left side, and Aparājitā on the right. ॥22॥
kavacha.23: May Dyotinī protect my topknot, and Umā, stationed on the crown of my head,
Mālādharī on the forehead, and may Yaśasvinī protect my eyebrows. ॥23॥
kavacha.24: May Citranetrā guard my eyes, and Yamaghaṇṭā my side;
Trinetrā with her trident, and Caṇḍikā the place between my eyebrows. ॥24॥
kavacha.25: Śaṅkhinī between my eyes, Dvāravāsinī in my ears;
may Kālikā protect my cheeks, and Śaṅkarī the roots of my ears. ॥25॥
kavacha.26: May Sugandhā protect the nose, and Carcikā the upper lip;
may Amṛtābālā protect the lower lip, and Sarasvatī the tongue. ॥26॥
kavacha.27: May Kaumārī protect the teeth, and Caṇḍikā the region of the throat;
may Citraghaṇṭā protect the uvula, and Mahāmāyā the palate. ॥27॥
kavacha.28: May Kāmākṣī protect the chin, and Sarvamaṅgalā my speech;
may Bhadrakālī protect the neck, and Dhanurdharī the spine. ॥28॥
kavacha.29: May Nīlagrīvā protect the outer throat, and Nalakūbarī the windpipe;
may Khaḍginī protect the two shoulders, and Vajradhāriṇī my two arms. ॥29॥
kavacha.30: May Daṇḍinī protect the two hands, and Ambikā the fingers;
may Śūleśvarī protect the nails, and Nareśvarī the belly. ॥30॥
kavacha.31: May Mahādevī protect the breasts, and Śokavināśinī the mind;
may the Devī Lalitā protect the heart, and Śūladhāriṇī the abdomen. ॥31॥
kavacha.32: May Kāminī protect the navel, and likewise Guhyeśvarī the private parts;
may Durgandhā protect the generative organ, and Guhyavāhinī my anus. ॥32॥
kavacha.33: May Bhagavatī protect the waist, and Meghavāhanā my thighs;
may Mahābalā protect the shanks, and Mādhavanāyikā the knees. ॥33॥
kavacha.34: May Nārasiṃhī protect the ankles, and Kauśikī the tops of the feet;
may Śrīdharī protect the toes, and Pātālavāsinī the sole. ॥34॥
kavacha.35: May Daṃṣṭrakarālī protect the nails, and Ūrdhvakeśinī the hair;
may Kaumārī protect the pores of the skin, and likewise Yogīśvarī the skin. ॥35॥
kavacha.36: May Pārvatī protect the blood, marrow, fat, flesh, bones and fatty tissue;
may Kālarātri protect the intestines, and Mukuṭeśvarī the bile. ॥36॥
kavacha.37: May Padmāvatī protect the lotus-calyx (the heart-lotus), and likewise Cūḍāmaṇi the phlegm;
may Jvālāmukhī protect the lustre of the nails, and Abhedyā all the joints. ॥37॥
kavacha.38: May Brahmāṇī protect my semen, and likewise Chatreśvarī my shadow;
may Dharmadhāriṇī protect my ego, mind and intellect. ॥38॥
kavacha.39: My vital airs prāṇa and apāna, and likewise vyāna, udāna and samāna,
may Vajrahastā protect; and may Kalyāṇaśobhanā protect my life-breaths. ॥39॥
kavacha.40: May Yoginī protect me in taste, form, smell, sound and touch;
may Nārāyaṇī always protect sattva, rajas and tamas, the three guṇas, the qualities of nature. ॥40॥
kavacha.41: May Vārāhī protect my span of life, and Pārvatī my dharma, my right conduct;
may Vaiṣṇavī always protect my renown, my fame and my prosperity. ॥41॥
kavacha.42: May Indrāṇī protect my lineage, and Caṇḍikā my cattle;
may Mahālakṣmī protect my sons, and Bhairavī my wife. ॥42॥
kavacha.43: May Dhaneśvarī protect my wealth, and likewise Kaumārī my daughter;
may Supathā protect the path, and likewise Kṣemaṅkarī the road. ॥43॥
kavacha.44: At the king's gate may Mahālakṣmī protect me, and Vijayā, who is ever present.
And whatever place is left without protection, not covered by the kavaca, this armour of prayer — ॥44॥
kavacha.45: — protect all that for me, O Devī Jayantī, destroyer of sin.
One should always recite this holy kavaca, which gives protection of every kind. ॥45॥
kavacha.46: O brahmin sage, because of your devotion I have told you this secret.
One should not take a single step without the kavaca if one wishes for one's own good. ॥46॥
kavacha.47: Wherever a man goes who is always covered by the kavaca,
there he gains wealth, and victory at all times. ॥47॥
kavacha.48: Whatever desire he thinks of, that he surely obtains;
such a man will attain supreme, unequalled sovereignty on earth. ॥48॥
kavacha.49: That mortal becomes fearless and unconquered in battles;
the man covered by the kavaca becomes worthy of worship in the three worlds. ॥49॥
kavacha.50: This kavaca of the Devī is hard to obtain even for the gods.
Whoever recites it every day at the three junctions of the day, self-controlled and pure, and full of faith — ॥50॥
kavacha.51: — a divine portion comes to him, and he is unconquered in the three worlds;
he lives a hundred years and more, free from untimely death. ॥51॥
kavacha.52: All diseases perish, skin sores from spider poison, boils and the like;
and whatever poison there is, from things that do not move, from moving creatures, or made by art, perishes too. ॥52॥
kavacha.53: All malevolent rites, the mantras and yantras on earth;
those that move on the earth and those that move in the sky, those born in the family and those got by instruction — ॥53॥
kavacha.54: afflictions inborn and hereditary, mālā, ḍākinī and śākinī as well,
and the terrible ḍākinīs who move in the mid-air with a mighty roar — ॥54॥
kavacha.55: grahas, the seizing spirits, bhūtas and piśācas, yakṣas, gandharvas and rākṣasas,
brahmarākṣasas and vetālas, kūṣmāṇḍas, bhairavas and the like — ॥55॥
kavacha.56: — all these perish at the very sight of one who is covered by the kavaca.
His honour rises with the king, and his splendour grows to the highest. ॥56॥
kavacha.57: Such men grow in renown, and their fame increases.
Therefore, O sage, a devotee should always recite the kavaca, which grants desires. ॥57॥
kavacha.58: Having first recited the kavaca, one should recite the Caṇḍī Saptaśatī;
the accomplishment born of reciting the Caṇḍī comes without obstacle. ॥58॥
kavacha.59: As long as the sphere of the earth endures, with its mountains, woods and forests,
so long does his line of sons and grandsons remain on the earth. ॥59॥
kavacha.60: At the end of the body, the supreme abode, very hard to reach even for the gods,
that eternal abode the man attains by the grace of Mahāmāyā. ॥60॥
kavacha.61: He goes there, and having gone, he does not come back again.
He gains the supreme abode and attains equality with Śiva. ॥61॥
kavacha.iti: Thus ends the Devī Kavaca in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, composed by Hari, Hara and Brahmā.
1.viniyoga: Of this sacred First Episode (Prathama Caritra), the seer is Brahmā;
the deity is Mahākālī; the metre is gāyatrī; the power (śakti) is Nandā;
the seed (bīja) is Raktadantikā; the element (tattva) is fire;
and its essential form is the Ṛgveda. For the pleasure of Śrī Mahākālī,
its application is in the recitation of the First Episode.
1.dhyana: Om. Holding in her hands a sword, a discus, a mace, arrows, a bow, an iron club, a trident, a bhuśuṇḍī (a kind of weapon), a severed head
and a conch, three-eyed, adorned with ornaments on every limb,
with the lustre of a sapphire, with ten faces and ten feet: I worship Mahākālikā,
whom the lotus-born Brahmā praised, when Hari had fallen asleep, so that Madhu and Kaiṭabha might be slain.
1.2: Sāvarṇi, son of the Sun, who is called the eighth Manu:
hear of his birth from me as I tell it in full, ॥2॥
1.3: and how, by the power of Mahāmāyā, he became the lord of a manvantara, the age of a Manu,
that illustrious Sāvarṇi, son of the Sun. ॥3॥
1.4: Long ago, in the Svārociṣa manvantara, a king born of the line of Caitra,
named Suratha, ruled over the whole circle of the earth. ॥4॥
1.5: While he was rightly protecting his subjects as if they were his own sons,
the Kolāvidhvaṃsin kings then became his enemies. ॥5॥
1.6: A war broke out between them and him, the bearer of a very mighty sceptre;
and in that war he was defeated by those Kolāvidhvaṃsins, though they were weaker. ॥6॥
1.7: Then he came back to his own city and became ruler of his own country alone.
Then that illustrious one was attacked by those powerful enemies. ॥7॥
1.8: From him, now weakened, his powerful, wicked and evil-minded ministers
seized his treasury and his army, then, there in his own city too. ॥8॥
1.9: Then, under the pretext of hunting, that king, robbed of his sovereignty,
mounted a horse alone and went into a dense forest. ॥9॥
1.10: There he saw the hermitage of Medhas, best of the twice-born,
full of wild beasts grown peaceful and adorned by the sage's disciples. ॥10॥
1.11: Honoured by that sage, he stayed there for some time,
wandering here and there in that hermitage of the excellent sage. ॥11॥
1.12: Then, there, his mind drawn by the sense of possession, he thought:
That city which my forefathers protected of old is now bereft of me. ॥12॥
1.13: Whether those servants of mine, men of evil conduct, protect it righteously or not,
I do not know. That chief elephant of mine, valiant and always in rut, ॥13॥
1.14: having passed into the power of my enemies, what comforts will he get?
Those who always followed me for my favour, wealth and food ॥14॥
1.15: surely now attend on other kings.
By those men given to spending wrongly, who keep on spending without end, ॥15॥
1.16: that treasury, gathered with great hardship, will be wasted away.
These and other things the king kept thinking over constantly. ॥16॥
1.17: There, near the brahmin's hermitage, he saw a merchant.
The king asked him: Friend, who are you? And what is the reason for your coming here? ॥17॥
1.18: Why do you appear as if grief-stricken, as if downcast?
Having heard these words of the king, spoken with affection, ॥18॥
1.19: the merchant, bowed down with humility, answered the king. ॥19॥
1.21: I am a merchant named Samādhi, born in a family of the wealthy. ॥21॥
1.22: Out of greed for wealth, my wicked sons and wife have driven me out;
they have taken my wealth, and I am left without wealth, wife and sons. ॥22॥
1.23: Grieving, and cast out by my trusted kinsmen, I have come to the forest.
Such as I am, I do not know whether the news of my sons is good or ill, ॥23॥
1.24: nor, staying here, the news of my kinsmen and my wife.
Is it well with them at home now, or is it ill? ॥24॥
1.25: How are they? Are my sons of good conduct, or are they of bad conduct? ॥25॥
1.27: Those greedy ones, sons, wife and the rest, who drove you out for the sake of wealth: ॥27॥
1.28: why does your mind bind itself to them in affection? ॥28॥
1.30: It is just as you have said, these words about me. ॥30॥
1.31: What am I to do? My mind will not turn hard towards those
who, greedy for wealth, gave up love for their father and cast me out, ॥31॥
1.32: and gave up love for husband and kinsmen; towards them alone my mind is loving.
Though I know, I cannot grasp what this is, O wise one: ॥32॥
1.33: that my mind leans in love even towards kinsmen without merit.
For their sake sighs and dejection arise in me. ॥33॥
1.34: What am I to do, since my mind does not grow hard towards those who have no love? ॥34॥
1.36: Then, O brahmin, the two together went up to that sage. ॥36॥
1.37: That merchant named Samādhi and that best of kings,
having exchanged courtesies with him as custom required and as he deserved, ॥37॥
1.38: sat down, and the merchant and the king talked of certain things. ॥38॥
1.40: O revered one, I wish to ask you one thing; tell me that. ॥40॥
1.41: That which, though my own mind has no control over it, brings distress to my mind:
the attachment that I, who have lost my kingdom, have even to all the parts of the kingdom, ॥41॥
1.42: this I have though I know, just as an ignorant man would. What is this, O best of sages?
And this merchant has been humiliated by his sons, his wife and his servants, and cast off as well, ॥42॥
1.43: and forsaken by his own people; yet he feels deep affection for them.
Thus he, and I as well, are both deeply distressed. ॥43॥
1.44: Our minds are drawn by attachment even to objects whose faults we have seen.
So what is this, O fortunate one, that delusion takes hold even of the two of us, who have knowledge? ॥44॥
1.45: And this bewilderment arises in me and in him, each blind in discernment. ॥45॥
1.47: Every creature has knowledge within the range of the objects of the senses. ॥47॥
1.48: And the objects, O fortunate one, come in this way to each separately:
some creatures are blind by day, and others likewise blind at night. ॥48॥
1.49: Some creatures see equally by day and by night.
Humans have knowledge, it is true; but they are certainly not the only ones, ॥49॥
1.50: for cattle, birds, wild beasts and the like all have knowledge;
and the knowledge of humans is that which those beasts and birds have. ॥50॥
1.51: And what belongs to humans belongs to them as well, and the rest too is alike in both.
Though they have knowledge, look at these birds: into the beaks of their young ॥51॥
1.52: out of delusion they are intent on dropping grain, though they themselves are tormented by hunger.
Humans, O tiger among men, look with longing to their sons ॥52॥
1.53: out of greed, for a return of the favour; do you not see them?
Even so, they are cast down into the pit of delusion, with its whirlpool of attachment, ॥53॥
1.54: by the power of Mahāmāyā, the great illusion, a power that keeps worldly existence in being.
So no wonder should be felt at this: she is the Yoganidrā, the yogic sleep, of the Lord of the world, ॥54॥
1.55: and she is the Mahāmāyā of Hari; by her the world is deluded.
For that Devī, the Bhagavatī, the minds even of the wise ॥55॥
1.56: she, Mahāmāyā, draws away by force and hands over to delusion.
By her this entire world, moving and unmoving, is brought forth. ॥56॥
1.57: When she is gracious, it is she who becomes the giver of boons to men for their liberation.
She is the supreme knowledge, the cause of liberation, eternal; ॥57॥
1.58: and she herself is the cause of bondage to worldly existence; she is the sovereign over all lords. ॥58॥
1.60: O revered one, who is that Devī whom you call Mahāmāyā? ॥60॥
1.61: How did she come into being, and what is her work, O twice-born?
And whatever power that Devī has, whatever her nature and whatever her origin, ॥61॥
1.62: all that I wish to hear from you, O best of the knowers of brahman, the supreme reality. ॥62॥
1.64: She is eternal indeed; the world is her form; by her all this is pervaded. ॥64॥
1.65: Even so, hear from me how she comes forth in many ways.
When she appears to accomplish the work of the gods, ॥65॥
1.66: then, though eternal, she is said in the world to have been born.
When the world had become one single ocean, and Viṣṇu, the blessed Lord and master, ॥66॥
1.67: spread out Śeṣa as his bed and took to yogic sleep at the end of the kalpa, the cosmic age,
then two terrible asuras, the renowned Madhu and Kaiṭabha, ॥67॥
1.68: sprung from the wax of Viṣṇu's ears, rose up to kill Brahmā.
Brahmā, the lord of creatures, seated on the lotus of Viṣṇu's navel, ॥68॥
1.69: seeing those two fierce asuras and Janārdana fast asleep,
and steady with a single-pointed heart, praised that Yoganidrā ॥69॥
1.70: to awaken Hari — her who had made her abode in Hari's eyes,
the sovereign of the universe, the sustainer of the world, who brings about its preservation and dissolution, ॥70॥
1.71: the Bhagavatī Nidrā, the incomparable Sleep of Viṣṇu: Brahmā, the lord of radiance, praised her. ॥71॥
1.73: You are Svāhā, you are Svadhā, you indeed are the call vaṣaṭ; svara, the sacred tone of recitation, is your very self. ॥73॥
1.74: You are sudhā, the nectar of immortality; in the eternal syllable Om you abide threefold, as its measures;
and you abide as the eternal half-measure, which cannot be uttered distinctly. ॥74॥
1.75: You alone are Sandhyā and Sāvitrī; you, O Devī, are the supreme mother.
By you this universe is upheld; by you this world is created. ॥75॥
1.76: By you, O Devī, it is protected, and you always devour it at the end.
At its creation you are the form of creation, and in its protection the form of preservation; ॥76॥
1.77: and likewise, at the end of this world, the form of its dissolution, O you whose being is the world.
You are the great knowledge, the great illusion, the great intellect, the great memory, ॥77॥
1.78: and you are the great delusion, the great Devī, the great sovereign.
And you are prakṛti, the primal nature of all, who brings forth the three guṇas, the strands of nature. ॥78॥
1.79: You are Kālarātri, the night of dissolution; Mahārātri, the great night; and the dreadful Moharātri, the night of delusion.
You are Śrī, you are the sovereign, you are Hrī, modesty; you are understanding, whose mark is awareness. ॥79॥
1.80: You are bashfulness, nourishment and likewise contentment; you are peace, and forbearance too.
You bear the sword and the trident, you are terrible, you bear the mace and likewise the discus, ॥80॥
1.81: the conch and the bow; arrows, the bhuśuṇḍī and the iron club are your weapons.
You are gentle, gentler still, and far more beautiful than everything that is gentle. ॥81॥
1.82: Of all things higher and lower, you alone are the highest; you are the supreme sovereign.
And whatever thing there is anywhere, whether real or unreal, O you who are the self of all, ॥82॥
1.83: the power of all of it is you: what praise of you can I offer?
You, by whom even he who creates the world, protects the world and devours the world ॥83॥
1.84: has been brought under the sway of sleep: who here is able to praise you?
Since Viṣṇu, I and Īśāna (Śiva) as well ॥84॥
1.85: have been made by you to take on bodies, who then could have the power to praise you?
You, O Devī, thus praised for your own exalted powers, ॥85॥
1.86: delude these two unassailable asuras, Madhu and Kaiṭabha,
and let Acyuta, the lord of the world, be quickly brought to wakefulness, ॥86॥
1.87: and let awareness be roused in him to slay these two great asuras. ॥87॥
1.89: Thus praised there and then by Brahmā the Creator, the Devī Tāmasī, ॥89॥
1.90: to awaken Viṣṇu so that he might slay Madhu and Kaiṭabha,
from his eyes, mouth, nose, arms and heart, and likewise from his chest, ॥90॥
1.91: came forth and stood before the eyes of Brahmā, whose birth is unmanifest.
And released by her, Janārdana, the lord of the world, rose up ॥91॥
1.92: from his serpent-bed on the one ocean; and then he saw those two,
Madhu and Kaiṭabha, evil-minded, of surpassing strength and valour, ॥92॥
1.93: their eyes red with anger, set on devouring Brahmā.
Then, rising up, the Lord Hari fought with the two ॥93॥
1.94: for five thousand years, the all-pervading Lord with his arms as his weapons.
And the two, maddened by their surpassing strength and deluded by Mahāmāyā, ॥94॥
1.95: said to Keśava: Choose a boon from us. ॥95॥
1.97: If you two are now pleased with me, then both of you must be slain by me. ॥97॥
1.98: What use is any other boon here? For this much alone is what I have chosen. ॥98॥
1.100: Thus deceived, the two then saw that the whole world was made of water; ॥100॥
1.101: seeing this, they said to the lotus-eyed Lord:
Slay us where the earth is not flooded with water. ॥101॥
1.103: Saying, So be it, the Lord, the bearer of the conch, discus and mace,
placed them on his thigh and with his discus cut off the heads of the two. ॥103॥
1.104: Thus, praised by Brahmā, she herself came forth.
Now hear once more of the power of this Devī; I shall tell you. Aiṃ Om. ॥104॥
1.iti: Svasti, may it be well. Thus ends the first chapter, named the Slaying of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, of the Devī Māhātmya in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, the age of the Manu Sāvarṇi. ॥1॥
2.viniyoga: Of this sacred Middle Episode (Madhyama Caritra), the seer is Viṣṇu;
the metre is uṣṇik; the power (śakti) is Śākambharī; the seed (bīja) is Durgā;
and its essential form is the Yajurveda. For the pleasure of Śrī Mahālakṣmī,
its application is in the recitation of the Middle Episode.
2.dhyana: Om. Holding in her hands a rosary and an axe, a mace, an arrow and a thunderbolt, a lotus, a bow, a water-pot,
a staff, a spear, a sword and a shield, a conch, a bell, a wine-cup,
a trident, a noose and the Sudarśana discus, with the lustre of coral:
I worship here Mahālakṣmī, crusher of the buffalo Mahiṣa, seated on a lotus.
2.2: Long ago there was a war between the gods and the asuras for a full hundred years,
when Mahiṣa was the lord of the asuras and Purandara (Indra) the lord of the gods. ॥2॥
2.3: There the army of the gods was defeated by the asuras of great valour,
and having conquered all the gods, Mahiṣāsura became Indra. ॥3॥
2.4: Then the defeated gods, with the lotus-born Brahmā, the lord of creatures,
at their head, went to where Śiva and Viṣṇu, whose banner bears Garuḍa, were. ॥4॥
2.5: Just as it had happened, the doings of Mahiṣāsura were told to those two
by the gods, the full account of how the gods had been overcome. ॥5॥
2.6: The gods said: Of Sūrya, Indra, Agni, Vāyu and Candra, of Yama and of Varuṇa,
and of the others too, he himself now occupies the offices. ॥6॥
2.7: All the hosts of the gods, driven out of heaven by him,
the evil-minded Mahiṣa, wander on the earth like mortals. ॥7॥
2.8: All this we have told you, the doings of the enemy of the immortals.
We have come to you for refuge; let thought be given to slaying him. ॥8॥
2.9: Hearing such words from the gods, Madhusūdana, the slayer of Madhu,
and Śambhu (Śiva) grew angry, both their faces twisted with frowning brows. ॥9॥
2.10: Then from the face of Viṣṇu, the bearer of the discus, filled with great anger,
there came forth a great radiance, and from Brahmā and Śaṅkara as well. ॥10॥
2.11: And from the bodies of the other gods too, Indra and the rest,
a very great radiance came forth, and it all merged into one. ॥11॥
2.12: A mass of exceeding radiance, like a mountain ablaze,
the gods saw there, its flames filling all the quarters of the sky. ॥12॥
2.13: That matchless radiance there, born from the bodies of all the gods,
gathered into one and became a woman, pervading the three worlds with her lustre. ॥13॥
2.14: The radiance that was Śiva's gave birth to her face;
from Yama's came her hair, and from the radiance of Viṣṇu her arms. ॥14॥
2.15: From the Moon's radiance came the pair of breasts, and from Indra's the waist;
from Varuṇa's the shanks and thighs, and the hips from the radiance of the Earth. ॥15॥
2.16: From Brahmā's radiance came the feet, and their toes from the Sun's radiance;
from that of the Vasus the fingers, and from Kubera's the nose. ॥16॥
2.17: Her teeth arose from the radiance of Prajāpati,
and likewise her three eyes were born from the radiance of Agni. ॥17॥
2.18: Her two brows were the radiance of the two twilights, and her ears that of the Wind;
and from the radiances of the other gods too the auspicious Śivā came into being. ॥18॥
2.19: Then, seeing her who had arisen from the mass of radiance of all the gods,
the immortals, oppressed by Mahiṣa, were filled with joy.
And then the gods gave her their own weapons, each his own. ॥19॥
2.20: Śiva, who bears the Pināka bow, drew a trident out of his own trident and gave it to her;
and Kṛṣṇa (Viṣṇu) drew a discus from his own discus and gave it. ॥20॥
2.21: Varuṇa gave her a conch, and Agni a spear;
Māruta, the Wind, gave a bow, and likewise two quivers full of arrows. ॥21॥
2.22: Indra, lord of the immortals, drew a thunderbolt out of his own thunderbolt,
and the thousand-eyed god gave it to her, with a bell taken from the elephant Airāvata. ॥22॥
2.23: Yama gave a staff from his staff of death, and the lord of the waters, Varuṇa, a noose;
Prajāpati gave a rosary, and Brahmā a water-pot. ॥23॥
2.24: The Sun filled all the pores of her skin with his own rays,
and Kāla, Time, gave her a sword and a spotless shield. ॥24॥
2.25: The Ocean of Milk gave a spotless necklace and a pair of garments that never wear out,
and a divine crest-jewel, a pair of earrings and bracelets; ॥25॥
2.26: a bright crescent-moon ornament as well, armlets on all her arms,
a pair of shining anklets likewise, a peerless necklet, ॥26॥
2.27: and jewelled rings on all her fingers.
Viśvakarmā gave her an exceedingly bright axe, ॥27॥
2.28: missiles of many forms, and impenetrable armour too.
A garland of unfading lotuses for her head, and another for her breast, ॥28॥
2.29: the Ocean gave her, and a most beautiful lotus as well.
Himavān gave a lion to be her mount, and jewels of many kinds. ॥29॥
2.30: Kubera, the lord of wealth, gave a drinking cup never empty of wine.
And Śeṣa, lord of all serpents, gave her, adorned with great gems, ॥30॥
2.31: a necklace of serpents; it is he who bears this earth.
By the other gods too, with ornaments and weapons likewise, the Devī, ॥31॥
2.32: being so honoured, roared aloud again and again, with peals of laughter.
With her terrible roar the whole sky was filled. ॥32॥
2.33: From that boundless, exceedingly great roar a mighty echo arose.
All the worlds were shaken, and the oceans trembled. ॥33॥
2.34: The earth quaked, and all the mountains shook.
And the gods in their joy said to her, the rider of the lion: Victory to you! ॥34॥
2.35: And the sages, their bodies bowed in devotion, praised her.
Seeing all the three worlds in turmoil, the enemies of the immortals, ॥35॥
2.36: with all their armies armed and ready, rose up with weapons raised.
Mahiṣāsura cried out in anger: Ah! What is this? ॥36॥
2.37: Surrounded by all the asuras, he rushed towards that sound.
Then he saw the Devī, who filled the three worlds with her radiance, ॥37॥
2.38: under the tread of whose feet the earth was bowed down, whose crown grazed the sky,
who shook all the netherworlds with the twang of her bowstring, ॥38॥
2.39: and who stood with her thousand arms spread over the directions all around.
Then began the battle of the enemies of the gods with that Devī, ॥39॥
2.40: a battle in which the spaces between the quarters blazed with weapons and missiles hurled in many ways.
Mahiṣāsura's general, the great asura named Cikṣura, ॥40॥
2.41: fought; and Cāmara too, with others, accompanied by an army of all four divisions.
The great asura named Udagra, with sixty thousand chariots, ॥41॥
2.42: fought; and Mahāhanu with an army of a crore (ten million),
and the great asura Asiloman with five crore; ॥42॥
2.43: and Bāṣkala fought in the battle with an army of sixty lakh (six million).
Parivārita, with many hosts of thousands of elephants and horses ॥43॥
2.44: and a crore of chariots around him, fought in that battle.
And the asura named Biḍāla, with five hundred crore ॥44॥
2.45: chariots around him, fought there in the conflict.
And others there, by tens of thousands, surrounded by chariots, elephants and horses, ॥45॥
2.46: great asuras, fought with the Devī there in the conflict.
And with thousands of crores upon crores of chariots, of elephants likewise, ॥46॥
2.47: and of horses around him, Mahiṣāsura was there in the battle.
With javelins and bhindipālas, short darts hurled by hand, with spears and pestles likewise, ॥47॥
2.48: with swords, axes and paṭṭiśas, edged spears, they fought the Devī in the conflict.
Some hurled spears, and others nooses. ॥48॥
2.49: With blows of their swords they set about killing the Devī.
Then the Devī Caṇḍikā, in her turn, those weapons and missiles ॥49॥
2.50: cut to pieces in mere play, raining down her own weapons and missiles.
Her face showing no strain, praised by the gods and seers, the Devī, ॥50॥
