2.51: the Sovereign One, hurled weapons and missiles into the bodies of the asuras as well.
And the Devī's mount, the lion, enraged too, shaking its mane, ॥51॥
2.52: ranged through the asura armies like a fire through forests.
And the breaths that Ambikā breathed out as she fought in the battle, ॥52॥
2.53: those very breaths at once became gaṇas, troops of attendants, by hundreds of thousands.
They fought with axes, bhindipālas, swords and paṭṭiśas, ॥53॥
2.54: Strengthened by the Devī's power, they went on destroying the hosts of asuras.
The attendants sounded drums, and others likewise conches, ॥54॥
2.55: and others likewise played mṛdaṅgas in that great festival of battle.
Then the Devī, with her trident, her mace and showers of spears, ॥55॥
2.56: and with swords and other weapons, slew great asuras by hundreds;
and she felled others as well, who were stupefied by the sound of the bell. ॥56॥
2.57: And she bound other asuras with her noose and dragged them over the ground.
Some were cut in two by sharp strokes of the sword, and others likewise, ॥57॥
2.58: crushed by the downward blow of the mace, lie on the ground.
And some, struck hard by the pestle, vomited blood. ॥58॥
2.59: Some fell to the ground, pierced in the chest by the trident.
Some on the battlefield were riddled through by a flood of arrows, ॥59॥
2.60: and, swooping like hawks, those tormentors of the gods gave up their lives.
The arms of some were cut off, and others likewise had their necks severed. ॥60॥
2.61: The heads of others fell; others were split through the middle;
and still other great asuras, their legs cut off, fell to the earth. ॥61॥
2.62: Some, split in two by the Devī, were left with one arm, one eye and one foot.
And others, even with their heads cut off, fell and rose up again. ॥62॥
2.63: Headless trunks, grasping their finest weapons, fought with the Devī;
and others there in the battle danced to the rhythm of the instruments. ॥63॥
2.64: Headless trunks whose heads had been cut off, with sword, spear and pike in hand,
other great asuras kept crying to the Devī: Stop! Stop! ॥64॥
2.65: With the chariots, elephants and horses that had been felled, and with the asuras, the earth
became impassable there, where that great battle took place. ॥65॥
2.66: There at once great rivers, floods of blood, flowed forth
in the midst of the asura army, the blood of elephants, asuras and horses. ॥66॥
2.67: In a moment Ambikā brought that vast army of the asuras
to destruction, just as fire destroys a great heap of grass and wood. ॥67॥
2.68: And that lion, letting out a mighty roar and shaking its mane,
seemed to be searching out the life-breaths from the bodies of the enemies of the gods. ॥68॥
2.69: There the Devī and those attendants fought such a battle with the asuras
that the gods in heaven, showering flowers, were delighted with them. ॥69॥
2.iti: Svasti, may it be well. Thus ends the second chapter, named the Slaying of Mahiṣāsura's Army, of the Devī Māhātmya in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, the age of the Manu Sāvarṇi. ॥2॥
3.dhyana: Om. She whose radiance is that of a thousand rising suns, who wears red silk and a garland of heads,
whose breasts are smeared with blood, who holds a rosary, knowledge (the book), the gesture of fearlessness and the gesture of granting boons
in her lotus hands, whose lotus face is lovely, shining with three eyes,
the Devī whose crown is set with the moon and jewels and who is seated on a lotus: to her I bow.
3.2: Seeing that army being slaughtered, the great asura
Cikṣura, the commander, then went in anger to fight Ambikā. ॥2॥
3.3: In the battle that asura rained a shower of arrows on the Devī,
as a cloud rains a shower of water on the peak of Mount Meru. ॥3॥
3.4: Then the Devī, cutting down his masses of arrows in mere play,
slew his horses with arrows, and the driver of the horses as well. ॥4॥
3.5: And at once she cut down his bow and his very lofty banner,
and with swift arrows pierced him in the limbs, his bow now cut. ॥5॥
3.6: With his bow cut, without a chariot, his horses slain and his charioteer slain,
that asura rushed at the Devī, bearing sword and shield. ॥6॥
3.7: Striking the lion's head with his sharp-edged sword,
he, very swift, struck the Devī too on her left arm. ॥7॥
3.8: On reaching her arm, the sword shattered, O prince.
Then he, his eyes red with anger, seized a trident. ॥8॥
3.9: And then the great asura hurled it at Bhadrakālī,
blazing with radiance like the disc of the sun coming from the sky. ॥9॥
3.10: Seeing that trident flying at her, the Devī released a trident of her own;
by it that trident was broken into a hundred pieces, and so was the great asura. ॥10॥
3.11: When that mighty commander of Mahiṣa's army was slain,
Cāmara, tormentor of the gods, came mounted on an elephant. ॥11॥
3.12: He too then hurled a spear at the Devī; and Ambikā swiftly
struck it with a cry of huṃ and brought it down to the ground, lustreless. ॥12॥
3.13: Cāmara, enraged at the sight of the spear fallen and broken,
hurled a trident; that too she cut down with arrows. ॥13॥
3.14: Then the lion leapt up and, settling between the elephant's frontal globes,
fought fiercely, hand to hand, with that enemy of the gods. ॥14॥
3.15: Then the two, fighting, came down from that elephant to the ground,
and fought on, greatly enraged, with most terrible blows. ॥15॥
3.16: Then, springing swiftly into the sky and swooping down, the lion
struck off Cāmara's head with a blow of its paw. ॥16॥
3.17: And Udagra was slain in battle by the Devī with stones, trees and the like,
and Karāla too was struck down with teeth, fists and open palms. ॥17॥
3.18: The Devī, enraged, crushed Uddhata with blows of her mace,
and slew Bāṣkala with a bhindipāla, and Tāmra and Andhaka with arrows. ॥18॥
3.19: Ugrāsya and Ugravīrya, and likewise Mahāhanu,
the three-eyed Supreme Devī slew with her trident. ॥19॥
3.20: She sent Biḍāla's head falling from his body with her sword,
and with arrows sent both Durdhara and Durmukha to the abode of Yama. ॥20॥
3.21: As his own army was thus being destroyed, Mahiṣāsura
terrified those attendants with his own buffalo form. ॥21॥
3.22: Some by blows of his muzzle, others likewise by the stamping of his hooves,
and others, lashed by his tail and torn apart by his two horns, ॥22॥
3.23: Some others, by his charge, by his bellowing and by his whirling,
and others by the blast of his breath, he felled to the ground. ॥23॥
3.24: Having felled the host of her attendants, the pramathas, that asura rushed forward
to kill the lion of the Great Devī. Then Ambikā grew angry. ॥24॥
3.25: He too, of great might, in his anger pounding the face of the earth with his hooves,
hurled lofty mountains with his two horns, and bellowed. ॥25॥
3.26: Crushed by his swift circling, the earth was shattered;
and the ocean, lashed by his tail, flooded everything around. ॥26॥
3.27: Torn apart by his tossing horns, the clouds went to pieces;
and mountains, flung up by the wind of his breath, fell from the sky by hundreds. ॥27॥
3.28: Seeing the great asura thus swollen with rage and rushing at her,
Caṇḍikā then grew wrathful, to slay him. ॥28॥
3.29: She cast her noose over him and bound that great asura.
And he, bound in the great battle, gave up his buffalo form. ॥29॥
3.30: Then at once he became a lion. Just as Ambikā was cutting off his head,
at that very moment a man appeared with a sword in his hand. ॥30॥
3.31: Then at once the Devī cut down that man with her arrows,
together with his sword and shield. Then he became a great elephant. ॥31॥
3.32: With his trunk he dragged at that great lion, and trumpeted;
but as he was dragging, the Devī cut off his trunk with her sword. ॥32॥
3.33: Then the great asura took on his buffalo body once more,
and just as before threw the three worlds, with all that moves and does not move, into turmoil. ॥33॥
3.34: Then Caṇḍikā, the Mother of the world, enraged, drank the excellent drink;
she drank again and again, and laughed, her eyes turned red. ॥34॥
3.35: And the asura too roared, swollen with the pride of his strength and valour,
and with his two horns hurled mountains at Caṇḍikā. ॥35॥
3.36: And she, pulverising with showers of arrows those mountains hurled by him,
spoke to him in faltering syllables, through the flush that intoxication had raised on her face. ॥36॥
3.38: Roar, roar for a moment, fool, while I drink this madhu, the honeyed wine.
When you are slain by me right here, the gods will soon be roaring. ॥38॥
3.40: Having spoken thus, she sprang up and mounted that great asura,
and pressing down his throat with her foot, she struck him with her trident. ॥40॥
3.41: Then he, trodden underfoot by her, out of his own mouth
had come only half-way, held fast by the power of the Devī. ॥41॥
3.42: Only half emerged and still fighting, that great asura
was felled by the Devī, who cut off his head with her great sword. ॥42॥
3.43: Then that whole army of the daityas, crying out in dismay, perished;
and all the hosts of the gods attained the highest joy. ॥43॥
3.44: The gods, together with the celestial great sages, praised that Devī;
the lords of the gandharvas, the celestial musicians, sang, and the troupes of apsarases, the celestial dancers, danced. ॥44॥
3.iti: Svasti, may it be well. Thus ends the third chapter, named the Slaying of Mahiṣāsura, of the Devī Māhātmya in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, the age of the Manu Sāvarṇi. ॥3॥
4.dhyana: Om. Her whose lustre is like a dark cloud, who strikes fear into the ranks of her enemies with her side-glances, who has the crescent moon bound on her crown,
who holds in her hands a conch, a discus, a sword and a trident too, who has three eyes,
who is mounted on the shoulders of a lion, who fills all the three worlds with her radiance,
Durgā named Jayā, surrounded by the gods and served by those who seek siddhi, spiritual attainment: on her one should meditate.
4.2: that evil-souled one, and the army of the gods' foes had been slain by the Devī, the hosts of gods led by Indra,
their necks and shoulders bowed low in reverence, praised her
in words, their bodies made lovely by hair standing on end in their great joy. ॥2॥
4.3: The Devī who by her own power has pervaded this world,
whose form is the gathered powers of all the hosts of gods:
to that Ambikā, worthy of worship by all the gods and great sages,
we bow in devotion. May she bring about what is auspicious for us. ॥3॥
4.4: She whose incomparable power the blessed Ananta,
Brahmā and Hara cannot describe, nor her might:
may that Caṇḍikā set her mind on the protection of the whole world
and on the destruction of the fear of evil. ॥4॥
4.5: You who are yourself Śrī, good fortune, in the homes of the virtuous,
Alakṣmī, misfortune, in the homes of the sinful, understanding in the hearts of the wise,
faith in the good, and modesty in one born of a noble family:
to you we bow. Protect the universe, O Devī. ॥5॥
4.6: How shall we describe this inconceivable form of yours?
Or your great and surpassing valour that brought the asuras to ruin?
Or those deeds of yours in battles which surpass all,
O Devī, among all the hosts of asuras, gods and the rest? ॥6॥
4.7: You are the cause of all the worlds; though you have the three guṇas, the strands of nature, you are not known
to have their faults; even to Hari, Hara and the others you are boundless.
You are the refuge of all; this whole world is a portion of you;
for you are prakṛti, nature, unmanifest, supreme and primal. ॥7॥
4.8: She at whose utterance the whole company of gods
attains satisfaction in every sacrifice, O Devī: you are that Svāhā;
and you are the cause of satisfaction for the hosts of ancestors too;
for that very reason people utter you as Svadhā as well. ॥8॥
4.9: You who are the cause of liberation, whose great vows are beyond thought,
who are constantly practised by those whose senses are well restrained and for whom truth is the essence,
by sages who seek liberation and have cast off every fault:
you indeed are that blessed and supreme Knowledge, O Devī. ॥9॥
4.10: Your very self is sound; you are the treasury of the most pure Ṛk and Yajus verses,
and of the Sāman chants, with their Udgītha and the lovely recitation of their words.
O Devī, you are the blessed Trayī, the three Vedas; for the sustaining of the world
you are Vārtā, livelihood; you destroy the gravest sufferings of all the worlds. ॥10॥
4.11: You are Medhā, intelligence, O Devī, who know the essence of all the scriptures;
you are Durgā, the boat across the hard-to-cross ocean of worldly existence, free of attachment;
you are Śrī, who has made her sole abode in the heart of Viṣṇu, the foe of Kaiṭabha;
you alone are Gaurī, who has her place in the moon-crested Śiva. ॥11॥
4.12: Your face, gently smiling, spotless, like the disc
of the full moon, lovely with the lustre of the finest gold:
it is most wonderful that even so, seized with fury,
Mahiṣāsura, having seen that face, suddenly struck at it. ॥12॥
4.13: But, O Devī, having seen your face angry, terrible with knitted brows,
its hue like the rising moon, that at once
Mahiṣa did not give up his life is very strange;
for who can survive the sight of Death in his anger? ॥13॥
4.14: Be gracious, O Devī; you who are supreme, be gracious for our welfare.
When angered, you destroy whole families at once.
This has been known just now, for
this vast army of Mahiṣāsura has been wiped out. ॥14॥
4.15: They are honoured in their lands; theirs is wealth,
theirs is fame, and their circle of kin does not falter;
they alone are blessed, with sons, servants and wives who are devoted to them —
those with whom you are pleased, you who always grant prosperity. ॥15॥
4.16: O Devī, the virtuous man always performs every righteous deed,
each day and with the greatest reverence,
and then goes to heaven by your grace;
are you not then, O Devī, the giver of rewards in all three worlds? ॥16॥
4.17: O Durgā, when remembered you take away the fear of every creature,
and when remembered by those at ease you grant them a mind exceedingly auspicious.
O remover of poverty, sorrow and fear, who is there other than you
whose heart is ever tender to do good to all? ॥17॥
4.18: By the slaying of these the world attains happiness; and these,
even though they may have committed sin enough to keep them long in hell,
may meet death in battle and go to heaven:
surely it is with this thought, O Devī, that you slay the enemies. ॥18॥
4.19: Why do you not reduce to ashes by a mere look
all the asuras? That you hurl your weapon at the enemies
is so that even foes, purified by the weapon, may go to the higher worlds:
such is your kindly thought towards those hostile ones. ॥19॥
4.20: That by the fierce flashing of the masses of light from your sword
and by the mass of lustre at your trident's point the eyes of the asuras
did not perish, the reason is this: on your face, a match for the radiant crescent of the moon,
4.21: O Devī, your nature subdues the conduct of the wicked;
this form of yours is beyond thought, and no other can equal it;
and your valour slays those who seized the gods' prowess;
thus you have shown compassion even towards enemies. ॥21॥
4.22: With what can this prowess of yours be compared?
And where is there a form that strikes fear into enemies yet is exceedingly captivating?
Mercy in the heart and ruthlessness in battle are seen,
O Devī, giver of boons, in you alone in all the three worlds. ॥22॥
4.23: By destroying the foes you have saved
this whole triple world; slaying them at the head of the battle,
you have brought even those enemy hosts to heaven; and our fear, too, is gone,
the fear born of the frenzied enemies of the gods. Salutation to you. ॥23॥
4.24: O Devī, protect us with the trident; protect us, O Ambikā, with the sword as well;
protect us with the sound of the bell and with the twang of the bowstring. ॥24॥
4.25: Protect us in the east and in the west, O Caṇḍikā; protect us in the south;
and likewise in the north, O sovereign Devī, by whirling your own trident. ॥25॥
4.26: Those gentle forms of yours which roam the three worlds,
and those that are exceedingly terrible: with them protect us, and the earth as well. ॥26॥
4.27: O Ambikā, the sword, the trident, the mace and whatever other weapons are yours,
clinging to your hands, tender as young leaves: with them protect us on every side. ॥27॥
4.29: Thus praised by the gods, with divine flowers sprung in the Nandana garden
the sustainer of the worlds was worshipped, and likewise with perfumes and unguents. ॥29॥
4.30: Devoutly perfumed with divine incense by all the gods,
she, her face bright with grace, spoke to all the gods, who were bowed before her. ॥30॥
4.32: All you gods, choose whatever you desire from me. ॥32॥
4.34: The Bhagavatī has done everything; nothing remains. ॥34॥
4.35: since this enemy of ours, Mahiṣāsura, has been slain.
And yet, if a boon is to be given to us by you, O great sovereign, ॥35॥
4.36: each time you are remembered, may you destroy our gravest calamities;
and, O you of spotless face, the mortal who will praise you with these hymns — ॥36॥
4.37: for the increase of his fortunes, such as riches and wife, through wealth, abundance and splendour,
may you, O Ambikā, always be gracious to us. ॥37॥
4.39: Propitiated in this way by the gods for the world's sake and their own,
Bhadrakālī said: So be it; and she disappeared, O king. ॥39॥
4.40: Thus, O king, I have told you how in former times
the Devī, who desires the good of the three worlds, arose from the bodies of the gods. ॥40॥
4.41: And again, how she came forth from the body of Gaurī
to slay the wicked daityas, and likewise Śumbha and Niśumbha, ॥41॥
4.42: and to protect the worlds, as the benefactress of the gods:
hear that as I relate it; I tell it to you just as it was. Hrīṃ Om. ॥42॥
4.iti: Svasti, may it be well. Thus ends the fourth chapter, named the Praise by Śakra and the Other Gods, of the Devī Māhātmya in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, the age of the Manu Sāvarṇi. ॥4॥
5.viniyoga: Of this sacred Final Episode (Uttara Caritra), the seer is Rudra;
the metre is anuṣṭubh; the power (śakti) is Bhīmā; the seed (bīja) is Bhrāmarī;
and its essential form is the Sāmaveda. For the pleasure of Śrī Mahāsarasvatī,
its application is in the reading of the Final Episode.
5.dhyana: Holding bell, trident and plough, conch and pestle, discus, bow and arrow
in her lotus-hands, radiant as the cool-rayed moon that shines when the clouds are gone,
born from the body of Gaurī, the support of the three worlds:
here I worship Mahāsarasvatī, who crushes Śumbha and the other daityas.
5.2: Long ago the two asuras Śumbha and Niśumbha took from Indra, the lord of Śacī,
the three worlds and the shares of the sacrifice, relying on their pride and might. ॥2॥
5.3: Those two themselves took over the place of the Sun, and in the same way the office of the Moon,
and then those of Kubera, of Yama and of Varuṇa as well. ॥3॥
5.4: Those two themselves took over the power of Vāyu, the wind, and the work of Agni, fire, as well.
Then the gods were driven out, robbed of their sovereignty and defeated. ॥4॥
5.5: Stripped of their offices, all the gods, cast out by those two
great asuras, called to mind that invincible Devī. ॥5॥
5.6: They thought: She gave us a boon, saying: When I am remembered in times of calamity,
I will at that very moment destroy all your gravest misfortunes. ॥6॥
5.7: Having so resolved, the gods went to Himavat, the lord of mountains,
and there they then praised the Devī, Viṣṇumāyā. ॥7॥
5.9: Salutation to the Devī, to the great Devī; to Śivā, the auspicious one, salutation always.
Salutation to Prakṛti, primal nature, to Bhadrā, the gracious one. With minds restrained, we bow to her. ॥9॥
5.10: Salutation to the fierce one; to the eternal one, to Gaurī, to the sustainer, salutation again and again.
To her who is moonlight and who has the form of the moon, to her who is happiness, salutation always. ॥10॥
5.11: To her who is the welfare, the growth and the success of those who bow, we offer salutation again and again.
To Nairṛtī, to the fortune of kings, to Śarvāṇī: to you, salutation again and again. ॥11॥
5.12: To Durgā, to her who carries us across difficulties, to the Essence, to her who does all things,
to Khyāti, who is renown, and likewise to Kṛṣṇā, the dark one, and to Dhūmrā, the smoke-hued one: salutation always. ॥12॥
5.13: We bow to her who is exceedingly gentle and exceedingly fierce; to her, salutation again and again.
Salutation to the Devī who is the foundation of the world; to Kṛti, who is action, salutation again and again. ॥13॥
5.14: The Devī who in all beings is called Viṣṇumāyā, the māyā of Viṣṇu:
5.16: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥16॥
5.17: The Devī who in all beings is called consciousness:
5.19: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥19॥
5.20: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of intelligence:
5.22: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥22॥
5.23: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of sleep:
5.25: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥25॥
5.26: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of hunger:
5.28: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥28॥
5.29: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of shadow:
5.31: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥31॥
5.32: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of power:
5.34: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥34॥
5.35: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of thirst:
5.37: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥37॥
5.38: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of forbearance:
5.40: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥40॥
5.41: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of birth:
5.43: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥43॥
5.44: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of modesty:
5.46: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥46॥
5.47: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of peace:
5.49: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥49॥
5.50: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of faith:
5.52: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥52॥
5.53: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of beauty:
5.55: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥55॥
5.56: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of good fortune:
5.58: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥58॥
5.59: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of livelihood:
5.61: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥61॥
5.62: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of memory:
5.64: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥64॥
5.65: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of compassion:
5.67: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥67॥
5.68: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of contentment:
5.70: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥70॥
5.71: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of a mother:
5.73: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥73॥
5.74: The Devī who abides in all beings in the form of error:
5.76: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥76॥
5.77: She who presides over the senses of beings, and who in all beings
is ever present: to that all-pervading Devī, salutation again and again. ॥77॥
5.78: She who abides pervading this entire world in the form of consciousness:
5.80: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥80॥
5.81: Praised in former times by the gods because they had gained what they desired,
and likewise served day after day by Indra, lord of the gods:
may she, the Sovereign One, the cause of good, bring about for us
what is auspicious and blessed, and strike down calamities. ॥81॥
5.82: She is the Ruler to whom now we gods, tormented by the arrogant daityas,
and she, when remembered by those whose bodies are bowed in devotion, at that very moment
5.84: As the gods there were intent on praise in this way, Pārvatī
came to bathe in the waters of the Jāhnavī, the Gaṅgā, O prince. ॥84॥
5.85: She of lovely brows said to those gods: Who is it that you are praising here?
And from the sheath of her body Śivā came forth and said: ॥85॥
5.86: This hymn to me is being offered by the gods, cast out by the daitya Śumbha,
assembled together, and defeated in battle by Niśumbha. ॥86॥
5.87: Because Ambikā came forth from the sheath (kośa) of that Pārvatī's body,
for that reason she is sung of in all the worlds as Kauśikī. ॥87॥
5.88: When she had come forth, that Pārvatī too became dark,
and, having made the Himālaya her dwelling, became known as Kālikā. ॥88॥
5.89: Then Ambikā, bearing a supreme and most enchanting form,
was seen by Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, the two who served Śumbha and Niśumbha. ॥89॥
5.90: And the two told Śumbha of her, exceedingly lovely as she was:
O great king, a certain woman dwells there, lighting up the Himālaya. ॥90॥
5.91: Such a supreme form has not been seen anywhere by anyone.
Let it be found out who this goddess may be, and let her be taken, O lord of the asuras. ॥91॥
5.92: A jewel among women, exceedingly lovely of limb, lighting up the directions with her radiance,
she is staying there, O lord of the daityas; you ought to see her. ॥92॥
5.93: O lord, whatever jewels, gems, elephants, horses and the like
there are in the three worlds, all of them now shine in your house. ॥93॥
5.94: Airāvata, the jewel among elephants, has been brought from Indra;
so too this Pārijāta tree, and in the same way the horse Uccaiḥśravas. ॥94॥
5.95: This aerial chariot yoked with swans stands in your courtyard;
a jewel of its kind, the wondrous one that was Brahmā's, it has been brought here. ॥95॥
5.96: This treasure, Mahāpadma, has been brought from Kubera, the lord of riches;
and a garland of unfading lotuses, full of filaments, was the ocean's gift. ॥96॥
5.97: Varuṇa's umbrella that streams gold stands in your house;
likewise this finest of chariots, which once belonged to Prajāpati. ॥97॥
5.98: O lord, Death's spear named Utkrāntidā (she who makes life depart) has been seized by you;
the noose of the king of the waters, Varuṇa, is in your brother's possession. ॥98॥
5.99: And all the kinds of gems born of the ocean are Niśumbha's;
Agni too gave you a pair of garments that are cleansed by fire. ॥99॥
5.100: Thus, O lord of the daityas, all the jewels have been brought to you.
This lovely lady is the jewel among women: why do you not take her? ॥100॥
5.102: Having heard these words of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, Śumbha then
sent the great asura Sugrīva to the Devī as his messenger. ॥102॥
5.103: Śumbha said: Go there and tell her this and this, on my word;
and act quickly, in such a way that she comes gladly. ॥103॥
5.104: He went there, to where she was staying on a very beautiful spot of the mountain,
and then he spoke to the Devī gently, in a sweet voice. ॥104॥
5.106: O Devī, Śumbha, lord of the daityas, is the supreme lord in the three worlds.
I am a messenger sent by him, and I have come here to you. ॥106॥
5.107: He whose command is never hindered among any of the divine orders of beings,
who has conquered all the enemies of the daityas: hear what he has said. ॥107॥
5.108: The whole of the three worlds is mine; the gods are subject to my will;
all the shares of the sacrifices I enjoy, each one separately. ॥108॥
5.109: The choicest jewels in the three worlds are, every one, in my power;
so too the jewel among elephants, the mount of the king of the gods, has been taken. ॥109॥
5.110: The jewel among horses that arose from the churning of the Ocean of Milk,
the one named Uccaiḥśravas, has been offered to me by the immortals, bowing low. ॥110॥
5.111: And whatever other beings and things among the gods, the gandharvas and the serpents
are jewels of their kind, O beautiful one, are with me alone. ॥111॥
5.112: O Devī, we regard you as the jewel among women in the world.
So come to us, for we are the enjoyers of jewels. ॥112॥
5.113: Me, or else my younger brother Niśumbha of mighty valour,
you should accept, O you of restless glances, for you are truly a jewel. ॥113॥
5.114: By becoming my wife you will gain supreme, unequalled sovereignty.
Weigh this well in your mind, and become my wife. ॥114॥
5.116: Thus addressed, the Devī then spoke, smiling deeply within,
Durgā, the blessed and auspicious one, by whom this world is upheld. ॥116॥
5.118: What you have said is true; nothing you have spoken here is false.
Śumbha is lord of the three worlds, and Niśumbha too is his like. ॥118॥
5.119: But in this matter, how can I make false what I have vowed?
Hear the vow that I made long ago, out of my little understanding. ॥119॥
5.120: He who conquers me in battle, who takes away my pride,
who in the world is equal to me in strength, he will be my husband. ॥120॥
5.121: So let Śumbha come here, or the mighty Niśumbha;
let him conquer me and quickly take my hand here: why delay? ॥121॥
5.123: You are arrogant; O Devī, do not speak like this before me.
In the three worlds, what man could stand before Śumbha and Niśumbha? ॥123॥
5.124: Even before the other daityas, none of the gods stands
face to face in battle, O Devī; how much less you, a woman, alone? ॥124॥
5.125: All the gods, led by Indra, could not stand before them in battle;
how will you, a woman, go to face them, Śumbha and the others? ॥125॥
5.126: So go, as I myself tell you, to Śumbha and Niśumbha;
do not go with your dignity stripped from you by being dragged by the hair. ॥126॥
5.128: So it is: Śumbha is mighty, and Niśumbha too is such.
But what can I do, since my vow was made long ago without reflection? ॥128॥
5.129: So go, and all this that I have told you,
tell the lord of the asuras with care; and let him do what is fitting. ॥129॥
5.iti: Svasti, may it be well. Thus ends the fifth chapter, named the Devī's Dialogue with the Messenger, of the Devī Māhātmya in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, the age of the Manu Sāvarṇi. ॥5॥
6.dhyana: Om. Her whose seat is the lord of serpents, whose slender, creeper-like body, with the great string of gems that crowns the serpents' hoods,
shines bright; who is like the sun in radiance, and lit with three eyes;
whose hands hold a rosary, a pitcher, a skull and a lotus; who wears the half-moon as her crest; the supreme one,
who dwells in the body of Bhairava, the all-knowing Lord: on Padmāvatī I meditate.
6.2: Having heard these words of the Devī, the messenger, filled with indignation,
went back to the king of the daityas and reported them to him in full. ॥2॥
6.3: Then, having heard that report of the messenger, the king of the asuras
spoke in anger to Dhūmralocana, a chief of the daityas: ॥3॥
6.4: O Dhūmralocana, quickly, surrounded by your own army,
bring that wicked woman by force, distraught from being dragged by the hair. ॥4॥
6.5: And if anyone else rises up to protect her,
he is to be slain, be he a god, a yakṣa or a gandharva. ॥5॥
6.7: Then, so commanded by him, the daitya Dhūmralocana quickly,
surrounded by sixty thousand asuras, set out at speed. ॥7॥
6.8: Then, seeing the Devī stationed on the snowy mountain,
he called out loudly: Go to Śumbha and Niśumbha. ॥8॥
6.9: If you do not come to my master willingly today,
then I will take you by force, distraught from being dragged by the hair. ॥9॥
6.11: Sent by the lord of the daityas, mighty and surrounded by an army,
if you take me thus by force, then what can I do to you? ॥11॥
6.13: Thus addressed, the asura Dhūmralocana rushed at her;
then Ambikā reduced him to ashes with the mere sound huṃ. ॥13॥
6.14: Then upon the enraged great army of the asuras Ambikā
rained sharp arrows, and spears and axes as well. ॥14॥
6.15: Then, shaking its mane in fury and letting out a most terrible roar,
the lion, the Devī's own mount, fell upon the army of the asuras. ॥15॥
6.16: Some daityas it slew with blows of its paw, others with its mouth,
and other great asuras by trampling them and with its lip. ॥16॥
6.17: The maned lion tore open the bellies of some with its claws,
and likewise, with blows of its paw, it struck heads from bodies. ॥17॥
6.18: Others in the same way it left with arms and heads cut off,
and, shaking its mane, it drank the blood from the bellies of yet others. ॥18॥
6.19: In a moment that whole army was brought to ruin by the mighty one,
that lion, the Devī's mount, exceedingly enraged. ॥19॥
6.20: Hearing that the asura Dhūmralocana had been slain by the Devī,
and that the whole army had then been destroyed by the Devī's lion, ॥20॥
6.21: Śumbha, the overlord of the daityas, grew furious, his lip quivering,
and he commanded the two great asuras, Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa: ॥21॥
6.22: O Caṇḍa, O Muṇḍa, surrounded by many troops,
go there, and when you have gone, let her be brought here quickly, ॥22॥
6.23: dragged by the hair or bound. If you are in any doubt in the fight,
then let her be slain by all the asuras with all their weapons. ॥23॥
6.24: When that wicked woman has been slain and the lion struck down,
come back quickly; or else bind and seize that Ambikā and bring her. ॥24॥
6.iti: Svasti, may it be well. Thus ends the sixth chapter, named the Slaying of Dhūmralocana, General of Śumbha and Niśumbha, of the Devī Māhātmya in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, the age of the Manu Sāvarṇi. ॥6॥
7.dhyana: Om. Let me meditate on her who, on a jewelled seat, listens to the sweet recitation of a parrot, and whose limbs are dark,
who has set one foot on a lotus, who bears a digit of the moon, who plays the vīṇā,
who wears a garland of kalhāra lilies, whose shining bodice is closely fastened, who is clad in jewelled garments:
Mātaṅgī, who holds a conch-shell cup, who is flushed with sweet wine, whose forehead shines with a tilaka mark.
7.2: Then, so commanded, those daityas, with Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa at their head,
with an army of four divisions, set out with weapons raised. ॥2॥
7.3: Then they saw the Devī, gently smiling, stationed
upon the lion on a great golden peak of the king of mountains. ॥3॥
7.4: Seeing her, they made ready and strove to seize her,
and others, with bows drawn and swords in hand, drew near her. ॥4॥
7.5: Then Ambikā grew fiercely angry with those enemies,
and with her anger her face then turned black as ink. ॥5॥
7.6: From the broad expanse of her forehead, knit with a frown, there swiftly
came forth Kālī, terrible of face, bearing sword and noose. ॥6॥
7.7: She bore a strange khaṭvāṅga, a skull-topped staff, and was adorned with a garland of human heads;
she was clad in a tiger-skin, her flesh was withered, and she was exceedingly dreadful. ॥7॥
7.8: Her mouth gaped very wide, she was fearsome with her lolling tongue;
her eyes were sunken and red, and she filled the quarters with her roar. ॥8॥
7.9: Falling upon them with speed and slaying the great asuras,
she devoured that host there in the army of the enemies of the gods. ॥9॥
7.10: The elephants, with their rear-guards, goad-bearing drivers, warriors and bells,
she seized with one hand and flung into her mouth. ॥10॥
7.11: Likewise a warrior with his horses, and a chariot with its charioteer,
she put into her mouth and chewed most dreadfully with her teeth. ॥11॥
7.12: One she caught by the hair, another by the neck;
another she pressed down with her foot, and yet another she crushed with her chest. ॥12॥
7.13: And the weapons and great missiles hurled by those asuras
she caught with her mouth in fury, and ground them to pieces with her teeth too. ॥13॥
7.14: That whole army of the mighty, evil-souled asuras
she then trampled; some she devoured, and others she struck down. ॥14॥
7.15: Some were slain by the sword, some beaten with the khaṭvāṅga;
and struck likewise by the points of her teeth, the asuras went to their destruction. ॥15॥
7.16: Seeing that entire army of the asuras felled in a moment,
Caṇḍa rushed at Kālī, that most fearsome one. ॥16॥
7.17: The great asura Caṇḍa covered her of the terrible eyes with showers of most dreadful arrows,
and Muṇḍa with discuses hurled by the thousand. ॥17॥
7.18: Those many discuses, entering her mouth,
shone like a great many orbs of the sun passing into the belly of a cloud. ॥18॥
7.19: Then, in exceeding wrath, roaring terribly,
Kālī, of the dreadful face, gleaming with teeth fearful to behold, laughed a fearsome laugh. ॥19॥
7.20: And rising up onto the great lion, the Devī ran at Caṇḍa,
and seizing him by the hair, cut off his head with that sword. ॥20॥
7.21: Then Muṇḍa, seeing Caṇḍa felled, rushed at her;
in her fury she struck him too with the sword and brought him down to the ground. ॥21॥
7.22: Then what was left of the army after the slaughter, seeing Caṇḍa felled
and Muṇḍa too, of very great valour, fled to every quarter, stricken with fear. ॥22॥
7.23: And Kālī, taking the head of Caṇḍa and the head of Muṇḍa as well,
went up to Caṇḍikā and spoke amid fierce peals of laughter: ॥23॥
7.24: Here I have offered you Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, two great sacrificial beasts;
in the sacrifice of battle you yourself will slay Śumbha and Niśumbha. ॥24॥
7.26: Then, seeing the two great asuras Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa brought before her,
the auspicious Caṇḍikā spoke gentle words to Kālī: ॥26॥
7.27: Since you have seized Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa and come here,
you will therefore be renowned in the world as the Devī Cāmuṇḍā. ॥27॥
7.iti: Svasti, may it be well. Thus ends the seventh chapter, named the Slaying of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, of the Devī Māhātmya in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, the age of the Manu Sāvarṇi. ॥7॥
8.dhyana: Om. She who is red as the dawn, whose eyes ripple with waves of compassion,
whose hands hold the noose, the goad, the arrow and the bow,
who is surrounded by rays, Aṇimā and the other powers:
on that Bhavānī I meditate as my very self.
8.2: When the daitya Caṇḍa had been slain and Muṇḍa struck down,
and many armies had been destroyed, the lord of the asuras, ॥2॥
8.3: Śumbha the mighty, his mind then wholly in the grip of anger,
ordered all the armies of the daityas to make ready. ॥3॥
8.4: Today let eighty-six daityas, weapons raised, go forth with all their forces;
let eighty-four of the Kambus march out, each surrounded by his own troops. ॥4॥
8.5: Let the fifty clans of asuras, of boundless valour,
and the hundred clans of the Dhaumras go forth at my command. ॥5॥
8.6: Let the Kālakas, the Daurhṛdas, the Maurvas and likewise the Kālikeya asuras,
equipped for battle, march out in haste at my command. ॥6॥
8.7: Having thus given his orders, Śumbha, lord of the asuras, whose rule was fearsome,
went forth surrounded by many thousands of great armies. ॥7॥
8.8: Seeing that most terrifying army approaching, Caṇḍikā
with the twang of her bowstring filled the space between earth and sky. ॥8॥
8.9: Then, O king, the lion gave an exceedingly great roar,
and with the sound of her bell Ambikā swelled those roars. ॥9॥
8.10: With the quarters filled by the sound of the bowstring, the lion and the bell,
Kālī, her mouth opened wide, outdid them all with her terrifying roars. ॥10॥
8.11: Hearing that roar, the daitya armies, from all four sides,
surrounded the Devī, the lion and Kālī in their rage. ॥11॥
8.12: Meanwhile, O king, for the destruction of the enemies of the gods
and for the welfare of the lions among the immortals, endowed with exceeding valour and strength, ॥12॥
8.13: the śaktis, the powers, of Brahmā, Śiva, Kārttikeya and Viṣṇu, and likewise of Indra,
came out of their bodies and went to Caṇḍikā in the forms of those gods. ॥13॥
8.14: Whatever form each god had, and whatever ornaments and mount,
in just that way his śakti came to fight the asuras. ॥14॥
8.15: Seated on a celestial car yoked with swans, holding a rosary and a water-pot,
came the śakti of Brahmā; she is called Brahmāṇī. ॥15॥
8.16: Māheśvarī, mounted on a bull, holding a splendid trident,
with great serpents for bracelets and adorned with the crescent moon, arrived. ॥16॥
8.17: And Kaumārī, spear in hand, whose mount is a splendid peacock,
came forth to fight the daityas: Ambikā in the form of Kārttikeya. ॥17॥
8.18: Likewise the śakti Vaiṣṇavī, seated upon Garuḍa,
came forward with conch, discus, mace, the Śārṅga bow and sword in her hands. ॥18॥
8.19: The śakti of Hari, who bears the incomparable form of the sacrificial Boar,
she too came there, bearing a boar's body. ॥19॥
8.20: Nārasiṃhī, bearing a body like that of Nṛsiṃha,
arrived there, the hosts of stars scattered by the tossing of her mane. ॥20॥
8.21: Likewise Aindrī, thunderbolt in hand, seated upon the king of elephants,
arrived, thousand-eyed; just as Śakra is, so was she. ॥21॥
8.22: Then Śiva, surrounded by those śaktis of the gods,
said to Caṇḍikā: Let the asuras be slain quickly, for my pleasure. ॥22॥
8.23: Then from the body of the Devī there came forth, most terrifying,
the śakti Caṇḍikā, exceedingly fierce, howling like a hundred jackals. ॥23॥
8.24: And she, the Unvanquished, said to Śiva of the smoke-grey matted locks:
O Lord, go as messenger to Śumbha and Niśumbha. ॥24॥
8.25: Tell Śumbha and Niśumbha, the two exceedingly proud dānavas,
and the other dānavas who are assembled there for battle: ॥25॥
8.26: Let Indra have the three worlds, and let the gods partake of the oblations;
go to Pātāla, the underworld, if you wish to live. ॥26॥
8.27: But if, from pride in your strength, you are eager for battle,
then come, and let my jackals be sated with your flesh. ॥27॥
8.28: Because Śiva himself was appointed by that Devī to the office of messenger,
she became renowned in this world as Śivadūtī, she whose messenger is Śiva. ॥28॥
8.29: The great asuras too, having heard the Devī's words as Śiva announced them,
were filled with fury and went to where Kātyāyanī stood. ॥29॥
8.30: Then, first of all, at the front, with showers of arrows, spears and pikes
the enemies of the gods, their wrath roused, rained down upon that Devī. ॥30॥
8.31: And she cut down those arrows, tridents, spears and axes hurled at her,
playfully, with great arrows loosed from her twanging bow. ॥31॥
8.32: Likewise, in front of him, Kālī, rending the foes with the fall of her trident
and crushing them with her khaṭvāṅga, then ranged about the field. ॥32॥
8.33: Robbed of valour by water flung from her kamaṇḍalu, her water-pot, and robbed of vigour:
so Brahmāṇī left the enemies wherever she ran. ॥33॥
8.34: Māheśvarī with her trident, likewise Vaiṣṇavī with her discus,
and Kaumārī, exceedingly wrathful, likewise with her spear, slew the daityas. ॥34॥
8.35: By the fall of Aindrī's thunderbolt, daityas and dānavas by the hundreds
fell to the earth torn apart, pouring forth streams of blood. ॥35॥
8.36: Shattered by blows of the snout, their chests wounded by the tips of the tusks,
struck by her of the boar form, they fell, torn also by the discus. ॥36॥
8.37: Devouring other great asuras torn apart by her claws,
Nārasiṃhī ranged through the battle, filling the quarters and the sky with her roar. ॥37॥
8.38: Stricken by Śivadūtī with her fierce peals of laughter, the asuras
fell to the earth, and then she devoured those who had fallen. ॥38॥
8.39: Seeing the host of Mothers, enraged, thus crushing the great asuras,
the soldiers of the gods' enemies fled by various means. ॥39॥
8.40: Seeing the daityas, harassed by the host of Mothers, intent on flight,
the great asura Raktabīja came forward in wrath to fight. ॥40॥
8.41: Whenever a drop of blood falls from his body to the ground,
a great asura of his own size springs up on the earth. ॥41॥
8.42: Mace in hand, that great asura fought against the śakti of Indra;
then Aindrī struck Raktabīja with her own thunderbolt. ॥42॥
8.43: From him, struck by the thunderbolt, much blood quickly flowed;
from it arose warriors of his form and of his prowess. ॥43॥
8.44: As many drops of blood as fell from his body,
so many men were born, with his valour, strength and prowess. ॥44॥
8.45: And those men born of the blood also fought there
against the Mothers, a fight most dreadful with the fall of exceedingly fierce weapons. ॥45॥
8.46: And again, when the stroke of the thunderbolt wounded his head,
blood flowed, and from it men were born by the thousands. ॥46॥
8.47: And Vaiṣṇavī struck him in battle with her discus;
Aindrī beat that lord of the asuras with a mace. ॥47॥
8.48: By great asuras born from the flowing blood of him whom Vaiṣṇavī's discus had pierced,
of his own size and by the thousands, the world was filled. ॥48॥
8.49: Kaumārī struck with her spear, and Vārāhī likewise with her sword,
and Māheśvarī with her trident, the great asura Raktabīja. ॥49॥
8.50: And that daitya too, the great asura Raktabīja, possessed by anger, struck with his mace
all the Mothers, each one separately. ॥50॥
8.51: As he was struck in many ways with spears, tridents and the like, the stream of his blood
that fell upon the ground brought asuras into being by the hundreds. ॥51॥
8.52: And by those asuras born from the asura's blood the whole world
was filled; then the gods were seized by the utmost fear. ॥52॥
8.53: Seeing those gods dejected, Caṇḍikā spoke quickly;
she said to Kālī: O Cāmuṇḍā, open your mouth wide. ॥53॥
8.54: The drops of blood arising from the strokes of my weapons, and the great asuras
that arise from the drop of blood, receive with this swift mouth of yours. ॥54॥
8.55: Roam the battlefield, devouring the great asuras born from it.
Thus this daitya, his blood drained, will go to destruction. ॥55॥
8.56: With the fierce ones being devoured by you, no others will arise.
Having said this to her, the Devī then struck him with her trident. ॥56॥
8.57: With her mouth Kālī took in Raktabīja's blood.
Then, there, he struck Caṇḍikā with his mace. ॥57॥
8.58: The blow of the mace caused her not even the slightest pain.
But from the body of him who had been struck, much blood flowed. ॥58॥
8.59: From wherever it flowed, Cāmuṇḍā received it with her mouth;
and the great asuras who arose in her mouth from the falling blood, ॥59॥
8.60: those Cāmuṇḍā then devoured, and she drank his blood.
The Devī, with trident, thunderbolt, arrows, swords and pikes, ॥60॥
8.61: struck down that Raktabīja, whose blood Cāmuṇḍā had drunk.
Struck by the multitude of weapons, he fell upon the face of the earth. ॥61॥
8.62: And the great asura Raktabīja, O protector of the earth, was left bloodless.
Then, O king, the gods attained incomparable joy. ॥62॥
8.63: The host of Mothers born from them danced, wild with the intoxication of blood. ॥63॥
8.iti: Svasti, may it be well. Thus ends the eighth chapter, named the Slaying of Raktabīja, of the Devī Māhātmya in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, the age of the Manu Sāvarṇi. ॥8॥
9.dhyana: Om. Glowing like the bandhūka flower and like gold, bearing a lovely rosary,
the noose and the goad, and the gesture of granting boons in its own staff-like arms,
with a digit of the moon for its ornament, three-eyed:
in that form, half Ambikā and half Īśa, the Lord Śiva, I ceaselessly take refuge.
9.2: O revered one, you have told me this wonderful account:
the greatness of the Devī's deeds in the slaying of Raktabīja. ॥2॥
9.3: And I wish to hear further: when Raktabīja had been struck down,
what deed did Śumbha do, and the exceedingly wrathful Niśumbha? ॥3॥
9.5: When Raktabīja had been struck down, they flew into an unequalled rage,
the asura Śumbha and Niśumbha, now that the others too had been slain in the battle. ॥5॥
9.6: Seeing his great army being slaughtered and swelling with indignation,
Niśumbha then charged with the chief host of the asuras. ॥6॥
9.7: In front of him, and likewise behind him and on both his flanks, great asuras,
biting their lips in anger, came up to slay the Devī. ॥7॥
9.8: Śumbha too, of great valour, came on, surrounded by his own forces,
having fought with the Mothers, to slay Caṇḍikā in his anger. ॥8॥
9.9: Then an exceedingly fierce battle took place between the Devī and Śumbha and Niśumbha;
the two loosed an exceedingly terrible rain of arrows, like two clouds pouring down rain. ॥9॥
9.10: With her own masses of arrows Caṇḍikā cut down the arrows those two had shot,
and she struck the two lords of the asuras on their limbs with floods of weapons. ॥10॥
9.11: Niśumbha, taking up a sharp sword and a gleaming shield,
struck on the head the lion, the Devī's excellent mount. ॥11॥
9.12: When her mount was struck, the Devī, with a kṣurapra, a razor-edged arrow,
swiftly cut down Niśumbha's excellent sword and also his shield, marked with eight moons. ॥12॥
9.13: When his shield and sword were cut down, that asura hurled a spear;
that too, as it came straight at her, she cut in two with her discus. ॥13॥
9.14: Then the dānava Niśumbha, swollen with rage, seized a trident;
and as it came, the Devī crushed that too to powder with a blow of her fist. ॥14॥
9.15: Then he too whirled a mace and hurled it at Caṇḍikā;
it too, shattered by the Devī's trident, was turned to ashes. ॥15॥
9.16: Then, as that foremost of the daityas came on, axe in hand,
the Devī struck him with floods of arrows and felled him to the ground. ॥16॥
9.17: When his brother Niśumbha, of terrible prowess, had fallen to the ground,
Śumbha, exceedingly enraged, set out to slay Ambikā. ॥17॥
9.18: Standing in his chariot, and with arms raised high aloft, holding supreme weapons —
eight arms beyond compare — he shone, filling the whole sky. ॥18॥
9.19: Seeing him coming, the Devī blew her conch,
and also made her bowstring twang, a sound exceedingly hard to bear. ॥19॥
9.20: And she filled the quarters with the sound of her own bell,
a sound that destroyed the vigour of all the daitya armies. ॥20॥
9.21: Then the lion, with great roars that made the elephants give up their great rut,
filled the sky, the earth and likewise the ten directions. ॥21॥
9.22: Then Kālī, leaping up into the sky, struck the earth
with both her hands; by that resounding blow the sounds before it were drowned out. ॥22॥
9.23: Śivadūtī let out a loud, ominous peal of laughter;
at those sounds the asuras trembled, and Śumbha went into the utmost rage. ॥23॥
9.24: When Ambikā cried out: Stand, stand, you wicked one!
then the gods stationed in the sky called out: Victory! ॥24॥
9.25: The spear that Śumbha came forward and hurled, exceedingly dreadful with its flames,
shining like a mass of fire as it came on, was beaten back with a great meteor. ॥25॥
9.26: Śumbha's lion-roar filled all the space within the three worlds;
and the dreadful crash of a thunderclap overpowered it, O lord of the earth. ॥26॥
9.27: The Devī cut down the arrows Śumbha shot, and Śumbha those she sent,
each with their own fierce arrows, by hundreds and by thousands. ॥27॥
9.28: Then Caṇḍikā, enraged, struck him with her trident;
and he, struck down then, fell senseless to the ground. ॥28॥
9.29: Then Niśumbha, regaining consciousness, took up his bow
and struck with arrows the Devī, Kālī and the lion as well. ॥29॥
9.30: And again, making ten thousand arms, the lord of the dānavas,
the son of Diti, covered Caṇḍikā with his discus-weapons. ॥30॥
9.31: Then the blessed Durgā, destroyer of the pain of hard straits, enraged,
the Devī cut down with her own arrows those discuses and those arrows. ॥31॥
9.32: Then Niśumbha, seizing a mace, rushed swiftly at Caṇḍikā
to slay her, surrounded by the daitya army. ॥32॥
9.33: Even as he rushed upon her, Caṇḍikā swiftly cut his mace
with her sharp-edged sword; and he took up a trident. ॥33॥
9.34: As Niśumbha, the tormentor of the immortals, came on, trident in hand,
Caṇḍikā pierced him in the heart with her trident, hurled with force. ॥34॥
9.35: From the heart of him, pierced by the trident, there came forth another,
a man of great strength and great valour, who was saying: Stand! ॥35॥
9.36: As he was coming out, the Devī laughed aloud and then
cut off his head with her sword; then he fell to the ground. ॥36॥
9.37: Then the lion, crushing their necks with his fierce fangs, devoured
those asuras; and likewise Kālī and Śivadūtī devoured others. ॥37॥
9.38: Some great asuras, pierced through by Kaumārī's spear, perished;
others were driven off by water made holy by Brahmāṇī's mantras. ॥38॥
9.39: Likewise others fell, pierced by Māheśvarī's trident;
some, by the blows of Vārāhī's snout, were pounded to dust on the ground. ॥39॥
9.40: Dānavas were cut to pieces by Vaiṣṇavī's discus,
and likewise others by the thunderbolt let fly from the tip of Aindrī's hand. ॥40॥
9.41: Some asuras perished; some fled from the great battle;
and Kālī, Śivadūtī and the lion, the king of beasts, devoured others. ॥41॥
9.iti: Svasti, may it be well. Thus ends the ninth chapter, named the Slaying of Niśumbha, of the Devī Māhātmya in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, the age of the Manu Sāvarṇi. ॥9॥
10.dhyana: Om. Her who glows like heated gold, whose eyes are the sun, the moon and fire,
who holds the bow and arrows with the goad, the noose and the trident
in her lovely arms, whose form is Śiva and Śakti,
Kāmeśvarī, who wears the crescent moon: her I worship in my heart.
10.2: Seeing his brother Niśumbha, dear to him as his own life, slain,
and his army being slaughtered, Śumbha in his anger spoke these words: ॥2॥
10.3: O Durgā, spoilt by the pride of your strength, do not be arrogant.
You fight relying on the strength of other women, and yet you are so very haughty. ॥3॥
10.5: I alone am here in the world; who else, a second, is there besides me?
See, wicked one, these powers of mine entering into me alone. ॥5॥
10.6: Then all those goddesses, headed by Brahmāṇī,
were dissolved into the body of that Devī; then Ambikā alone was there. ॥6॥
10.8: The many forms in which I stood here through my power,
those I have withdrawn; I stand alone in the battle. Be steady. ॥8॥
10.10: Then a battle began between the two, the Devī and Śumbha,
a terrible battle, as all the gods and the asuras looked on. ॥10॥
10.11: With showers of arrows, with sharp weapons and with most dreadful missiles,
the battle between the two went on again, terrifying all the worlds. ॥11॥
10.12: The hundreds of divine missiles that Ambikā then let fly,
the lord of the daityas broke with weapons that warded them off. ॥12॥
10.13: And the divine missiles he let fly, the Supreme Devī
broke as if in play, with fierce cries of huṃ and the like. ॥13॥
10.14: Then that asura covered the Devī with hundreds of arrows;
and the Devī, angered at that, cut his bow with her arrows in turn. ॥14॥
10.15: When his bow was cut, the lord of the daityas then took up a spear;
that too, as it rested in his hand, the Devī cut with her discus. ॥15॥
10.16: Then, taking up a sword and a shining shield marked with a hundred moons,
the sovereign lord of the daityas rushed at that Devī. ॥16॥
10.17: Even as he rushed on, Caṇḍikā swiftly cut his sword
with sharp arrows loosed from her bow, and also his shield, spotless as the sun's rays;
and she struck down his horses, and his chariot with the charioteer. ॥17॥
10.18: Then that daitya, his horses slain, his bow cut, left without a charioteer,
seized a dreadful war-hammer, intent on killing Ambikā. ॥18॥
10.19: As he rushed on, the Devī cut his war-hammer with sharp arrows;
even so he ran at her swiftly, raising his fist. ॥19॥
10.20: That bull among the daityas brought his fist down on the Devī's heart;
and the Devī too struck him on the chest with the palm of her hand. ॥20॥
10.21: Struck by the blow of her palm, that king of the daityas fell to the ground,
and at once rose up again, just as before. ॥21॥
10.22: And leaping up, he seized the Devī and rose high into the sky;
there too Caṇḍikā fought with him, with nothing to support her. ॥22॥
10.23: Then in the sky the daitya and Caṇḍikā fought each other hand to hand,
a combat never seen before, which filled the siddhas and sages with wonder. ॥23॥
10.24: Then Ambikā, having fought hand to hand with him for a long time,
lifted him up, whirled him round and hurled him to the ground. ॥24॥
10.25: Thrown down, he reached the earth and, swift, raising his fist,
the wicked one rushed at her, wishing to slay Caṇḍikā. ॥25॥
10.26: Then, as he came on, the lord of all the daitya people
the Devī pierced in the chest with her trident and felled to the ground. ॥26॥
10.27: Wounded by the point of the Devī's trident, he fell to the ground, lifeless,
shaking all the earth with its oceans, islands and mountains. ॥27॥
10.28: Then, when that evil-souled one was slain, all became serene;
the world attained great well-being, and the sky became clear. ॥28॥
10.29: The clouds of ill omen, with their meteors, that had been there before were stilled;
and when he was felled there, the rivers likewise flowed within their courses. ॥29॥
10.30: Then all the hosts of gods became full of joy at heart
when he was slain, and the gandharvas sang sweetly. ॥30॥
10.31: Likewise others played music, and the hosts of apsarases danced;
pure winds likewise blew, and the sun shone with a fair light. ॥31॥
10.32: The fires that had gone out blazed up, and the sounds that had arisen in the quarters were stilled. ॥32॥
10.iti: Svasti, may it be well. Thus ends the tenth chapter, named the Slaying of Śumbha, of the Devī Māhātmya in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, the age of the Manu Sāvarṇi. ॥10॥
11.dhyana: Om. Her whose radiance is that of the rising sun, who wears the moon as her crown, whose breasts are high, who has three eyes,
whose face is smiling, whose hands show the gesture of granting boons, the goad, the noose and the gesture of fearlessness: Bhuvaneśī I worship.
11.2: When the great lord of the asuras had been slain there by the Devī,
the gods together with Indra, with Agni at their head,
praised her, Kātyāyanī, for they had gained what they desired,
their blooming lotus-faces lighting up the quarters. ॥2॥
11.3: O Devī, who take away the distress of those who come to you for refuge, be gracious.
Be gracious, O Mother of all the world.
Be gracious, O ruler of the universe; protect the universe.
You, O Devī, are the sovereign of all that moves and does not move. ॥3॥
11.4: You alone have become the support of the world,
for you abide in the form of the earth;
by you, abiding in the form of the waters,
all this is nourished, O you whose valour none can overstep. ॥4॥
11.5: You are the power of Viṣṇu, of boundless valour;
you are the seed of the universe, the supreme māyā, the power that deludes.
O Devī, all this is held in delusion;
you indeed, when gracious, are the cause of liberation on earth. ॥5॥
11.6: All forms of knowledge, O Devī, are your aspects,
and so are all women, every one, throughout the worlds.
By you alone, the Mother, all this is filled.
What praise can there be of you? You are beyond all that is to be praised, the highest speech. ॥6॥
11.7: When, as the Devī who are all beings, the giver of enjoyment and liberation,
you have been praised, what excellent words could there be for further praise? ॥7॥
11.8: O you who abide in the heart of every person in the form of intelligence,
O Devī, giver of heaven and liberation, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥8॥
11.9: O you who, in the form of kalā, kāṣṭhā and the other measures of time, bring about change,
O you who have the power to bring the universe to its end, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥9॥
11.10: O auspiciousness of all that is auspicious, O Śivā, the auspicious one, accomplisher of every aim,
O giver of refuge, O three-eyed one, O Gaurī, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥10॥
11.11: O you who are the power of creation, preservation and destruction, O eternal one,
O abode of the guṇas, the strands of nature, O you who are made of the guṇas, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥11॥
11.12: O you who are intent on rescuing the wretched and the afflicted who come to you for refuge,
O Devī who take away the distress of all, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥12॥
11.13: O you who are seated in the celestial car yoked with swans, who bear the form of Brahmāṇī,
O Devī who sprinkle water with kuśa grass, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥13॥
11.14: O you who hold the trident, the moon and the serpent, who ride the great bull,
O Nārāyaṇī in the form of Māheśvarī, salutation to you. ॥14॥
11.15: O you who are surrounded by peacocks and cocks, who bear the great spear, O sinless one,
O you who abide in the form of Kaumārī, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥15॥
11.16: O you who have taken up the supreme weapons, the conch, the discus, the mace and the Śārṅga bow,
be gracious, O you in the form of Vaiṣṇavī; O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥16॥
11.17: O you who hold the fierce great discus, who lifted up the earth on your tusk,
O Śivā in the form of the Boar, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥17॥
11.18: O you who, in the fierce form of the Man-Lion, set out to slay the daityas,
O you who undertake the protection of the three worlds, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥18॥
11.19: O crowned one, wielder of the great thunderbolt, resplendent with a thousand eyes,
O Aindrī, taker of Vṛtra's life, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥19॥
11.20: O you who, in the form of Śivadūtī, slew the mighty host of the daityas,
O you of terrible form and mighty roar, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥20॥
11.21: O you whose face is dreadful with fangs, who are adorned with a garland of heads,
O Cāmuṇḍā, crusher of Muṇḍa, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥21॥
11.22: O Lakṣmī, O Modesty, O great Knowledge, O Faith, O Nourishment, O Svadhā, offering to the ancestors, O Constant one,
O great Night, O Mahāmāyā, great power of illusion, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥22॥
11.23: O Medhā, intelligence, O Sarasvatī, O excellent one, O Prosperity, O tawny Bābhravī, O dark Tāmasī,
O self-restrained one, O Sovereign, be gracious; O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥23॥
11.24: O you who are the form of all, O Mistress of all, O you who are endowed with every power,
protect us from fears, O Devī; O Devī Durgā, salutation to you. ॥24॥
11.25: May this gentle face of yours, adorned with three eyes,
protect us from all beings. O Kātyāyanī, salutation to you. ॥25॥
11.26: Fearsome with flames, exceedingly fierce, the slayer of all the asuras:
may your trident protect us from fear. O Bhadrakālī, salutation to you. ॥26॥
11.27: That bell which, filling the world with its sound, destroys the might of the daityas:
may it protect us from sins, O Devī, as children are protected. ॥27॥
11.28: Smeared with the mire of the blood and fat of the asuras, gleaming in your hand,
may your sword be auspicious. O Caṇḍikā, we bow to you. ॥28॥
11.29: When pleased, you destroy all diseases,
but when angered, all the desires that are longed for.
For people who have taken refuge in you there is no calamity;
those who have taken refuge in you indeed become a refuge for others. ॥29॥
11.30: This slaughter which you have wrought today,
O Devī, of the great asuras, the haters of dharma, of what is right,
making your own form manifold through many forms:
O Ambikā, who else could accomplish that? ॥30॥
11.31: In the branches of knowledge, in the scriptures, and in the lamps of discernment,
the primeval words (the Vedas), who is there other than you?
In the pit of attachment, filled with exceedingly great darkness,
who else makes this universe whirl about so intensely? ॥31॥
11.32: Where there are rākṣasas, where there are serpents of deadly venom,
where there are enemies, where there are hosts of robbers,
where there is a forest fire, and likewise in the midst of the ocean:
there you stand and protect the universe. ॥32॥
11.33: O Queen of the universe, you protect the universe;
as the very self of the universe, you uphold the universe here.
You are to be revered by the lord of the universe;
those who bow to you in devotion become the refuge of the universe. ॥33॥
11.34: O Devī, be gracious; protect us from the fear of enemies
always, just as you have done at once, now, by slaying the asuras.
Swiftly quell the sins of every world,
and the great calamities that arise when evil portents ripen. ॥34॥
11.35: O Devī, remover of the afflictions of the universe, be gracious to those who bow to you.
O you who are worthy of praise by the dwellers of the three worlds, be the giver of boons to the worlds. ॥35॥
11.37: O hosts of gods, I am the giver of boons. Whatever boon you desire in your minds,
choose it; I shall give it, a boon for the good of the worlds. ॥37॥
11.39: O Sovereign of all, the quelling of every affliction that besets the three worlds
and the destruction of our enemies: may you accomplish them in just this way. ॥39॥
11.41: When the Vaivasvata manvantara, the age of the Manu Vaivasvata, has come, in the twenty-eighth yuga, cycle of ages,
two other great asuras, Śumbha and Niśumbha, will be born. ॥41॥
11.42: Born in the house of the cowherd Nanda, from the womb of Yaśodā,
I shall then destroy those two, dwelling on the Vindhya mountain. ॥42॥
11.43: Again, in an exceedingly terrible form, upon the earth
I shall descend and slay the dānavas of Vipracitti's line as well. ॥43॥
11.44: And as I devour those fierce great asuras of Vipracitti's line,
my teeth will become red, like pomegranate flowers. ॥44॥
11.45: Then the gods in heaven, and humans in the world of mortals,
praising me, will ever call me Raktadantikā, the red-toothed one. ॥45॥
11.46: And again, in a drought lasting a hundred years, when there is no water,
remembered by the sages, I shall appear on the earth, not born of a womb. ॥46॥
11.47: Then I shall look upon the sages with a hundred eyes,
and so people will celebrate me as Śatākṣī, the hundred-eyed. ॥47॥
11.48: Then, O gods, with vegetables grown from my own body,
which sustain life, I shall nourish the whole world until the rains come. ॥48॥
11.49: Then I shall become renowned on earth as Śākambharī, she who nourishes with vegetables,
and right there I shall slay the great asura called Durgama. ॥49॥
11.50: And so my name will become renowned as Durgā Devī.
And again, when on the Himālaya I take on a terrible form ॥50॥
11.51: and devour the rākṣasas to protect the sages,
then all the sages, their bodies bowed low, will praise me. ॥51॥
11.52: And so my name will become renowned as Bhīmā Devī, the terrible Devī.
When the asura named Aruṇa causes great affliction in the three worlds, ॥52॥
11.53: then I shall take on a bee-form made up of countless bees,
and for the good of the three worlds I shall slay that great asura. ॥53॥
11.54: And then people everywhere will praise me as Bhrāmarī, the Devī of the bees.
Thus, whenever affliction arising from the dānavas comes about, ॥54॥
11.55: then each time I shall descend and bring about the destruction of the enemies. ॥55॥
11.iti: Svasti, may it be well. Thus ends the eleventh chapter, named the Praise of Nārāyaṇī, of the Devī Māhātmya in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, the age of the Manu Sāvarṇi. ॥11॥
12.dhyana: Om. Her whose radiance equals the splendour of lightning, who is seated on the shoulder of the lion, who is fearsome,
who is attended by maidens whose hands gleam with swords and shields,
who holds in her hands the discus, mace, sword, shield, arrows, bow, bowstring and the threatening gesture of the raised forefinger,
who is fiery in nature, who bears the moon: the three-eyed Durgā I worship.
12.2: Whoever, with a collected mind, will praise me constantly with these hymns,
all his affliction I shall bring to rest, without doubt. ॥2॥
12.3: Those who will tell of the destruction of Madhu and Kaiṭabha and the slaying of Mahiṣāsura,
and likewise of the slaying of Śumbha and Niśumbha, ॥3॥
12.4: and those who, single-minded, on the eighth, the fourteenth and the ninth days of the lunar fortnight,
will listen with devotion to my excellent Māhātmya, ॥4॥
12.5: for them there will be no wrongdoing at all, nor calamities born of wrongdoing;
there will be no poverty, nor parting from those they love. ॥5॥
12.6: No fear will come to him from enemies, from robbers or from the king,
nor will it ever arise from weapons, from fire or from a flood of water. ॥6॥
12.7: Therefore this Māhātmya of mine should be recited by those of collected mind,
and always heard with devotion: it is the supreme and great means of welfare. ॥7॥
12.8: All calamities born of great epidemics,
and likewise the threefold portent, my Māhātmya can quell. ॥8॥
12.9: The shrine of mine where this is duly recited every day,
that I shall never forsake; my presence is established there. ॥9॥
12.10: At the presenting of offerings, in worship, in the fire rite and at a great festival,
this whole Māhātmya of mine should be recited and also made to be heard. ॥10॥
12.11: The offering and worship, done as it may be by one who knows or even by one who does not,
I shall receive with love, and likewise the fire oblation so offered. ॥11॥
12.12: In the autumn season the great worship is performed, the yearly one;
having heard this Māhātmya of mine at it, filled with devotion, ॥12॥
12.13: a man will be freed from all afflictions and endowed with wealth and grain
by my grace; of this there is no doubt. ॥13॥
12.14: Having heard this Māhātmya of mine, and likewise my auspicious manifestations
and my valour in battles, a man becomes fearless. ॥14॥
12.15: Enemies are destroyed, welfare comes about,
and the family of men who listen to my Māhātmya rejoices. ॥15॥
12.16: In every rite of pacification, and likewise on seeing a bad dream,
and in severe afflictions from the planets, one should listen to my Māhātmya. ॥16॥
12.17: Calamities subside, and so do the dreadful afflictions from the planets,
and a bad dream seen by men turns into a good dream. ॥17॥
12.18: It brings peace to children seized by the bālagrahas, the spirits that seize children,
and when men's union is broken, it is the best means of making friendship. ॥18॥
12.19: It is supreme in destroying the strength of all the wicked;
by its mere recitation it destroys rākṣasas, evil spirits and piśācas. ॥19॥
12.20: This whole Māhātmya of mine brings about my presence.
With animal offerings, flowers, arghya water and incense, and likewise with excellent perfumes and lamps, ॥20॥
12.21: with the feeding of brāhmaṇas, with oblations, with sprinkling water day and night,
and with various other enjoyments and gifts, the pleasure given to me over a year, ॥21॥
12.22: that same pleasure is given to me when this is recited or heard but once.
Heard, it removes sins and grants health as well. ॥22॥
12.23: The recital of my manifestations gives protection from evil spirits.
My deeds in battles, the slaying of the wicked daityas: ॥23॥
12.24: when they are heard, men feel no fear caused by enemies.
And the hymns which you gods have made, and those which the brahmarṣis have made, ॥24॥
12.25: and those made by Brahmā, may they grant an auspicious understanding.
In a forest or on a desolate road, surrounded by a forest fire, ॥25॥
12.26: or surrounded by robbers in a lonely place, or seized by enemies,
or pursued by lions and tigers, or in the forest by wild elephants, ॥26॥
12.27: or ordered by an angry king to be put to death, or held in bonds,
or tossed by the wind while on a ship on the great ocean, ॥27॥
12.28: or when weapons are falling in an exceedingly terrible battle,
or in all dreadful afflictions, or even when tormented by pain, ॥28॥
12.29: A man who remembers these deeds of mine is set free from danger.
By my power, lions and the like, robbers, and enemies as well ॥29॥
12.30: flee while still far off from one who remembers my deeds. ॥30॥
12.32: Having spoken thus, the blessed Caṇḍikā, of fierce valour, ॥32॥
12.33: vanished right there while all the gods looked on.
And those gods too, free from fear, took up their own offices as before; ॥33॥
12.34: their enemies slain, they all enjoyed their shares in the sacrifice.
As for the daityas, when Śumbha, the enemy of the gods, had been slain by the Devī in battle, ॥34॥
12.35: he, the destroyer of the world, exceedingly fierce and of matchless valour,
and Niśumbha too, of great might, had been slain — those of them who were left went to Pātāla, the underworld. ॥35॥
12.36: Thus that blessed Devī, though eternal, again and again
comes forth, O king, and protects the world. ॥36॥
12.37: By her this universe is deluded, and she alone brings the universe to birth;
when entreated she grants knowledge, and when pleased, prosperity. ॥37॥
12.38: This whole cosmos, O lord of men, is pervaded by her,
by the Great Devī, Mahākālī, whose very form is Mahāmārī, the great destroyer. ॥38॥
12.39: She herself, at the appointed time, is Mahāmārī; she herself, the unborn, becomes creation;
she herself, the eternal one, in due time sustains living beings. ॥39॥
12.40: In times of prosperity she herself is Lakṣmī in the homes of men, granting increase;
and in times of want she herself likewise becomes Alakṣmī, misfortune, for their ruin. ॥40॥
12.41: Praised, and duly worshipped with flowers, and with fragrances, incense and the like,
she gives wealth and sons, a mind set on dharma (right conduct), and an auspicious destiny. ॥41॥
12.iti: Svasti, may it be well. Thus ends the twelfth chapter, named the Words of the Bhagavatī, of the Devī Māhātmya in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, the age of the Manu Sāvarṇi. ॥12॥
13.dhyana: Om. She whose radiance is like the orb of the rising sun, who has four arms and three eyes,
who holds the noose and the goad and shows the gestures of granting boons and of fearlessness: I worship her, Śivā, the auspicious Devī.
13.2: This supreme Glory of the Devī, O king, has been told to you.
Such is the power of that Devī by whom this world is upheld. ॥2॥
13.3: In the same way, knowledge is brought about by the divine Viṣṇumāyā, Viṣṇu's power of illusion.
By her you, this merchant, and likewise other discerning men ॥3॥
13.4: are being deluded and have been deluded, and others too will fall into delusion.
Go for refuge, O great king, to her, the supreme sovereign Devī. ॥4॥
13.5: When worshipped, she alone gives men enjoyment, heaven and final liberation. ॥5॥
13.7: Having heard these words of his, Suratha, that lord of men, ॥7॥
13.8: bowed down before that greatly blessed sage of rigorous vows,
and, despondent through his excessive sense of possession and the seizure of his kingdom, ॥8॥
13.9: went at once to practise austerity, and so did that merchant, O great sage;
and, for the sake of beholding Ambā, the Mother, the king took his place on the sandy bank of a river. ॥9॥
13.10: And that merchant too performed austerity, reciting the supreme Devī Sūkta, the hymn to the Devī.
The two of them made an earthen image of the Devī on that sandbank, ॥10॥
13.11: and worshipped her with flowers, incense, fire offerings and libations,
fasting, self-controlled, their minds fixed on her, and wholly absorbed. ॥11॥
13.12: And the two also made an offering sprinkled with blood from their own bodies.
When, self-controlled, they had worshipped her thus for three years, ॥12॥
13.13: Caṇḍikā, the upholder of the world, well pleased, appeared before them and spoke. ॥13॥
13.15: Whatever is asked for by you, O king, and by you, O joy of your family,
receive all of it from me: well pleased, I give it to you. ॥15॥
13.17: Then the king chose, for another birth, an imperishable kingdom,
and here, in this very life, his own kingdom, with his enemies' forces crushed by might. ॥17॥
13.18: Then the merchant too, his mind weary of the world, chose knowledge:
being wise, he chose the knowledge that ends attachment in the form of 'mine' and 'I'. ॥18॥
13.20: In a very few days, O king, you will obtain your own kingdom. ॥20॥
13.21: When you have slain your enemies, it will stand unshaken for you there. ॥21॥
13.22: And when you have died, obtaining birth once more from the god Vivasvat, the Sun, ॥22॥
13.23: you will be on earth the Manu named Sāvarṇika. ॥23॥
13.24: And, O best of merchants, the boon that you have desired from me, ॥24॥
13.25: that I grant you: for your final perfection, knowledge will be yours. ॥25॥
13.27: Having thus given the two of them the boon each desired, the Devī, ॥27॥
13.28: praised by the two of them with devotion, vanished at once.
Thus, having received the boon from the Devī, Suratha, the foremost of kṣatriyas, the warrior order, ॥28॥
13.29: will obtain birth from Sūrya, the Sun, and become Sāvarṇi, the Manu. ॥29॥
13.end: Thus, having received the boon from the Devī, Suratha, the foremost of kṣatriyas, the warrior order,
will obtain birth from Sūrya and become Sāvarṇi, the Manu. Klīṃ Om.
13.iti: Svasti, may it be well. Thus ends the thirteenth chapter, named the Granting of Boons to Suratha and the Merchant, of the Devī Māhātmya in the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, the age of the Manu Sāvarṇi. ॥13॥
aparadha.1: Om. Having committed a hundred offences, if one then calls out the name Jagadambā, Mother of the world,
the state one attains is not attained even by Brahmā and the other gods. ॥1॥
aparadha.2: I am guilty of offences, and I have come to you for refuge, O Mother of the world.
Now I am one who deserves your compassion; do as you wish. ॥2॥
aparadha.3: Through ignorance, forgetfulness or confusion, whatever has been done too little or too much,
may all that be forgiven, O Devī; be gracious, O Supreme Sovereign. ॥3॥
aparadha.4: O Kāmeśvarī, O Mother of the world, whose form is being, consciousness and bliss,
accept this worship with love; be gracious, O Supreme Sovereign. ॥4॥
aparadha.5: The Devī is made of all forms, and the whole world is made of the Devī.
Therefore I bow to you, the Supreme Sovereign, whose form is the universe. ॥5॥
aparadha.6: Whatever syllable has dropped out, and whatever may be lacking its mātrā, the measure of a vowel,
may all that become complete by your grace, O Great Sovereign. ॥6॥
aparadha.7: O Mother of the world, whatever I have uttered here in this recitation
lacking a visarga, a bindu (the nasal dot) or a syllable,
may that become wholly complete through your grace,
and may the fulfilment of my resolve always come about. ॥7॥
aparadha.8: Whatever lacks a mātrā, a bindu, the pair of dots (the visarga), a word, a pair of words, a letter or the like;
whatever was done with devotion or without it, in due order or by force, clearly or indistinctly, O Mother;
and whatever, through delusion or ignorance, has now been read or left unread in this hymn of yours:
may all that be complete in all its parts by your grace, O Bhagavatī, giver of boons; be gracious. ॥8॥
aparadha.9: Be gracious, O Bhagavatī, O Mother; be gracious, O you who love your devotees.
Show me your grace, O Devī; O Durgā, O Devī, salutation to you. ॥9॥
aparadha.iti: Thus ends the Aparādhakṣamāpaṇa Stotra, the hymn asking pardon for offences.
devi-sukta.1: Om. I move with the Rudras and with the Vasus;
I move with the Ādityas and with the Viśvedevas, the All-gods, too.
I uphold both Mitra and Varuṇa;
I uphold Indra and Agni, and I uphold both the Aśvins. ॥1॥
devi-sukta.2: I uphold Soma, who is to be pressed;
I uphold Tvaṣṭṛ, and Pūṣan and Bhaga.
I bestow wealth on the one who offers oblations,
on the zealous sacrificer who presses the Soma. ॥2॥
devi-sukta.3: I am the sovereign queen, the gatherer of riches,
the knowing one, the first of those worthy of worship.
Such as I am, the gods have set me out in many places,
me who dwell in many places and make myself enter into many beings. ॥3॥
devi-sukta.4: Through me he eats food, he who sees,
who breathes, who hears what is spoken.
Not knowing me, they yet dwell in me.
Hear, O famed one: I tell you what is worthy of belief. ॥4॥
devi-sukta.5: I myself declare this, which is welcomed
by gods and by men alike.
Whomever I desire, him I make mighty;
him I make a Brahmā, him a seer, him one of fine wisdom. ॥5॥
devi-sukta.6: I stretch the bow for Rudra,
so that his arrow may slay the hater of sacred knowledge.
I make battle for the people;
I have entered into heaven and earth. ॥6॥
devi-sukta.7: I give birth to the father on the summit of this world;
my source is within the waters, in the ocean.
From there I spread out over all the worlds,
and I touch yonder heaven with my height. ॥7॥
devi-sukta.8: I alone blow forth like the wind,
laying hold of all the worlds.
Beyond heaven, beyond this earth too,
so vast have I become through my greatness. ॥8॥
devi-sukta.iti: Thus ends the Devī Sūkta, as the Ṛgveda gives it.
